items.quote: if what I spoke about previously that we have scaled up so much in solar, where we were about 20 crores, and we are going to be close to the number which I already spoke about, we would like to mirror that.

items.statement: Sales volume ~135,000 tons in Q1 FY27
items.quote: all put together, we have done about 135,000 tons this quarter.

items.statement: Revenue seasonality: 40-42% in H1, 58-60% in H2 historically
items.quote: As a business, as a sector, we normally have 40% to 42% of the revenue that comes in , in the first six months, and then 58% to 60% of the revenue that comes in the last six months.

items.statement: Broad product portfolio enables one-stop-shop; existing large clients encouraged PEB entry for data centers
items.quote: Our existing clients, a lot of the large ones today that are getting into this business have been encouraging us over the last six, nine months to get into it, to be able to support them in the quick turnaround for these plants of theirs.

items.statement: No major Indian competition in US for our product categories; qualified globally in 50+ countries
items.quote: As of now, we don't see any major real competition coming in our kind of products from any Indian company as of at this at this point.

items.statement: US Section 232 tariffs at 50% on steel/aluminum fully passed through via change of law provisions
items.quote: When that Russian oil tariff got removed, and India came back to 25%, and then it was lowered again, we still remained at 50%. So for us, globally, the tariff on steel and aluminum products to the US remains at 50%.

items.statement: Elevated global freight and delivery costs due to high fuel prices impacting margins; expected to normalize over time
items.quote: what's happening globally, because of fuel costs have gone up world over, and local costs of fuel, even in countries that are oil -producing, like the Middle East, like Saudi and the UAE, and US, which is a large producer of oil, the domestic cost itself of fuel cost oil has gone up. That has increased the shipment cost and the delivery costs

items.statement: Tariff revenue component: Q1 FY27 INR250 crores, Q1 FY26 INR113 crores, Q4 FY26 INR196 crores; fully passed through to customers
items.quote: the tariff was of INR250 crores and odd figure, which is a part of our Q1's revenue. But as mentioned earlier by Rajiv s ir, that everything is passed on to our customers, so it doesn't impact our profitability

items.statement: Target utilization of 60-65% over time; new boilers expected at 50% utilization initially
items.quote: Our intent is to take this utilization to 60 % to 65% of and with our experience and learning in the last decade, the newer boilers that we are commissioning, the newer boilers that we are commissioning will be expected to be in the range of 50% at the very initial months of the commissioning.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton of INR1,000 sustainable for steam generation sites; annual EBITDA per ton at par or better than Q1
items.quote: EBITDA per ton of INR1,000 can be safely assumed that it will be maintained in our steam generation and distribution sites for next few quarters, as the new facilities that are coming up are on waste and will definitely help in keeping EBITDA per ton at INR1,000 or better.

items.statement: Volume growth of 5-10% at current locations; 20-25% company-level volume growth achievable with new capacity
items.quote: Yes we can expect similar growth in at least, say, 5% to 10% for the current locations where we are already there, with the current installed capacity on smaller numbers. But as we said that we are already installing new projects, new locations, that would add to the capacity utilization basis the basis the capacity that we are installing.

items.statement: INR60 crore for four under-construction projects; INR170 crore for IPO projects and Tarapur over 15-18 months
items.quote: We'll have to do around another, INR60 -odd crores of capex to take all these four projects live. And the -- for the balance, the IPO end -use project and one of the project which is planned in Tarapur, we intend to do another INR170 crores worth capex in next 15 months to 18 months.

items.statement: Steam capacity to expand from 345 TPH to ~705 TPH; Una project adds 300 TPH
items.quote: These initiatives expected to increase our steam distribution capacity from 345 tons per hour currently to approximately 705 tons per hour capacity, providing a strong foundation for long -term growth.

items.statement: Four under-construction projects to go live in FY27; Tarapur (60 TPH) in Q4 FY28; IPO projects (Dahej, Ankleshwar, Panoli) in Q1 FY29
items.quote: four under-construction facilities should go live in current financial year, this is what we are targeting. The 60 tons per hour capacity, which is in Tarapur, should get live in Q4-FY2028. And the IPO end-use facilities, -- which are in Dahej GIDC, Ankleshwar, and Panoli, should go live in Q1-FY2029.

items.statement: ~70% of 345 TPH capacity tied up with customers; contracts 1-10 years with non-exit clauses
items.quote: Out of the 345 tons per hour capacity installed, we have -- around 70% capacity tied up for the for the customers. So, yes, that's the answer to your question.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 24.05% (+702 bps YoY); PAT margin 14.26% (+529 bps); EBITDA per ton INR1,011 (+37% YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA for Quarter 1 FY27 increased by 60.08% year -on-year to INR30.93 crores from INR19.32 crores , EBITDA margin expanded substantially to 24.05% compared with 17.03% in Quarter 1 FY26, an improvement of 702 basis points.

items.statement: Una project expected 8-10% EBITDA margin (pass-through model, no capex)
items.quote: This will be instead of EBITDA margin, this should be basically the EBITDA per ton. We should be getting around 8 % to 10% clear-cut margin. We are doing no capex there. But that will depend upon what will be the fuel price when we will be billing to the customer.

items.statement: Steam supply agreements have variable component linked to coal price; pass-through predominantly monthly
items.quote: Most of our customers are covered by steam supply agreements comprising fixed and variable components, with the variable component linked to the coal price. This contractual structure enables us to pass through changes in fuel cost.

items.statement: Switched coal purchases from credit to cash post May 2026, lowering fuel cost
items.quote: And we were purchasing coal on credit basis till May 2026, and post that we have converted entire credit purchases to cash purchases. So, that is also helping us in improving the margins , because you can understand that any cash purchases will help you in lowering the cost of fuel.

items.statement: Increasing waste-to-energy fuel mix; Vapi project operational, more under development
items.quote: We are also actively diversifying our fuel mix by increasing the use of waste-to-energy solutions wherever commercially viable. Our experience at Vapi, along with projects under development, reflects our commitment to combining operational efficiency with sustainable energy solutions.

items.statement: Nitrogen generation started at Ankleshwar (350 Nm3/hr PSA plant); evaluating ASU for oxygen, liquid nitrogen, liquid oxygen; exploring hydrogen
items.quote: We have commenced nitrogen generation and pipeline distribution at Ankleshwar , through a PSA-based plant with a capacity of 350 Nm 3 per hour, leveraging our existing industrial customer relationship and pipeline infrastructure.

items.statement: Industrial gases to leverage existing pipeline infrastructure; incremental pipeline cost 10-20% of current infra
items.quote: Second is the cost of pipeline laying will be very tough thing to answer, but what I want to still say is it would be hardly 10% to 20% at the max of the current infrastructure that we've already invested in. You can understand that 80% infrastructure will be reutilized or leveraged for a better revenue.

items.statement: 99.38% Q1 FY27 revenue from repeat customers (vs 90.7% FY26); 21 customers with multiple units
items.quote: In quarter one FY2027, the proportion increased further to approximately 99.38%. This provides a strong base of recurring business and supports visibility as we add capacity and increase utilization.

items.statement: Cost advantage 25-35% vs captive boilers using expensive fuels or intermittent consumption
items.quote: So, that could be in range of 25% to 35% cost efficiency. So, that's the predominant reason why industries stick to us.

items.statement: No direct competitors in most geographies; value prop vs captive generation is cost efficiency
items.quote: So, one, there is generally not a competitor in -- most of the geographies that we're talking about or we are operating. So, the question of competition doesn't really, arise.

items.statement: CPCB 2024 guideline mandates SMEs shift to common boilers; government pushing community boilers for pollution reduction and plug-and-play industrial parks
items.quote: In March 2024, the Central Pollution Control Board, rolled out a guideline saying that all the SMEs of India should shift to the umbrella of common boilers. So, for the government and the pollution control board authorities, it is like CETPs.

items.statement: Target 35-40 days positive working capital cycle; fortnightly billing, collections 7-15 days; CFO/EBITDA ~1.2x
items.quote: So, working capital days going forward between 35 to 40 days positive working capital cycle should be going forward.

items.statement: Gross debt INR359.48 crore (up from INR281.62 crore FY26) due to borrowings to be repaid from IPO proceeds; finance costs to moderate in FY27
items.quote: As of Q1 FY2027, gross debt stood at INR359.48 crores compared with INR281.62 crores at the end of FY2026. The increase was primarily due to additional borrowings for general corporate purposes, which were intended to repaid from IPO proceeds.

items.statement: IPO proceeds used for debt repayment and capacity expansion at Ankleshwar, Panoli, Dahej
items.quote: Part of the funds were utilized to reduce the debt.

items.statement: Steam sales 305,816 tons (+16.7% YoY, +11.5% QoQ); utilization 41.4% (vs 36.1% YoY, 38.3% QoQ); saleable capacity 4.46M tons at 705 TPH (80% load, 330 days)
items.quote: Quarter 1 FY27 was a strong quarter for Steamhouse India Limited, with steam volumes reaching a record quarterly level of approximately 3,05,816 tons, representing a growth of 16.70% year -on-year and 11.52% sequentially.

items.statement: Revenue from steam +46% YoY to INR123.37 crore; own generation 73.7%, traded steam 22.2% in Q1
items.quote: Importantly, the quality of revenue has improved significantly. The revenue from steam increased by 46.07% year -on-year to INR123.37 crores from INR84.46 crores in Quarter 1 FY26.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA seasonally lower due to monsoon (wet fuel, flooding); structural changes (cash coal, solar, inventory optimization) to mitigate
items.quote: Q2 of every financial year is an exception, considering EBITDA gets impacted on account of monsoon. However, we have done certain structural changes like moving coal purchases from credit to cash, installation of solar power to reduce cost. We are also tryin g to optimize the inventory quantity and value.

items.statement: Related party steam purchase from Sanjoo Dyeing at Sachin to continue for few quarters; may stop if new Sachin projects executed
items.quote: So, that the related party transaction still continues at least for next few quarters. We have some future plans wherein we would like to evaluate further opportunities in Sachin GIDC or nearby to do other projects. In that case, maybe this the steam purchase from Sanjoo Dyeing can stop.

name: Canara HSBC Life Insurance Company Limited

items.statement: Guided 30-35% revenue and PBT CAGR through FY28 with EBITDA margin 17-20%
items.quote: Looking ahead, management has guided towards 30% to 35% CAGR in revenue and profit before tax through FY28, while maintaining an EBITDA margin range of 17% to 20%.

items.statement: Kidcity FY27 revenue target INR80-100 crore, FY28 target INR180-200 crore
items.quote: For the current year, we are targeting, assuming in between from INR80 crores to INR100 crores, which we are targeting, and hopefully, we want to achieve that target. And next year, we are targeting for approx INR180 crores to INR200 crores.

items.statement: Kidcity internal target INR500 crore revenue by FY29-30 with 1,000 SIS and 300-400 EBOs
items.quote: For Kid city, we are targeting, aiming to reach by FY '29-'30, we internally have a revenue projection target of INR500 crores that we are carrying, that we have to do around 1,000 SIS shop-in-shop counters for SIS. By FY '29-'30, we have to do approximately 300 to 400 outlets for EBOs or these kiosk model for airport or high-street shopping malls.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 18.8% vs 20.7% YoY due to higher yarn, dyeing chemical and processing costs
items.quote: Our EBITDA has increased 38.1% to INR20 crores, while EBITDA margin moderated to 18.8% from 20.7%, primarily due to higher yarn prices, dyeing-related chemical costs, and processing charges.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 18.2% vs 18.9% YoY
items.quote: H1 FY27 revenue increased 74.7% to INR180 crore s, while EBITDA grew 68.1% to INR33 crore s. EBITDA margin stood at 18.2% vis-a-vis 18.9% in H1 FY26

items.statement: Full year FY27 EBITDA margin guided 17-20%
items.quote: Right. EBITDA margins would be in between 17% to 20%.

items.statement: Kidcity PAT margin 10-13%
items.quote: PAT margins would be in between 10% to 13%.

items.statement: Healthy orders from Style Baazar, FirstCry, Srijan and Hopscotch in H1 FY27
items.quote: During H1 FY27, we saw healthy orders from customers and retail chains, including Style Baazar, FirstCry, Srijan and Hopscotch.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue split: Karnika INR140 crore (B2B), Kidcity INR40 crore (B2C)
items.quote: INR140 crores is from the Karnika, INR40 crores is from Kidcity. Consolidation is around INR180 crores for H1.

items.statement: Kidcity shop-in-shop capex INR2-3 lakh per store, new EBO model INR10-15 lakh per store
items.quote: Numbers, if we say, per store for shop-in-shop, we are getting with around INR2 lakhs to INR3 lakhs per store for shop-in-shop model for capex. And one of the new model which we are trying to bring upon by the end of this quarter or by the end of this year, we are planning to do so. For that, we definitely need some capex approx INR10 lakhs to INR15 lakhs per EBO.

items.statement: Karnika minimal capex expected as SEDEX-compliant unit already in place
items.quote: Capex in the -- from the point of view Karnika will be not much because, currently, we have already -- last year we have introduced our SEDEX-compliant unit, we have already taken up.

items.statement: 85+ shop-in-shop counters operational in H1 FY27
items.quote: During H1 FY27, we had 85-plus shop-in-shop counters across our network.

items.statement: Cotton prices normalized, cost increases passed on in Q2 after Q1 absorption
items.quote: Margins will remain almost same what we are achieving in this H1 because prices of the cotton is now, I think, normalized. Whatever increase has been done on the cotton prices, they will remain stable for the next half or so forth.

items.statement: Shop-in-shop MRP INR199-499, Brands of Brand MRP INR799-1,499
items.quote: In shop-in-shop concept, we are doing for INR199 to INR499 MRP, and brands of brand, our MRP tag would be in between INR799 to INR1,499.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 143 in H1 FY27 from 178 in FY26; debt-to-equity 0.6x
items.quote: Working capital days improved to 143 days in H1 FY27 from 178 days in FY26, while our debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.6x.

items.statement: Plan to maintain current debt level; fund expansion via preferential allotment or equity if needed
items.quote: Sir, we do not want to grow the debt too much. We want to continue with this debt level. If we required next round of fund for the expansion, we will go for preferential allotment or equity, whatever our professional will suggest to us, we will go for that.

items.statement: Eligible for main board migration effective 13 October 2026 subject to regulatory requirements
items.quote: We are delighted to share a proud milestone in our journey with the company eligible for migration to the main board effective 13th October 2026, subject to completion of the applicable regulatory and procedural requirements.

items.statement: Airport kiosks high rental cost (4-6x mall) may only achieve break-even; used for visibility to drive mall/online sales
items.quote: second, footfall, again, what we are currently presuming is that at the mall, you already have footfall coming in, because at the mall your primary concentration is to buy the goo ds. The customers, the consumers coming there, somewhere or the other, they are mentally prepared that you will find goods there and you have to purchase from there. At the airport, your visibility is much better because

items.statement: Kidcity per EBO revenue target INR50 lakh/year with 13-14% margin
items.quote: Per store, per EBOs, we are targeting for INR50 lakhs per year. If we are achieving that, we will be margin of around 13% to 14%.

items.statement: Full-year disbursement guidance maintained at INR 13,000 crores for FY27
items.quote: For the full year, we continue to have the same guidance of INR 13,000 crore s in terms of disbursement

items.statement: AUM growth guidance maintained at 13%-14%, closer to 14% for FY27
items.quote: With the full year guidance continuing at INR13,000 crores, we hold the same guidance for AUM of 13%- 14%, closer to 14% in terms of our AUM growth for the year.

items.statement: Spread and NIM guidance maintained at 2.75% and 3.75%+ respectively
items.quote: Our guidance of 2.75 and 3.75 for spread and NIM, whereas we have been operating around 2.8 and 3.8. We should continue to protect our spread and NIM.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 10 basis points for FY27
items.quote: Overall, our credit costs, we have guided for 10 basis points and for the quarter, end of the quarter, it is about 9 basis points. And I think we can continue with the guidance of 10 basis points.

items.statement: Internal target of INR 16,000 crores disbursement for FY28 implying 15%+ AUM growth
items.quote: Next year at least we are internally looking at around INR 16,000 crores disbursement for FY28. So that should translate to around 15% plus AUM growth for next year.

items.statement: Project Tejas IT transformation fully live across all branches as of 1st October
items.quote: Presently, we are completely online in the new system. All the aspects of the project, including the security aspect, the infrastructure aspects which were already implemented earlier, and now all the operational or functionalities which are there in the project have all been implemented, and we have gone live with the entire LOS, LMS across all the branches.

items.statement: 25 of 28 planned branches for FY27 already operational with staffing in place
items.quote: We have 28 branches, which are planned for the full year, as against that 25 branches have already been started, and they are operational with staffing also in place.

items.statement: Sales team to expand from ~90 to 150 people by December, targeting 250 next year
items.quote: We are targeting 90 people are there, we are targeting to increase it to about 150 people. And we are looking at about INR 1,500 crores this year coming from INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores coming from the sales team.

items.statement: Demand remains robust across geographies; Karnataka stabilized at INR 230-250 crores monthly disbursement
items.quote: We are still seeing a robust demand across all the geographies. Karnataka also, which has been in the past always a point of observation, has stabilized around INR230 to INR250 crores of disbursement consistently.

items.statement: Half percentage point rate hike not expected to materially impact home loan demand
items.quote: 1/2% increase from here is not going to make much of impact in the terms of the demand, because once it is converted into a 15-year EMI, the impact on the EMI is very, very limited.

items.statement: 10 bps rate hike passed on to housing customers effective 12th October; further hikes may be 15 bps to match liability cost increase of 12-13 bps
items.quote: We have already increased 10 basis points. As you know, last year also, when the rates were coming down, we did it in four parts of 10 basis points, 15 basis points, 15 basis points and 10 basis points. Same way the next hike, maybe we may look at a 15 so that we can average out to about 12 to 13 basis points.

items.statement: Q2 disbursements at INR 2,375 crores net of INR 29 crores cancellations due to NHB guidelines and IT impact
items.quote: As a result, the disbursements for the quarter were at only INR2,375 crores. This, of course, is net of the INR29 crores which we have reduced from the disbursements because of the NHB guidelines which have come saying that regarding the cancellation of DDs.

items.statement: Q3 disbursement target of INR 3,500 crores to cover Q2 shortfall
items.quote: We are targeting for about INR3,500 crores in this quarter, and the balance in the next quarter.

items.statement: Sanctioned but undisbursed pipeline increased by ~INR 118 crores QoQ providing buffer for Q3
items.quote: about INR118 crores is the extra amount that we are carrying in terms of the sanctioned but not disbursed, as compared to the previous quarter

items.statement: NCD issuance not compelled as 25% market borrowing requirement already met for FY27
items.quote: We are already complied with complying with the regulatory guidelines on the 25% borrowing through the market for this financial year. We are not having any compulsion to go to the market and raise at 8.3.

items.statement: Delinquency stable; SMA-0 uptick due to daily vs monthly computation methodology change
items.quote: Our overall delinquency has not been impacted much, only there's a little bit of an increase in the SMA -0, which also is mainly because of the methodology of computation or flagging of this cases.

items.statement: Gross NPA addition of INR 35 crores in H1 FY27 vs INR 40 crores in H1 FY26; expect reduction in H2
items.quote: Last year, our increase in NPA in the first half was about INR40 crores. As against this, in the current year, the six months, it has been INR35 crores. Again, the pushback will come in the second half.

items.statement: NHB guideline implemented: disbursements netted off for DD cancellations during quarter and post-quarter pre-announcement
items.quote: There was NHB regulation or a guideline regarding this the reporting of disbursements as netting off the cancellations during the quarter, and the cancellations of the DD which have been from the date of the end of the quarter to the date of reporting. So that we have already implemented in this quarter, and we have netted off 29 crores from our disbursements.

items.statement: Wage bill regulations (minimum salary INR 25k, basic+DA >50%) have no impact as entry salary starts at INR 36k
items.quote: We are having a salary more than 25,000. So even the joining entry-level salary starts from about 36,000. So basically, that is not impacting. And second thing is again, earlier last quarter also we had indicated, our basic plus DA is more than 50% of the total package.

items.statement: Insurance commission reduction proposal would have minimal impact as insurance income <1% of PBT
items.quote: The entire year last year, our commission from insurance business was only to the tune of about 12 and odd crores, which is less than 1% of our PBT of INR1,304 crores of last year. So basically, even if it is implemented in the way it is has been shared or publicized in the media, it would not have any meaningful impact.

items.statement: El Nino/drought risk in South may slow construction activity but limited Tier 3/4/5 exposure mitigates impact
items.quote: if there is a water shortage, of course, it can impact in terms of the construction activity, but we'll have to see how much because sometimes there have been delayed rain s. And at least Maharashtra, Karnataka and some of the states, yes, there has been definitely a lot of drought - prone this thing, drought has been announced in quite a few villages and stuff like that. Of course, in our case, w

items.statement: Industry-wide slowdown from drought could risk FY27 disbursement target; may pivot to LAP/top-ups as short-term strategy
items.quote: See, if the overall industry is going to slow down, I think we are part of the industry. We cannot be very different, and I don't think we will then that be this thing. But as of now, as I said, it's a little early to start projecting that. But as of now, I mean, there are a lot of constructions, there are other ways also. Like we may maybe look at a little more of LAP or we may look at some const

items.statement: Prepayment rate improved to INR 1,795 crores in Q2 vs INR 1,857 crores in Q1; expect further reduction as rate gap narrows
items.quote: Plus, now with the rate hike, which has been there, the gap between the what the m arket is offering and what we are offering will come down because whereas there was a 25 basis points increase in the repo rate, whereas we have only increased 10 basis points for our housing customers, old as well as new customers. Basically, the gap will now start reducing, which will also help us in retaining goo

items.statement: LCR maintained well above 100% requirement; HQLA steady at ~INR 2,300 crores; short-term borrowings reduced from 26-27% to ~12%
items.quote: Normally, we have a standard amount of approximately INR2,300 crores or something that we are maintaining as our HQLA. So, therefore what happens, if this figure keeps changing, this ratio also slightly keeps changing. But what we are maintaining HQLA will always be above 100%.

items.statement: New branch productivity reaches maturity in 18-24 months targeting 5 cases per staff per month
items.quote: In terms of the productivity, so there are, I mean, productivity, of course, I think it will take about 18 normally, we say 18 to 24 months. Some do it much earlier, but on an average, this is what it works out to, to reach that kind of a level of productivity of whatever we generally maintain our productivity of five cases per staff per month.

items.statement: Digital sourcing channel enabled by new tech stack; targeting 10% of business by Q4 FY28
items.quote: If you see one of our sourcing, we have a 10% business we are expecting to come from the digital source. So that will be an enhancement to our business.

items.statement: CEO expects to sustain NIM at 2.55% given 53% repo-linked book repriced and retail margin at 8.65%
items.quote: I guess we will be able to sustain this NIM at 2.55% considering, I mean, there is a rate hike also of 0.25 basis point. We are at 25 basis points. And our Repo rate linked book is 53%.

items.statement: FCNR(B) leverage of $3.2bn has only 40-50bps spread which will offset NIM benefit from repricing
items.quote: This quarter, the effect of that FCNR(B) leverage will also come, wherein we do not have a spread of 2.55%. The spread in this, $3.2 billion, in leverage is only 40 basis or 50 basis points.

items.statement: Corporate loan yield improved to 7.72% from 7.68% QoQ; Gold loan yield improved to 9.10% from 8.96% QoQ
items.quote: The corporate the yield is 7.72% and on gold it is increased to 9.10%. It has improved from 8.96% to 9.10%.

items.statement: Gold loan yield expected to rise further as rates harden; currently 9.10% but below peer banks
items.quote: Yeah, certainly. When it comes to Gold loan, we are earning as of now 9.10%, but it is going to give further because rates are now hardening.

items.statement: Robust retail demand: housing loans growing 17-18%, total retail 21%, vehicle loans 25% even before festive season
items.quote: We are seeing very robust demand for retail lending products. Our Housing loan in excess of 17%, 18% is growing. Total retail, 21%, vehicle loan, 25%.

items.statement: Corporate pipeline of sanctioned-but-undisbursed plus hot leads at ~₹50,000 crore, driven by power, green energy, battery storage, data centers, infra
items.quote: Altogether, already sanctioned not disbursed, and we have got good hot leads in hand. That is around ₹47,000 crore. Let's say, around, in and out, ₹50,000 crore.

items.statement: Gold loan book at ₹2.82 lakh crore: ₹1.74 lakh crore agri, ₹1.08 lakh crore non-agri
items.quote: ₹2.82 lakh crore is the total Gold loan. Out of which, Agriculture is ₹1.74 lakh crores and ₹1.08 lakhs crores is the Non-agriculture.

items.statement: Core agriculture (ex-gold) grew ~9% YoY to ₹1.30 lakh crore; agri gold grew to ₹1.74 lakh crore from ₹1.51 lakh crore QoQ
items.quote: To be very specific, out of the Total Agri of ₹304,000 crore, Gold is ₹1,74,000 crore and core Agri is ₹1,29,000 crore...₹1,30,000 crores.

items.statement: Total slippages ₹1,844 crore: agri ₹687 cr, corporate ₹13 cr, gold ₹40 cr, MSME ₹777 cr, retail ₹327 cr
items.quote: Total slippage is ₹1,844 crore. Segment-wise, I will tell you. I will just tell you. Yes. ₹687 crore we slipped in agriculture, ₹13 crore in corporate, gold by ₹40 crore, ₹777 crore in MSME, Retail ₹327 crore.

items.statement: SMA 0+1+2 at 2.42% of book (₹33,340 cr); for >₹5 cr exposure SMA 0+1+2 at 0.51% (₹7,043 cr)
items.quote: If we take all, even ₹1, then SMA 2 is 0.9%, SMA 1 is 0.53%, total SMA 1 and 2 is 1.43%, and SMA 0 is 0.99%. Taken together all, it is 2.42% only.

items.statement: Written-off pool dwindling to ~₹18,000 cr (1.33% of gross advances); recoveries exceed slippages each quarter
items.quote: But, yes, at the same time, let me accept that very pool of that written off accounts is dwindling down. All those Gross advances also, you have seen, it is only 1.33%.

items.statement: Bulk deposits held flat at ₹4.38 lakh cr; FCNR(B) replaced ₹30-35k cr of bulk/CD at 100bps lower cost, saving CRR/SLR too
items.quote: During this process, we have decreased the cost of deposit by 1% because the FCNR deposits were at 1% less than the bulk's prevailing market price.

items.statement: FCNR(B) deposits $5.8bn raised, $3.2bn deployed; used to fund credit growth and replace bulk deposits
items.quote: $3.2 billion. Out of $5.8 billion, $3.2 billion.

items.quote: Similarly, the Dussehra calendar too has shown a strong upsurge with a mid -teens like-for-like growth.

items.quote: We expect the losses to reduce further in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Opened 1 MAC shop-in-shop in Q2
items.quote: During the quarter, we opened seven stores, four departmental stores, two Beauty boutiques and one MAC shop -in-shop.

items.statement: Customer entry grew 1% for LFL stores and 7.7% overall
items.quote: Our customer entry grew by 1% for like -for-like stores and overall growth of 7.7%.

items.statement: Power categories outperforming: Watches 24%, Handbags 16%, Fragrances 13%, Footwear 9%, Sunglasses 8%

items.statement: Private brands inventory reduced 26% with significant profitability uptake
items.quote: Despite reducing the number of brands and reducing the inventory by 26%, I'm very happy to share that we have seen a significant uptake in the profitability of the private brands concept.

items.statement: Beauty business revenue Rs 367 crores, up 18% YoY led by Fragrances 35% growth
items.quote: The overall Beauty business, including Global SS Beauty delivered a revenue of Rs 367 crores Shoppers Stop Limited October 16, 2026 Public during the quarter, registering a healthy year -on-year growth of 18%, led by Fragrances, which grew by 35

items.statement: E-commerce grew 52% YoY with ATV up 9%

items.statement: Total inventory optimized by Rs 78 crores YoY

items.quote: All these areas, areas of profitable growth, they will need some kind of capital investments, and we'll have internal accruals as well as the balance sheet robustness to fund for that growth.

items.statement: Festive mid-teens growth driven by 7% ASP increase and 8% volume growth

items.statement: INTUNE differentiated by family-led positioning with kids wear, strong CRM and customer engagement

items.quote: The GDP growth in Q2 FY27 has been better than anticipated and high performance indicators such as industrial production, strong e-way bill, cargo activity, credit growth reflects sustained momentum.

items.quote: The pace of retail disbursements is accelerating and has cro ssed Rs 90,000 crores during Q2 FY27 as against Rs 76,000 crores in Q1 of this year

items.quote: See, our PSL achievement is at aggregate level, about 50% or so. So aggregate level, we are quite okay. The place where we always scramble around to make it is the last 2 miles on the small and marginal and weaker section

items.quote: As a part of the restructuring, going forward, both LKA and Rhion are being led by Shweta Sagar, the Chief Business Officer of Butterfly. Moreover, R hion and LKA will leverage the broader Butterfly ecosystem. We expect this to materially reduce the overall cost structure and drive profitability in this segment

items.statement: No significant new manpower for new businesses; leveraging existing sales team and infrastructure
items.quote: idea is not to create multiple dedicated sales or manpower for this but leverage the existing team. There will be marginal increase in category specialists and other teams being created for this, but not significant

items.statement: Fan volume growth robust in general trade and rural; target 1.5-1.7x category growth driven by BLDC, regulation-driven consolidation in entry fans
items.quote: As we move forward, in the investor day, we clearly called out that Fan as a category, we want to be at 1.5x-1.7x the category growth, which means that underlying volume growth also going to come in. We see that being driven by BLDC

items.statement: Commodity cost pressures and unpredictable geopolitical developments remain macro headwinds
items.quote: The industry is currently facing commodity cost pressures and unpredictable geopolitical developments. We have and are continuing to a ddress these through disciplined combination of strategic price increases, consistent execution of Unnati cost savings

items.statement: Solar pumps slowdown as Kusum 1.1 nears completion; expect ramp-up with Kusum 2.0 announcement
items.quote: Solar pumps witnessed a slowdown as order inflow from Kusum 1.1, which is nearing completion, tapered. We are aware that this will pick up in the next quarter with GOI having announced Kusum 2.0. We expect the business to ramp up accordingly in the coming quarters

items.statement: AUM crossed INR1.5 lakh crore with 25% YoY growth; quarterly AUM addition INR8,580 crore vs INR6,329 crore YoY
items.quote: Total AUM stood at INR1.58 lakh crores as of 30th September, and a quarterly AUM addition was close to INR8,580 crores this quarter against INR6,329 crores in Q2 of last year.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 25% YoY to INR19,900 crore in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Disbursement momentum was good during the last quarter with 25% growth, moving from INR15,900 crores to INR19,900 crores in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Home loans AUM grew 22% YoY to 53.9% mix; LRD grew 39%, LAP 26%, DF 13% YoY
items.quote: Home loans AUM improved to 22% growth in Q2 against 20% in last quarter, while LRD growth was also strong at 39% against 41% growth in Q1. LAP grew 26%, and DF grew 13% on Y-o-Y basis. AUM mix remained well -diversified with a higher home loan composition at 53.9%.

items.statement: GNPA flat at 29 bps, NNPA at 12 bps; credit cost 10 bps vs 16 bps YoY; Stage 3 coverage 59.8%
items.quote: Asset quality was stable during the quarter with GNPA flat on sequential basis at 29 bps and NNPA at 12 bps. Credit cost overall moderated by 6 bps on Y-o-Y basis to 10 bps in Q2 FY27 against 16 bps in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: PAT grew 18% YoY to INR980 crore; ROA 2.2%, ROE 12.7%; opex/NTI improved to 19.1%
items.quote: PAT growth was 18% Y-o-Y to INR980 crores in Q2, while ROA was 2.2%, and ROE improved to 12.7%. Operating efficiency continues to improve with opex to NTI ratio at 19.1% as against 19 .7%, which was in Q2 last year.

items.statement: Sambhav monthly disbursement run rate crossed INR500 crore; constitutes 16% of home loan originations; target INR600 crore run rate by year-end
items.quote: Business crossed a critical milestone of INR500 crore s monthly disbursement run rate in the last quarter with quarterly improvement in disbursement growth, and now Sambhav constitutes 16% of overall home loan originations in Q2.

items.statement: Sambhav target 20% of home loan mix by year-end, 30% in 3-4 years; AUM growth guidance 21-23% unchanged; ROA range 2.1-2.3%
items.quote: We have said in the medium next year we will take it to around 20% of the home loan mix. In a longer term, longer term means I am saying 3 years, or 3.5 years, 4 year s, we'll take it to 30% of our home loan mix.

items.statement: Repo hike transmission ~80-82% to COF; portfolio re-pricing matched; 15 bps PLR hike effective Oct 16; new acquisition pricing up 15-20 bps
items.quote: So, largely we are an optimized balance sheet with interest rate having asset to liability floating almost completely matched. So, the flow -through of a repo hike to the cost of funds should be to the extent of close to 80%-82% of the hikes which will happen, and the similar flow-through will happen in the portfolio as far as it is concerned.

items.statement: If acquisition pricing doesn't rise with COF, margin compression 2-3 bps; higher attrition risk; will accelerate non-prime to offset
items.quote: At a company level, there is a margin available, which is what I called out in answer to the first question, saying DF, we have gone down in last two quarters, while our sanctions are very healthy, momentum is healthy. So, there is an uptick which will -- at a company level in the margin offset which will come because the highest -margin business today has been least growing in the current first h

items.statement: Borrowing mix: NCDs 50.8% (+430 bps QoQ), bank lines 35%, NHB 9%, CP reduced; money market 56%
items.quote: The borrowing mix continues to be diversified, but with higher composition of NCDs at 50.8%, which has improved 430 bps sequentially, which has offset the moderation of 280 bps in bank borrowing s, 90 bps in commercial paper, and 60 bps in NHB as a overall refinancing mix for the company.

items.statement: PBC at 60.49% (housing assets) and 50.6% (individual home loans) vs 60%/50% regulatory minima; denominator is tangible assets per regulatory definition
items.quote: Capital adequacy was 21.24%, and principal business criteria stood at 60.49% as of 30th September '26 against the 60% regulatory criteria.

items.statement: Salary costs up 19% YoY due to Sambhav and non-top-6 market expansion; elevated for next 1.5-2 years
items.quote: No, this is a salary cost because this last year, when you look at a Y -o-Y, last 1 -1.5 year, we have been investing very heavily in Sambhav and our non-top-six market structure what we had called out last year.

items.statement: Assignment income INR40 crore vs INR68 crore QoQ on lower assignment volume (INR1,428 crore vs INR2,600 crore); off-book 11-13% corridor
items.quote: So, it's basically quantum of assignment which we do in a particular quarter. Generally, so this quarter like the income is around INR40 crores. Last quarter was INR68 crores. That's predominantly driven by lower assignment which we did in this quarter. It was around INR1,400 odd crores of INR1,428 crores of assignment which we did in this quarter versus INR2,600 odd crores of assignment we did la

items.statement: Insurance commission draft guidelines may hit 10-11% of PBT; only 4-5% offset feasible in short term; opex/NTI may flatten next year
items.quote: What we are seeing that what we will if we have to call out specifically, there's a 10% -11% of the PBT which is generated from the cross -sell income, which is the income in conversation. I think 4%-5% of that can be offset by various methods, whether higher efficiencies or there. Balance 6%-7% impact on the PBT is likely to be there, which will also have an impact on opex to NTI in the next year

items.statement: Sambhav ATS INR28 lakh; bureau score >750 at 65%; salaried mix 66%; centralized underwriting model
items.quote: ATS remains stable at INR28 lakhs and customer having bureau score greater than 750 increased to 65%. Salaried customers continue to have a higher mix of 66% even in this business.

items.statement: Housing demand driven by real estate price expectations, not interest rates; BT-out rises in any rate instability; part-prepayment priority unchanged
items.quote: So, I believe housing demand is a core demand or a core need. It is driven less of interest rate, because every customer understands it's a variable rate. Today, you do not get into -- you do not buy a house because interest rate is low, because during the currency of the loan, the price can the rate can go up or it can go down.

items.statement: Operational network 223 branches across 182 locations
items.quote: Asset quality remains stable with GNPA of 29 bps and NNPA of 12 bps, same in line with last quarter, and operational network today 223 branches across 182 locations.

items.statement: H1 FY27: NTI up 16% to INR2,429 crore; opex up 10%; PBT/PAT up 20%; opex/NTI 19.3%; credit cost 8 bps; ROA 2.2%, ROE 12.6%
items.quote: Coming to half -yearly performance, NTI grew 16% to INR2,429 crore s in H1, while opex growth was 10% on Y -o-Y basis to INR470 crore s. Both PBT and PAT growth was 20% to INR1,908 crores and INR1,472 crores, respectively, for first half of the year and opex to NTI improved from 20.4% in H1 FY26 to 19.3% in H1 FY27, and credit cost was 8 bps in H1 FY27.

items.statement: Incremental NCD cost 7.04% pre-policy (10-yr post-hedge); NCD cheaper than bank lines; no fresh borrowing post Oct 6 policy
items.quote: Which is a incremental rate in NCD, which we last did it on I think before the policy, 1 day before the policy, a 10-year money post hedging was costing at around 7.04% for us.

items.statement: Product GNPA: HL 36 bps (+2 bps), LAP 61 bps (-1 bps), LRD 2 bps (one account), DF 12 bps flat; NNPA HL 16 bps (+1), LAP 21 bps (-4), LRD 1 bps, DF -3 bps
items.quote: Product -level GNPA, home loans stood at 36 bps in Q2 against 34 bps in Q1, marginally up. LAP GNPA moderated by 1 bps sequentially to 61 bps. LRD GNPA of 2 bps due to movement of one retail LRD account to NP A during the quarter, which was in Stage 2 last quarter, which moved to Stage 3, excluding which portfolio quality continue to remain strong. Developer finance GNPA was flat at 12 bps.

items.statement: Developer finance book declined 13% YoY on higher repayments and slower disbursements; sanctions up significantly in H1; target 15-17% of portfolio
items.quote: It was much higher repayments during the quarter coupled with slower disbursements, both. But larger part was higher repayment because a project-led cash flows, the cash flow momentum was significantly higher. That is what resulted to the book to there. Our strategy remains to grow the book. It is not a strategic call or a conscious call from the company to reduce the growth in this portfolio.

items.statement: COF exit March ~7.6% assuming three 25 bps hikes (61-62 bps transmission); new borrowing marginal impact 2-3 bps
items.quote: So, 75 bps will result into 61 -62 kind of. It doesn't factor in the new marginal cost of borrowing, so 2-3 bps plus/minuses can be there because of the new borrowing which will come. We are talking the portfolio through the portfolio impact, but the additional new borrowing, it will depend on the market scenario, how's the market scenario, how's the new borrowings available.

items.statement: NIM compression guidance ~25 bps for FY27; 17 bps already occurred; further 1-2 bps if acquisition pricing passes only 60-70%
items.quote: In terms of a margin, what we called out around 25 bps kind of a NIM compression, as of today, our calculation would be that we should be in that broadly the range. Even if we stress test it to a certain extent of acquisition pricing not growing in line with cost to the extent of only it grows 60%-70%, then 1-2 bps further can be the NTI pressure.

items.statement: Assignment strategy for PBC, ALM, income; off-book maintained at 11-13% of AUM; income varies by asset type assigned
items.quote: The asset strategy, the liability strategy remains same that as Gaurav has called out, 11% to 13% of the book will get assigned out, and the assignment is a strategy we follow for maintaining PBC, followed by ALM, followed by income booking.

items.statement: Liability mix 88% floating (EBLR); asset mix 88% floating (25-30% repo-linked, 60-62% PLR-linked); NHB refinance on PLR
items.quote: It is like I think I called out in the earlier question, 88% is both asset and the liability side.

items.statement: Fee income up on higher insurance commission (Sambhav attachment) and foreclosure income; fee expenses marginal and range-bound
items.quote: So, fee income predominantly is higher because of higher insurance income, and also this quarter we had some higher foreclosure income. These are the two reasons why fee income is higher, so fee and commission line is higher.

items.statement: Expects H2 FY27 revenue growth to be better than H1 both sequentially and year-on-year
items.quote: I'm confirming to you that H2 will be better year-on-year and quarter-to-quarter than H1, sequentially as well as year-on-year, right?

items.statement: Long-term aspiration of 13-15% revenue CAGR with EBIT margins in 16-17% range over next 3-5 years
items.value: 13% to 15% revenue CAGR with EBIT margins in the 16% to 17% range
items.quote: This progress supports our long-term aspiration of 13% to 15% revenue CAGR with EBIT margins in the 16% to 17% range over the next 3 years to 5 years.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBIT margin at 16.3%, up 60 bps QoQ, achieving mid-16% aspiration ahead of schedule
items.quote: EBIT margins improved 60 bps quarter-on-quarter to 16.3%, delivering ahead of timeline on our aspiration for mid-16% EBIT levels.

items.statement: Near-term margins expected to sustain at mid-16% levels with wage hike impact of 50-80 bps in Q3
items.quote: Near term, you should take it to be at these levels, around mid-16% EBIT levels.

items.statement: Q2 large deal TCV at $203 million with over 50% AI-led; order backlog and pipeline up year-on-year
items.quote: Large deal TCV was at $203 million across segments with over 50% of them being AI-led wins. Both order backlog and pipeline are up year-on-year.

items.statement: Clients doubling down on growth; tech spend shifting to AI Infrastructure, Silicon, Cloud, Data Centers and Time to Market
items.quote: Across our client interactions this quarter, the common theme is that clients are doubling down on growth. This makes us cautiously optimistic about their investment plans.

items.statement: Engineering Intelligence annualized revenue at $120 million; AI patent filings crossed 253 this quarter, total 1808
items.quote: EI has an annualized led revenue of $120 million for us in this quarter.

items.statement: Sustainability segment grew 13.4% YoY and 4.9% QoQ, now contributes 30% of revenues
items.quote: Sustainability continues to be a strong growth engine, up 13.4% year-on-year and 4.9% quarter-on-quarter as we execute multiple large deals won over the past 6 quarters.

items.statement: Mobility revenue up 2.3% QoQ; Auto Europe muted but expected to bounce back next year
items.quote: Mobility has delivered a phase of steady growth with revenues up 2.3% sequentially.

items.statement: Tech segment stable; Data Center Engineering business line created; AI-led telecom deal ramping up
items.quote: Tech was stable this quarter. The demand was driven by client investments in Agentic AI, AI Infrastructure, Cloud Native Modernization, Data Center Software, Advanced Connectivity and Semiconductors.

items.statement: Launched new EI lab in partnership with NVIDIA for physical AI native applications
items.quote: EI for Manufacturing and Operations, we launched a new EI lab in partnership with NVIDIA to build and deliver next-gen physical AI native applications across manufacturing, robotics and supply chain.

items.statement: Overall DSO at 78 days (billed 60, unbilled 18), well below guided 80-85 day range
items.quote: Quarter two FY27, overall DSO came in at 78 days. This is split as billed DSO of 60 days and unbilled DSO of 18 days, which remains stable versus 77 days in quarter one FY27, well below our guided range of 80 days to 85 days.

items.statement: YTD free cash flow at ₹790 crores, 108% of net income
items.quote: Our year-to-date free cash flow was ₹790 crores, a healthy 108% of net income.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of ₹20 per share
items.quote: The Board has approved an interim dividend of ₹20 per share, reflecting our focus on creating value for our stakeholders.

items.statement: Headcount increased to 24,035; attrition range-bound at 14.7%; wage hikes confirmed for Q3 with 50-80 bps margin impact
items.quote: Headcount marginally increased from ₹23,845 in Q1 to ₹24,035 in Q2. Attrition remained largely range bound at 14.7% during the quarter.

items.statement: AI-led deals command premium pricing; fixed price mix improved to 35.6%
items.quote: Fixed price mix improved to 35.6% in Q2, progressing towards higher value fixed price and outcome-based engagements.

items.statement: Client profile stable sequentially; added 4 new logos in Trucks & Off-highway; strategic renewal with automotive tech provider
items.quote: Client profile remains stable on a sequential basis, reflecting the strength of our customer relationships.

items.statement: Believes 9-12 months ahead of competition in Engineering Intelligence; gaining market share
items.quote: I believe that we are about 9 to 12 months ahead of competition and peer group in this area. So, we're actually gaining market share as opposed to competition.

items.statement: European auto recovery expected in 6-12 months; Middle East conflict minimal business impact currently
items.quote: I do believe that should clear up in the next 6, 9, 12 months, if you look at it.

items.statement: Completed divestment of SWC business on schedule; one-time gain of ₹165 crores in Q2
items.quote: We successfully concluded this investment of SWC business in this quarter. This resulted in a onetime gain of ₹165 crores in quarter two FY27.

items.statement: Offshore mix improved to 55.9%; realized rupee at 95.9% to dollar with 1.09% depreciation QoQ
items.quote: For quarter two FY27, our offshore mix improved to 55.9% in the quarter, reflecting our continued efforts in improving offshore mix.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected to remain in 26-26.5% range going forward
items.quote: Effective tax rate for the quarter was 26%. Going ahead, we expect ETR to remain in the range of 26% to 26.5%.

items.statement: Pipeline up more than 25% year-on-year; targeting $200M+ deal pace for Q3 and Q4
items.quote: Our pipeline is up more than 25% year-on-year. Order bookings are up. So, knock on wood, let's see where it goes.

items.statement: AI revenue definition: significant part of deliverable created through AI stack; 9.5% of quarterly revenue
items.quote: See, what we do is if you take any deliverable that we are creating and a significant part of the deliverable is getting created through leverage of AI stack. Then we classify that as an AI revenue.

items.statement: Upskilled more than 16,000 engineers (67% of workforce) in AI
items.quote: To date, we have upskilled more than 16,000 engineers, about 67% of our workforce in AI.

items.statement: No significant regulatory issues mentioned; Middle East situation minimal portfolio impact
items.quote: Our heart goes out for whatever is happening there, but the impact, we don't have any significant business impact from that yet.

items.statement: Revenue $317.1M, up 2.7% QoQ and 4.8% YoY in constant currency
items.quote: Revenue was $317.1 million, up 2.7% sequentially and 4.8% year-on-year in constant currency on a continued operations basis.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance raised to at least 80% for FY27; FY29 revenue target of ₹10,000 crore expected to be achieved much earlier
items.quote: Friends, you will recall that we began FY27 with a revenue growth aspiration of approximately 20% over FY26. After the first quarter, we revised it to 40%, and today when I present Q2FY27 results to you, i am extremely pleased to share that, based on our current expectations and business visibility, we expect revenue growth of at least 80% in this financial year.

items.statement: Defence revenue target of ₹500-600 crore for FY27, ₹2,000 crore next year, aspiration of ₹5,000 crore in 3 years
items.quote: We remain on track towards our aspiration of approximately ₹500 crore of Defence revenue in FY27.

items.statement: Consolidated order book stands at ₹28,900 crore with multi-year visibility; pipeline of advanced-stage orders expected to convert
items.quote: Our order book stands at ₹28,900 crore, providing multi -year revenue visibility. Beyond this secured business, we also have a strong pipeline of orders at advanced stages likely to be converted into firm contracts in due course.

items.statement: Defence aerospace acquisition brings unexecuted order book of ~₹1,600 crore, expected to close this quarter
items.quote: Importantly, the aerospace business being acquired already has unexecuted order book of approximately ₹1600 crore, providing good visibili ty from the outset.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 25.89% in Q2 FY27 (+640 bps YoY, +264 bps QoQ); management expects margin profile to improve further
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded to 25.89%, improving by 640 basis points year-on-year and 264 basis points quarter-on- quarter, while PAT margin rose to 15.51%, gaining 862 basis points year-on-year and 268 basis points over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Management confident margins will improve due to higher connectivity solutions share, backward integration, and capacity utilization
items.quote: On an overall basis, I would say margin profile is going to get better only. There is no chance I see of getting reverse or less. It is going to get somewhat better only because more orders are coming up for connectivity solutions, more orders are coming for higher fiber capacity fiber cables, which are not so much in supply by many suppliers.

items.statement: Planned investment of ~₹1,800 crore across optical fiber, cable and preform manufacturing to expand capacities and deepen integration
items.quote: To support the next phase, our planned investment of approximately ₹1,800 crore across optical fiber, cable and preform manufacturing will expand capacities and deepen integration.

items.statement: Fiber capacity expanding from 28M to 38M to 43M fkm; cable capacity from 39M to 56M to 63M fkm
items.quote: Fiber optic itself is going from 28 million to 38 million and 38 million to 43 million. Cable is going to about from 39 million fiber kilometers to 56 million and 56 million to 63 million fiber kilometers.

items.statement: Demand accelerating across AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centres and telecom networks; no slowdown seen despite rate hikes
items.quote: Demand continues to accelerate across AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centres and telecom networks. Encouragingly, opportunities with hyperscalers and telecom operators across international markets are steadily converting into firm contracts, strengthening our order pipeline and providing revenue visibility for long term.

items.statement: Telcos restarting fiber purchases after 2-year pause; large telco inquiries received; Europe/Asia data centre growth to offset any US slowdown
items.quote: Telcos have not b een buying much since last 2 years. Reason being simple, because the prices increased so much, telcos were not ready to absorb that shock. But finally, they have realized they also need to increase their fiber network because data has to be ultimately carried from the subscriber by the telcos only in most cases. So they are also going to start buying fiber.

items.statement: Data centre revenue share 65-75%, telco 25-35% in Q2; data centre pricing higher due to specialized fiber (180 micron A2 vs 250 micron G.657B)
items.quote: I would generally say anywhere between data center would be 65% to 75%, telcos would be between 25% to 35%. Somewhere will vary between that.

items.statement: Fiber prices up ~20% in Q2, now stabilizing; long-term contracts have annual price reset clauses; cost pass-through balanced via negotiation
items.quote: Prices in Q2 have really gone up. And I now see more or less stabilizing. But again, I may be completely wrong. I said this in the last quarter also that looks to be stabilizing, but then it has gone up by some 20%.

items.statement: Preform facility (600 MT) on track for Oct'28; mid-term preform solution from Q1 next calendar year; germanium supply discussions initiated for 2-year horizon
items.quote: We are going to start having I can't give you more details on that particular aspect becaus e of commercial confidentiality, but we are going to have a midterm solution for our own preform starting from the first quarter of the next year itself -- calendar year itself.

items.statement: Hyperscalers ~70% of ₹18,500 crore export OFC/DC interconnect order book; domestic orders mainly from telcos
items.quote: Out of INR 18,500 crores, a large portion would be from hyperscalers only, a large portion. I don't have the exact number, but yes, maybe 70% would be from hyperscalers of the export orders.

items.statement: Telecom segment revenue split ~70% hyperscalers / 30% conventional telcos
items.quote: I would probably say it's something like 70-30, something like, not exactly number, something more or less 70-30.

items.statement: Aerospace acquisition expected to close this quarter; brings ₹1,600 crore unexecuted order book; ammunition complex in AP (1,000 acres allotted) construction starting soon
items.quote: We expect to complete the acquisition during the current quarter. Importantly, the aerospace business being acquired already has unexecuted order book of approximately ₹1600 crore, providing good visibili ty from the outset.

items.statement: Connectivity solutions revenue target ₹800 crore FY27 (Q2 ~₹300 crore), ₹2,000 crore next year
items.quote: This year itself, we have a connectivity solution revenue of about more than INR 800 crores we had projected, which may be better rather. And next year, we have projected a revenue of INR 2,000 crores, which was INR 800 crores this year.

items.statement: EPC segment loss of ~₹121 crore in Q2 due to unbilled BharatNet milestones and pending Army AMC; next 2 quarters combined loss ≤₹75-100 crore; profitability expected Q1 FY28
items.quote: So the loss which we incurred because of expenses incurred, but not billed, that will not happen this quarter. So this I would say this loss, which is you have seen INR 121 crores or some crores in the current quarter, next 2 quart ers put together should not be more than INR 75 crores to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Export revenue grew ~493% YoY; hyperscaler orders driving international growth; Europe/Asia data centre demand emerging
items.quote: These initiatives are now translating into meaningful business growth, which is also reflected in our export performance, representing a growth of approximately 493% year-on-year.

items.statement: Key risks: preform price normalization, germanium supply geopolitical risk, interest rate impact on debt-reliant data centre players, but offset by Europe/Asia/telco demand
items.quote: So I don't foresee any big risk out of t his interest rate change, except there may be some closures, some less expansion in heavily debt -reliant companies, but that would be offset by Asia, Europe, and demand of telcos, as I have already said.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on execution capability across optical and defence platforms
items.quote: We are determined to convert it into sustained revenue growth, stronger profitability and lasting value for all our stakeholders.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 will be similar to depreciation; some assets will be leased instead of purchased
items.quote: the idea is to invest as similar to what we have in terms of depreciation. However, the slight change what we have adopted is in certain cases, which will—I think as the machines will roll in, capex will roll in, what you will see at the end of the year, there will be some leased assets also will be coming in

items.statement: TMD order book is ₹3,400 crores with active order book of ₹2,600 crores
items.quote: With respect to the order book, we hold an order book currently of around ₹ 3,400 crores, of which an active order book is roughly ₹2,600 crores.

items.statement: LMW Global export order book is ₹163 crores; LMW China order book is ₹128 crores
items.quote: The order book for exports is closer to ₹163 crores on hand for LMW Global. In LMW China, we have been able to clock a turnover of ₹36 crores, and for the comparative period last year it stood at ₹41 crores. The order book stands at around ₹128 crores.

items.statement: ATC order book is around ₹1,000 crores with 70% metallics and 30% composites
items.quote: the order book still remains the same number; it's around 1,000-odd crores. The percentage of metallics versus composite is around 30% on composite side and 70% would still be metallics.

items.statement: MTD capacity utilization is 75% to 80%
items.quote: We are operating at a utilization of around 75% to 80% in the Machine Tool Division.

items.statement: ATC capacity utilization is closer to 70%
items.quote: ATC, from a capacity standpoint, we will be closer to 70% capacity utilization in this division.

items.statement: MTD seeing consistent order inflow and ~50% growth for current year driven by China+1, upgrades, and auto sector (>50% of deliveries)
items.quote: if you see the growth pattern as of now, I think it is closer to a 50% growth for the current year. There are a lot of positive signs and which we have again mentioned even in the previous call as well, which, for example, the China+1, which we spoke about a few years back today, we are actually seeing it happening on the ground.

items.statement: TMD net order inflow up ~₹200 crores; 60-70% of order book are project orders for expansion
items.quote: even this quarter, if you see the numbers. our net order inflow is up by around 200 odd crores. I think this is an indication and when we actually look at the flow of order book, it is closer to 70% is basically project orders.

items.statement: TMD margins under pressure from unprecedented cost increases (copper, aluminum, electronics); price hike discussions ongoing but no pass-through yet; VAVE efforts underway
items.quote: yes, the costs are hitting us, and I think the discussion on price always is there; it's on the table. But right now, the unprecedented level of cost increase, availability so if you look at copper, aluminum, you just look at apart from steel, which is probably coming much later, the availability of electrical, electronics, it's a very tough situation out there.

items.statement: MTD 5-axis machines are high-value, low-volume with potential for higher margins vs imported machines; volume growth also drives operational efficiency and margins
items.quote: 5 axis machines are high value, low volume. Yes, the ideal scenario is when we place our machines against the imported machines, you expect to get more value for the machines and thereby higher margin. But like I said, we will see two things happening in the machine tool division. We have got enough volume to still flow through. As you increase volume, you will see incremental operational efficien

items.statement: TMD: no cost pass-through currently for domestic industry (fixed price); active internal discussion on price hikes; VAVE activities to control costs
