items.statement: IRDAI consultation paper on insurance commissions under discussion; seeking softer landing
items.quote: This thing is currently, I would say, under discussion, right. So, for us, we would obviously engage with the regulator and try to see if the industry, we are part of the industry, whether the industry, as we said, gets a soft landing.

items.statement: CGTMSE/CGFMU covers provide capital efficiency via risk weight reduction
items.quote: Because the risk weights go down on CGTMSE coverage on the SME portfolio, we actually get a lot of capital efficiency and that leads to a capital release actually, right.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio fallen to ~39%; targeting further reduction
items.quote: If you see our cost-to-income ratio actually has been falling. Cost-to-income ratio right now is about 39%. And it has fallen below 40%. Our objective is to drive it down further downwards.

items.statement: Fee and other income typically 180-185 bps; Q1 impacted by excess liquidity investment income
items.quote: Usually, it is about 180 to 185 bps. That has been the range for us. So major difference that you see in terms of reduction is on account of that.

items.statement: Rabi crop forecast near normal; reservoir levels at 71% pan-India
items.quote: Our rabi crop, the overall reservoir levels are at about 71% pan-India. I think that's sufficient to support rabi crop, right. And I also foresee that the rabi crop should also be near normal.

items.statement: Gold Loan branches reaching critical size in average 6 months
items.quote: Our branches are attaining critical size very fast, right. We have branches attaining critical size on an average of 6 months is what the branches are attaining critical size.

items.statement: BESS installation target of 10 GWh for FY27, confident of surpassing it
items.quote: We are very committed to not only commission the 10 gigawatt by the end of the year, but would be definitely able to surpass it too.

items.statement: Committed to INR 2.4 lakh crore capex program through FY30, backed by long-term contracts and prudent capital allocation
items.quote: We remain focused on disciplined execution of our INR2.4 lakh crores capex program through FY '30, backed by securing new capacities under long-term contracts and prudent capital allocation.

items.statement: Operational capacity reached 20.8 GW in H1 FY27, up 24% YoY; 10.8 GW commissioned at Khavda
items.quote: Adani Green Energy delivered another strong performance in H1 FY '27, crossing the significant milestone of 20 gigawatts of operational capacity. Our 20.8 gigawatt portfolio supplied clean power equivalent to the needs of more than 4.4 million homes

items.statement: BESS capacity at 6.6 GWh as of Q2 FY27, over 50% of India's operational BESS; targeting >10 GWh by year-end
items.quote: During the quarter, we commissioned 3 gigawatt hour of battery energy storage at Khavda, taking our total installed storage capacity to 6.6 gigawatt hour. This capacity accounts for more than 50% of India's operational BESS.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 93% (INR 7,957 crore, up 41% YoY); Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 92% (INR 3,835 crore, up 51% YoY)
items.quote: Revenue from power supply in H1 FY '27 increased 36% year-on-year to INR8,299 crores, while EBITDA grew 41% Y -o-Y to INR7,957 crores, enabling us to deliver industry -leading EBITDA margin of 93%.

items.statement: Strong demand from AI, data centers, hyperscalers, and C&I customers for firm, dispatchable renewable plus storage solutions
items.quote: Looking ahead, we see significant opportunities emerging from growing needs for firm and dispatchable renewable energy, rising power demand from AI, data centers and hyperscalers alongside growing demand for integrated renewables plus storage solutions fro m commercial as well as industrial customers

items.statement: 3.5 GWh of BESS capacity tied up in long-term contracts; remaining 3.1 GWh (of 6.6 GWh total) in process of tying up
items.quote: Currently, we have 3.5 gigawatts. Ashish Khanna: 3.5 gigawatt hour, which is already tied up. The rest, since it has just come at the end of this last quarter, we are in the process of doing it

items.statement: All PPAs on take-or-pay basis; deemed generation paid for grid curtailment; payment received for scheduled power not taken by procurer or grid
items.quote: See, all our PPAs are on a take-or-pay basis on the supply, which we give it to them. Mohit Kumar: Understood. Ashish Khanna: And curtailment, whenever there is a curtailment from the grid to us, specifically being asked to backdown, we are paid for it as the deemed generation

items.statement: Leverage to remain in 5.6x range till FY28-29, then decline to 4.5x and below 4x as operating assets grow and debt amortizes
items.quote: So, see what happens is our leverage , it will be in this range till FY '28, '29. After '29, '30, as the more and more operating assets starts to increase as a percentage of under-construction assets, as we move towards that, the leverage profile will start to be in the range between 4.5 to 5x, and then moving towards 4 x and below 4x also as we move further into the number of years

items.statement: Strategy combines solar, wind, BESS, and pump storage; 500 MW Chitravathi pump storage progressing to completion by year-end
items.quote: While our maiden 500-megawatt pump storage project at Chitravathi is also progressing towards completion by year -end. At Khavda, the world's largest renewable energy plant, we have commissioned 10.8 gigawatt hour of solar, wind and hybrid capacity.

items.statement: 30% of loan book USD-denominated; principal and interest fully hedged per lender documents; RG2 hedged to FY30, RG1 to FY28 with rollover planned
items.quote: About 30% is in dollar denominated. Within that 30% dollar denominated, we fully hedge our principal plus interest. There is no change in that policy because that's governed by the lender documents.

items.statement: Rajat Seksaria highlighted BESS execution speed (1-10 months for world's largest plants) providing flexibility to deconstrain solar/wind from transmission delays
items.quote: So it's a relatively short period of time. We're talking about a month, 8 to 10 months for the largest plants in the world. So that leaves us an adequate amount of flexibility should the situation demand so, we now have an added tool in our arsenal to respond to that

items.statement: Retained #1 global ranking in alternative electricity subsector by FTSE Russell for second consecutive year; Khavda BESS recognized as largest project of year at India Energy Storage Week 2026
items.quote: On sustainability, AGEL retained its number 1 global ranking in alternative electricity subsector by FTSE Russell for the second consecutive year. Our Khavda BESS project was also recognized as the largest project of the year at India Energy Storage Week 2026.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR300-350 crores
items.quote: This year, we believe -- we trust we should fetch revenue between INR300 crores and INR350 crores.

items.statement: FY27 year-end order book target of INR600-800 crores
items.quote: With that, I think we believe, with the end of the year, we may maintain between -- the order book may maintain between INR600 crores and INR800 crores.

items.statement: FY27 PAT margin guidance of 9-12%
items.quote: Based on the order book, the margin can be maintained between -- the PAT margin can be maintained between 9% to 12%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 order inflow of 11 orders worth INR209.24 crores
items.quote: During H1 FY27, we secured 11 orders aggregating INR209.24 crores, with execution timelines ranging between 7 months and 17 months.

items.statement: Current order book stands at over INR565.80 crores
items.quote: Our curr ent order book stands at over INR565.80 crores, providing strong execution visibility for the coming periods

items.statement: Order book product mix: 75-78% power transformers, 16-17% distribution, 5% inverter duty
items.quote: Out of this INR565 crores, distribution is around 16% to 17%, that is less than INR95 crores. And power transformer is around INR440 crores that comes around 78% -- 75% to 78%. And inverter duty transformers is around INR30 crores, that comes 5% of the total order book.

items.statement: Execution timeline: INR353 crores before March 2027, INR212 crores after
items.quote: Actually as per customer requirements, before the end of this March 2027, INR353 crores is to be executed. After March, it's INR212 crores.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 17.42%, PAT margin 10.07%
items.quote: EBITDA has increased by 65.46% year-to-year to INR23.62 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 17.42%. Profit after tax grew by 45.09% to INR13.65 crores, with a PAT margin of 10.07%.

items.statement: Power transformer margins slightly higher but absorbed by overheads
items.quote: power transformers, the margin is slightly higher than the distribution transformer. But at the same time, it is absorbed by the overheads. So, it needs skilled manpower, so we have to deploy experienced people. So, this 0. 5% or 1% margin is absorbed by the -- so this margin will maintain and it will sustain

items.statement: 70-75% of order book covered under price variation clauses
items.quote: Importantly, around 70% to 75% of our order book is covered under price variation clauses, which provides a degree of protection against volatility in key raw material prices.

items.statement: Pressure from higher CRGO steel and transformer oil prices
items.quote: During the period, we have seen pressure from higher prices of key inputs, particularly CRGO steel and transformer oil.

items.statement: Kannur facility ramp-up progressing; targeting 40-50% utilization by March 2027, 80% next year
items.quote: This year, we are expecting 50% of -- 40% to 50% before this March. And next year, almost 80%, I think we should utilize.

items.statement: Strong demand environment supported by transmission, renewable energy, industrial expansion
items.quote: We are encouraged by the demand environment across the tran sformer industry, supported by continued investments in transmission and distribution infrastructure, renewable energy integration and industrial expansion

items.statement: Good demand expected for next 8-10 years in power sector
items.quote: As per market information, next 8 to 10 years, there will be good demand for this power sector.

items.statement: Order book split: 27-28% government, 72-73% non-government
items.quote: On INR565 crores, almost 27%, 28% is from government and balance 72%, 73% from non-government.

items.statement: PGCIL approval process underway, expected within a year
items.quote: This PGCIL approval is on the process. So we need to -- this all documents is getting ready. And we are yet to approach PGCIL. So, this year, within a year, we should -- we believe we should get the PGCIL approval.

items.statement: Inventory to be maintained at 2-2.5 months (INR60-70 crores) to support revenue growth
items.quote: because we are expecting this year revenue -- top line of INR350 crores. And for that, we need to keep inventory at least to 2 months to 2.5 months inventory we need to hold. So on that basis, see, this inven tory will maintain, that is INR 60 crores, INR70 crores of invento ry we'll maintain

items.statement: Cash flow from operations expected to turn positive in H2 FY27
items.quote: Yes, it should get positive in this second half.

items.statement: Receivable terms: private customers 10-30% advance, 90% before dispatch, 45-60 days credit for repeat; government 60-90 days
items.quote: Private, some customers, we are getting advance. Most of the customers we get 10% to 30% advance. And before dispatch, we use to get 90% and balance 5% to 10% will be after commissioning. And for repeat customers, we used to give credit for 45 days to 60 days. From the government, we get payments in 60 to 90 days.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue split: ~60% power transformers, balance distribution and inverter duty
items.quote: Almost like 60% will be from power transformer and the balance from distribution and inverter duty transformers.

items.statement: Realization: distribution transformers ~INR20 lakhs/MVA, power transformers ~INR10 lakhs/MVA
items.quote: Distribution transformer will be around INR20 lakhs per MVA. Power transformer will be around INR10 lakhs.

items.statement: Company capacity small relative to overall industry expansion, no impact expected
items.quote: And our capacity is -- when compared to the overall capacity expansion, our capacity is too low. So I think this will not impact our business.

items.statement: Power transformers require skilled manpower, deploying experienced people
items.quote: It needs skilled manpower, so we have to deploy experienced people.

items.statement: Offtake agreement with Pirelli to start in calendar year 2027 and scale to 800,000 tires per year by calendar year 2030
items.quote: We expect the offtake from this partnership to commence in 2027. And this will scale up to supply 800,000 Pirelli-branded tires per year by the year of 2030.

items.statement: JV formation deadline is calendar year 2030, subject to preset conditions
items.quote: We have till 2030 to announce the work on the JV, and then once we have that ready, we will probably come up with an announcement when we already. That's the deadline.

items.statement: Phase 1 PCR capacity at Bhuj is 6,700 tires per day; Pirelli offtake will use ~20% of Phase 1 capacity
items.quote: So, the 6,700 capacity that we have in phase one, maybe 80% of that would be still for the BKT brand. Only the remaining will be for the Pirelli offtake.

items.statement: Plant operates roughly 350-355 days per year
items.quote: Roughly 350 days to 355 days.

items.statement: Pirelli offtake covers 17-inch and above tires; BKT brand will address full portfolio from 13-inch upwards
items.quote: It will be 17-inch and above, which we will be giving them. And regarding the, there is no restriction on either party on supplying their own respective branded tires to whichever part of the world that respective company would like to sell to.

items.statement: BKT will use its own technology for BKT-branded tires; Pirelli technology used only for Pirelli-branded tires
items.quote: We do not want to rely on any third-party partner for their own technology or designs. We will make everything on our own. There will be a clear partition between what we produce for them and what we produce for us and using our own technology.

items.statement: Pirelli offtake primarily for Indian market; some portion may go to global markets
items.quote: Yes, there would be some component which may be used by them for their global markets, but majorly it will be for them to serve the Indian market.

items.statement: Management declined to disclose revenue or margin potential for Pirelli offtake; stated policy of maintaining blended margins unchanged
items.quote: I think at this stage, we would like to stay away from those numbers. We are yet working on those, and we'll come back at a later. Once we start the business, we'll have more clarity on that.

items.statement: Second phase envisages 50-50 JV and dedicated plant for high-value passenger car tires for both brands
items.quote: The agreement paves the way for the second phase in which there is an envisagement, at certain conditions, the creation of a 50-50 joint venture and the construction of a production plant dedicated to high-value passenger car tires, both with the Pirelli brand, as well as the BKT brand, to serve India and other international markets.

items.statement: Service agreement covers testing and simulation infrastructure access for BKT products for a consideration
items.quote: See, the service agreement is largely in the field of testing, simulation, sort of technical things, where the infrastructure in India is poor and currently poor. And we will -- as a partner, they will extend willing support to us for rendering those services by opening up their infrastructure for our BKT-branded products, where we can use their infrastructure to test, simulate, etcetera, and ther

items.statement: India passenger car market growing 6-7% annually; premium segment expected to grow faster
items.quote: India is a fast-growing passenger car market, which is growing at 6% to 7% annually. The premium car market is expected to grow at a faster pace in India over the next few years.

items.statement: Pirelli targets super-premium segment (~10% of market); BKT targets full market breadth
items.quote: They are looking to address the very high end of the Indian market, which is not a very big market to start with. It's about 10% of the market is what you can classify loosely as the very high end of the market.

items.statement: Non-OHT revenue target of 20% by FY30 unchanged; Pirelli offtake revenues included within this target
items.quote: No, it will be part of that same 20%.

items.statement: BKT carbon black to be used for Pirelli-branded tires produced at Bhuj
items.quote: Also, Arvind-ji, one more thing is that the carbon black business of ours will also benefit, because for these tires that we will be making for them, we will be using BKT-branded carbon black only.

items.statement: JV formation subject to preset conditions; no guarantee JV will materialize
items.quote: There are some preset conditions which both parties have to reach. If we reach there, then that will sort of trigger the discussion for a JV.

items.statement: No royalty payments discussed or agreed for JV or offtake arrangement
items.quote: We have never spoken about any royalty. None of our press releases also states any royalty. So, there is no discussion of royalty, sir.

items.statement: Partnership validates BKT manufacturing quality and accelerates go-to-market for on-road segment
items.quote: This agreement and partnership is a landmark moment in BKT's history, especially at a time when we are at an early stage in our on-highway tire journey. Our partnership with Pirelli is a testimonial to BKT's capabilities, BKT's quality standards, and the strength of the BKT brand

items.statement: AUM growth guidance for FY27 cut to 15-17% from 18% earlier due to monsoon impact
items.quote: Looking at the impact of the war situation in West Asia and the weak monsoon, we have been growing a little less than that. The first quarter, our growth was around 15%. In the second quarter, it was 17%. We will be anywhere growing anywhere between these two 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance remains 2% for full year with temporary 30-40 bps elevation for 1-2 quarters due to seasonal monsoon impact
items.quote: Credit cost, we had given a long -term guidance of 2%. But tempora rily, maybe certain geographies, it may go up by 30, 40 basis points, is what we indicated. And in the being seasonal and monsoon being weak, we are seeing a little increase in Stage 2 and Stage 1 in certain geography. I believe that it will be seasonal and it should get normalized to overall expectation of 2

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio medium to long-term guidance at 25%
items.quote: Having said that, the medium to long-term guidance will be the cost to income will be around 25%.

items.statement: Gold loan book target to double in 3 years from 2.5% to 5% of AUM remains unchanged
items.quote: No change in there is no change. We will go as per the plan.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle sales grew 28.7% YoY in Q2 FY27 with M&HCV up 37% and LCV up 23.8%
items.quote: commercial vehicle sales has increased by 28.7% in Q2 FY27, and stands at 3.09 lakh units against 2.4 lakh units sold in the Q2 FY26. Within commercial vehicle, medium and heavy commercial vehicle sales recorded growth of 37% in Q2 FY2 7, and stands at 1,21,171 units against 88,431 units sold in Q2 FY2 6. LCV's sales recorded a growth of 23.8% in Q2, and stands at 1.88 lakh units versus 1.52 lakh

items.statement: NIM expanded to 9.52% in Q2 FY27 from 8.19% YoY and 9.04% QoQ due to capital infusion
items.quote: Our net interest margin in Q2 FY27 was 9.52% as against 8.19% in Q2 FY26 and 9.04% in Q1 FY27.

items.quote: The cost of liabilities on balance sheet is 8.41% versus 8.56% in the previous quarter, a reduction of 15 basis points, and from March, it is down by 18 basis points. The incremental cost of fund for the quarter was 7.3 versus 7.7 in the previous quarter.

items.statement: AUM grew 16.96% YoY to INR3,29,021.72 crores and 4.85% QoQ
items.quote: Our AUM as on 30th September 2026 registered a growth of 16.96% over Q2 FY26 and a 4.85% sequentially. Our AUM stood at INR3,29,021.72 crores as against INR2,81,309.46 crores a year ago and INR313,798. That is INR3,13,798.39 crores in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 25.71% YoY to INR54,079.02 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We registered disbursement growth of 25.71% year -on-year. Our disbursement in Q2 FY2 7 this year aggr egated to INR54,079.02 crores versus INR43,019.17 crores in Q2 FY26

items.quote: our MSME was mostly focused in the southern market . So, we expect MSME book to grow much faster than other segment because of th e bigger geographical reach

items.quote: On our asset quality, gross Stage 3 in Q2 FY2 7 stood at 4.65% and net Stage 3 at 2.31%, as against 4.57% gross and 2.49% net in Q2 FY26, and was 4.64% gross and 2.33% net in Q1

items.quote: See, if you see the absolute amount, it is still coming down quarter-on-quarter, even though the disbursement have been better this quarter. Similarly, gross Stage 2, if you see, it's 953 previous quarter, this quarter is 963, so not much of a difference as such. So it's more of a denominator effect,

items.quote: No, no, it's basically because we had introduced EMI and interest servicing gold loans. Abhishek Murarka: Okay. So that's the only thing. So once people get used to it, then I think there may not be a

items.statement: MSME unsecured exposure at 28% of book, 72% secured
items.quote: 28% is unsecured and 72% is secured.

items.statement: Yield differential between new and used vehicle financing 200-400 bps depending on segment
items.quote: It is normally it depends upon segment to segment. It will be between 200 to 400 basis points.

items.quote: This quarter we have started our borrowing program, be it bonds, bank borrowing. It is back to the pre-March level. So, we have borrowed around INR27,000 crores in the last quarter. Liquidity-wise, we have brought down the liquidity, and it is now at our 3 months of future liability level. items.quote: affair, the income may come down by 50% of what it is now. items.quote: The Board also declared an interim dividend of INR6.5 per share, that is 325%. The record date for the entitlement thereof has been fixed at October 29, 2026.

items.statement: West Asia crisis and weak monsoon (El Niño) creating headwinds, 51.2% of India abnormally dry, impacting rural consumption in drought-prone areas
items.quote: As you're aware, there were multiple headwinds for us in last two quarters, one due to West Asia crisis, where the petroleum product prices went up, and so many other raw material prices went up, and secondly, now due to El Niño situation, monsoon being a weak. In spite of that, the company has performed very well.

items.statement: FY27 lamination volume target maintained at 82,000+ tons
items.quote: FY27, I think we'll still hold on to the upgraded guidance given last quarter.

items.quote: the line that you see as 6,054 tons for the half year, these are casting and machine components going as pure vanilla machine components. To do the comparison vis-a-vis the overall sales, you also have to add the other machine components going into the lamination assemblies

items.quote: It would be about INR2,350 crores to INR2,400 crores. Pranay Chatterjee: Got it. Akshay Pitti: At Q2 FY prices, sorry, at Q2 FY27 prices, right? Pranay Chatterjee: Correct. items.statement: New INR450 crore greenfield lamination and machining facility in Bangalore phased through FY31
items.quote: The total planned capex for this project is INR450 crores, comprising approximately INR125 crores towards land procurement and the remaining INR325 crores towards infrastructure, plant, and equipment.

items.statement: Cumulative capex INR740 crores including earlier INR290 crore Hyderabad project
items.quote: The capex announced earlier was INR290 crores. The current capex announced is INR450 crores. And the cumulative capex for the two announcements is INR740 crores.

items.statement: Capex funding through internal accruals and debt, practically fully from internal accruals by FY31
items.quote: Practically, it should be funded entirely from internal accruals if that clarifies.

items.statement: Bangalore lamination capacity to increase from 108,000 to 160,000 metric tons per annum by FY31
items.quote: The objective is to consolidate our lamination operations in Bangalore and progressively increase our sheet metal capacity to 160,000 metric tons per annum and machining capacity to 1.31 million hours by financial year '31.

items.statement: Hyderabad greenfield casting and machining facility commissioning phased through FY30
items.quote: A few months ago, we had announced the first of our major capacity expansion for a greenfield facility in Hyderabad covering the casting and machining. The project was to be commissioned in a phased manner through FY30.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility across data centers, railways, mining, off-highway, and specialized industrial applications
items.quote: Beyond data centers, we continue to see strong demand visibility across railways, metros, mining, off-highway equipment, and specialized industrial applications.

items.statement: Data center segment at 7% of revenue, seen as strong near-term growth opportunity
items.quote: Among these segments, data centers have emerged as a strong near-term growth opportunity. As we have highlighted on multiple occasions before, the demand remains robust driven by significant power requirements of AI-led data center infrastructure.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 15.8%, impacted by forex loss, consumable, packing, fuel and power costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margins stood at 15.8%, impacted by an increase in forex loss, increase in consumable and packing cost, and along with increase in fuel and power costs.

items.statement: Sustainable blended EBITDA margin 17%+ at current steel prices, 18% potentially achievable with value-added mix
items.quote: On a blended basis, you should be looking -- I'm talking of current raw material prices. When I say current quarter two raw material price levels. Steel prices are obviously increasing and decreasing every quarter. But if you take a Q2 price level, your sustainable blended margin should be in the vicinity of 17% plus

items.statement: Strong order visibility from marquee customers in data centers, mining, off-highway, railways backing capacity expansion
items.quote: This investment was backed by strong order visibility from marquee customers across high-growth sectors such as data centers, mining, off-highway vehicles, and railways.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 segment revenue: traction motor/railway 27%, power generation 16%, industrial/commercial 12%, mining/oil/gas 10%, special purpose motors 8%, data centers 7%
items.quote: In terms of segment-wise revenue, Q2 FY27 traction motor and railway components continued to contribute the highest share of the revenue at 27%. Power generation accounted for 16%, followed by industrial and commercial applications at 12%, mining, oil, and gas at 10%, special purpose motors at 8%, and data centers at 7%.

items.statement: Data center revenue share not expected to exceed 9% of overall revenue in next 3-5 years
items.quote: However, I would not look at it increasing more than probably 9-odd percent of the overall revenue as a segment. We see that other segments like mining and special-purpose motors, power gen in general, will also grow, and overall mix should remain similar.

items.statement: Top 5-7 customers still contribute major revenue, concentration managed at beneficial ownership level
items.quote: I would say that even if you look forward, I would say, the major revenue will still come from the top five, top seven customers, because when we do the grouping, we would take the beneficial ownership level.

items.statement: Trade payables increased to INR470 crores from INR236 crores, strategy to sustain higher payables to fund capex cycle
items.quote: Yes, it is here to sustain. We will be looking to work more on the trade payables side rather than, leverage our cash positions to buy materials going forward, as we are going into a capex cycle over the next 4 years.

items.statement: Total borrowings currently INR640 crores, capex to be funded by internal accruals and debt mix
items.quote: how will it be funded given the total borrowings currently stand at INR640 crores?

items.statement: Maharashtra incentive claim deferred to FY28 to maximize recovery, eligible for INR400 crores over 7 or 9 years
items.quote: We have decided to defer this claim of incentive in the current year to the next financial year, with the objective of maximizing its cash flow.

items.statement: Maharashtra incentive recovery estimated at INR40 crores per annum near term, 7-year approval requires INR57 crores/year, 9-year would be INR44 crores/year
items.quote: Based on the local Maharashtra sales, we don't estimate that we would be able to recover more than INR40 crores per annum, irrespective of the eligibility, at least in the near term.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 lamination and assembly volumes 21,600 tons, up 26% YoY; H1 volumes 41,000 tons, up 22% YoY
items.quote: On the volumes front, total lamination and assembly volumes for the quarter stood at 21,600 tons, a growth of 26% Y-o-Y. H1 lamination volumes increased to 41,000 tons, up by 22% compared to H1 FY26.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 raw casting and machine components volume 3,086 tons, up 6% YoY; H1 6,054 tons, up 1.6% YoY
items.quote: Total raw casting and machine components volume for Q2 FY27 was 3,086 tons, growing by 6%, and 6,054 tons for H1, with a growth of 1.6%.

items.statement: Casting capacity utilization ~52% in Q2 FY27 (24,600 tons capacity vs ~3,100 tons sales volume)
items.quote: So, if you look at it, what I had given in a conversation in the last Investor call, INR400 crores, the Board has just approved INR450 crores instead of INR400 crores. It's just a in our estimate, which I had given that time. So, it is exactly what we discussed in the last call. In terms of timeline, it's going to be done by

items.statement: Q3 FY27 volume challenge due to holiday season in India (Dussehra, Diwali) and Europe/US (Christmas)
items.quote: Execution will be a challenge. Quarter three is always a little bit of challenge, considering the holiday season in India and Europe. We have Dussehra, Diwali, then Christmas for our European and American clients.

items.statement: Exploring copper winding outsourcing initially, may bring in-house if demand and margins justify
items.quote: We have not discussed it to bring it in-house, but we are exploring to get it outsourced to start with and get into that segment slowly. Mayank Chaturvedi: Okay. Akshay Pitti: If we see enough demand coming and margin profile being strong enough, then we could consider bringing it in

items.statement: Gross margin target of 36%-38%
items.quote: Basically, we're looking at the gross margin level at being approximately in the region of at least 36% -38% is what we're looking at ideally is what we should be in a position to do.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR2,000 crores by FY29 on track
items.quote: So we're not very far off track. We're fairly on track, I would say. This year, the last 6, 8, 9 months have shown that opportunities are there and the market is moving in a certain direction.

items.statement: Capex of INR30-35 crores for FY27, rising to INR60-70 crores for FY27-28
items.quote: This year will be approximately INR30 -INR35 crores, which if you see the trend for the last 2 years is similar. But we do have capex planned which will be in the -- for the next 2 financial years, it will be in the region of INR60-INR65 crores to INR70 crores.

items.statement: Q2 gross margin 34.2% due to input cost inflation and growth strategy
items.quote: Gross margins for the quarter was 34.2%, with input cost inflation, particularly higher steel and other raw material prices, being one of the key pressures.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin 11.2%, slightly higher than last year
items.quote: Despite this pressure, EBITDA grew 9% in the quarter and H1 EBITDA margin was 11.2%, slightly higher than last year.

items.statement: Revenue grew 23% YoY in Q2 and H1, supported by healthy demand across core end markets
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter grew about 23% year-on-year to INR345 crores and H1 revenue was also up 23% at INR654 crores. Growth was supported by healthy demand across core end markets.

items.statement: Volume growth in mid-teens, expecting continued double-digit volume growth
items.quote: It's in the approximate high, I would say, teens somewhere I'll just put it there because I don't want to get into too much more of that, but we're approximately in the mid-teen level.

items.statement: Inventory build-up 75-80% due to order backlog, 15-20% due to steel availability concerns
items.quote: One is order back. So that's, I would say, 75% -80% of the reason. Another 15% -20% of the reason is availability of steel in the market was a concern.

items.statement: Steel prices increased 7-8% QoQ in Q2, calibrated price increases taken
items.quote: Percentage increase in steel Q2 versus Q1 must be anywhere in the region of 7%, 8%.

items.statement: Most cost increases passed through, Q2 had temporary lag in pass-through
items.quote: All of it will get passed through -- always it got passed through a bit later than I would have liked. In Q2, it happened a bit later. Now it's getting done now.

items.statement: 60-70% of incremental growth to come from product mix improvement
items.quote: If I have to estimate, I'd say 60%-70% of that growth will come from product mix, which doesn't necessarily mean that it can't be at the right margin level.

items.statement: Export share 15-20% in H1, Middle East 80-85% of exports, expanding into Europe
items.quote: Anywhere in the region of 15% to 20% with it in H1 being slightly more -- being slightly in the higher part of that.

items.statement: Middle East is 80-85% of export sales, expanding into US, Africa, Europe
items.quote: But the Middle East is about 80%-85% of the export sales. But we expect that the other markets will grow and these FTAs and all of that, that are coming in, we're seeing greater push, greater pull.

items.statement: Focusing on top 50-100 consumers for direct engagement and wallet share
items.quote: So we talk of the top 50, top 100 consumers in the country, we feel we should be more aggressive sitting in front of them. That takes time. It doesn't happen overnight.

items.statement: Investing in new consumables line per capex plan to modernize manufacturing base
items.quote: On operations, we are investing in new consumables line in line with the capex plan we had shared earlier. These investments will modernize our manufacturing base, support future demand and improve our ability to scale efficiently.

items.statement: Short-term borrowing increase due to LCs/BGs and strategic purchases, balance sheet strong for capex
items.quote: So most of it -- so just to explain, a lot of it has got to do with LCs and BGs and stuff like that as we go. So a fair amount of it is from that angle. We have a little bit of the working capital perspective, very controllable levels.

items.statement: No major debt or equity dilution needed for planned capex
items.quote: No, I don't think so. I think we're quite well. Our balance sheet is quite strong to be able to take that on. So I don't think that's part of the plan at the moment.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR7.5 per equity share declared
items.quote: To reward our shareholders for their trust, the Board has declared an interim dividend of INR7.5 per equity share.

items.statement: ESOP plan for ~50 senior employees introduced over a year ago
items.quote: Yes. We have ESOP plan for approximately 50 people in the company are part of our ESOP plan with senior management, obviously having a larger chunk of that. We introduced ESOP plan probably a year and just a little bit over a year ago.

items.statement: Exploring acquisition options in automation/robotics, early stages
items.quote: We're exploring options that would be -- I think it's very early that nothing is going to happen because the ecosystem you're dealing in is very tiny. So it's not like a very large industry.

items.statement: Raw material inflation across steel, copper, chemicals, electronics, PCBs with import factor
items.quote: Everything, I think, everything across the board, everywhere it's going up. I don't think it's only particular to us. But I think everywhere across the board, copper, we've seen fluctuating quite a bit.

items.statement: Welding consumable growth linked to steel consumption data
items.quote: And it's simply related to steel consumption. So it's about steel consumption data. If you see growth happening there, you believe that steel will continue to be consumed at good levels in various industries.

items.statement: Steel prices not softening soon, but not increasing as rapidly either
items.quote: I don't see them softening anytime soon. I don't think they're going to be as rapidly increas ed either, but that's my perspective on it right now

items.statement: Unorganized sector not a concern, focus on organized competitive sector market share
items.quote: So I think everything has a place in the market. And I don't get stressed about the unorganized sector too much. I care about within the organized competitive sector that we play in, how is our market share going from that angle.

items.statement: Payables decline due to mix of availability, growth reasons, product mix, will stabilize
items.quote: No, it's a mix of availability. It's a mix of what the conditions are demanding. It's a mix of our growth reasons that we have in certain segments and product mix. So I think it's from that perspective, it will stabilize.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 15-20% YoY for next 10-15 quarters
items.quote: So as I've been saying, 15% to 20% volume growth year -on-year you can safely consider for Rajratan. It is a combination of growth in Thailand, in Chennai and some in Indore. So this will continue for next at least 10 to 15 quarters.

items.statement: Full year export target of more than 30,000 tons from India and Thailand combined
items.quote: This year total export target from India and Thailand is more than 30,000 tons.

items.statement: India export target of 14,000-15,000 tons for FY27
items.quote: Close to 14,000 tons, 15,000 tons.

items.statement: Consolidated volume target of 160,000 tons for FY27
items.quote: So this year we should end up close to 160,000 tons of business.

items.statement: Thailand brownfield expansion capex of INR100 crores from now, total INR125 crores including past spend
items.quote: Broadly, we should be able to do it in INR100 crores, ballpark number. Last year or up till now we have spent about INR20 crores in acquiring a new factory there, where we'll be shifting some of the facilities. And so there is hardly investment in infrastructure. So investment will be there only in the machines and plant and machinery. So total, including everything, it will be INR125 crores, but

items.statement: Chennai expansion incremental capex of INR30-35 crores to reach 60,000 tons from 30,000 tons
items.quote: I recall we had spent 270 crores for a facility of 30,000 tons, and we spent another 30 crores, 35 crores to complete it to 60,000 tons.

items.statement: Chennai plant expansion to 60,000 tons on track for completion in Q3 FY27, current rated capacity 40,000 tons
items.quote: Our Chennai plant expansion to 60,000 tons is on track and should be completed in the current quarter. We are almost at full capacity utilization in the initial 30,000 tons capacity we have installed -- which we had installed in the first phase and now expanding it to 60,000 tons.

items.statement: Indian tyre market growing at 8-10% with no demand dip seen in last year
items.quote: The Indian tire market is growing at 8% to 10% now. In the last entire year, we didn't see a dip in demand. We didn't see even two, three months where customers had cut down the production, okay?

items.statement: Thailand domestic tyre industry growing at 10-15% locally
items.quote: if you look at regional growth, Thailand capacities are growing much faster, okay, which ar e growing at 10% to 15% locally. Domestically, Thailand tyre industry is growing

items.statement: Current EBITDA margins at rock bottom (12.7-13%), should not fall below this level
items.quote: I can say that our current margins are rock bottom. It should not go below this, so anything from here will improve.

items.statement: Thailand EBITDA expected to improve in coming quarters, India EBITDA improvement limited due to competition
items.quote: Our projection for Thailand is better. You will see better number from Thailand in the coming quarter as far as EBITDA is concerned. We do not expect much improvement in EBITDA in the remaining 2 quarters in India.

items.statement: Price hikes taken in some counters, remaining to be passed on by end of Q3 FY27
items.quote: We have been able to take some hike in some cases where prices were not finalized or we were not committed at old price, but remaining we will have to take end of this quarter.

items.statement: Input cost pressures from energy, gas, petroleum, packing, dies, transportation and sea freight
items.quote: The impact is more of other costs mainly energy, gas, petroleum, packing products and dies, everything has gone up, transportation cost. Yes. Export sea freights, they are like crazy.

items.statement: Thailand premium customer mix to grow from 30-32% to 40% in coming year
items.quote: Currently, around 30% to 32% of our sales are towards the premium customers, and as sir has mentioned, it will take time to grow, but few marquee customers are already approved and we will supply them. So we expect this to grow by 40%, means 30% will become 40% in the coming year product mix.

items.statement: India premium customer share already at 50-60%, limited further consolidation expected
items.quote: it won't make a big difference in India because in India, premium customers we are already at more than 50%, 60% counter share. So we are not projecting to further consolidate that market share.

items.statement: Major approvals from global tyre MNCs in Thailand for supply to Europe, America and Southeast Asia
items.quote: For us in Thailand, we have got major approvals from world leaders in tyres. Whom we were supplying locally, now we are supposed to supply them in their different locations in Europe, America and Southeast Asia.

items.statement: Only supplier of green bead wire from Thailand using 92-95% scrap-based wire rod
items.quote: Thailand, we are the only company in bead wire space who can supply green bead wire because our source of raw material is green, and which is not available in India, which is not available elsewhere in the world.

items.statement: Consolidated borrowing increase driven by 27% revenue growth and higher export working capital cycle
items.quote: There has been 27% revenue growth. So majority of this is working capital borrowing. And it is more so because working capital cycle for export is higher than the local. So majority of this is borrowing for working capital, and it is in proportion to the growth of business.

items.statement: Thailand expansion funded by combination of internal accruals and bank loans below 4%
items.quote: Both. It's a combination of internal accrual. Thailand balance sheet is accruing cash on a month-on-month basis. And there are banks; loan is also at a very competitive rate, below 4% we borrow from bank. So it will be a combination of loan and internal accrual.

items.statement: CBAM quota in Europe creating advantage for Thailand green bead wire exports
items.quote: And then there is CBAM in Europe, there is a quota which has started in Europe. So Rajratan, being an agile and smart company, we are able to supply bigger quantities in those markets, and we are of course taking risk of all this volatility.

items.statement: Main competitors identified as Bansal Wire and Tata Steel, more competition with Tata Steel currently
items.quote: We consider both of them as competitors, but Bansal is new. Still, according to us, he is not in all the counters able to supply. So more competition with Tata than

items.statement: Thailand realization at INR97,500 per ton driven by premium customer approvals and export improvement
items.quote: We are getting more approvals from major customers, the multinational clients and more volume will be going to them in the current quarter and next quarter. And also the export f rom Thailand is also improving. So all this will improve the performance of Thailand and that is why the capacity is -- further capacity is planned

items.statement: Freight rates volatile, company taking risk on DDP basis with some freight surcharge agreements
items.quote: freight remains very volatile. We are supposed to supply material on DDP basis, deliver to their door of customer, and freight rates are fluctuating. So to mitigate that risk, some places we have built up a mark up or kind of freight surcharge; some customers have agreed.

items.statement: Full-year capex guidance maintained at around INR 10,000 crores
items.quote: I will still stick to INR 10,000, but it will be better to look at a full year number after the Q3 results. Plus minus INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton target of INR 1,400 by exit March 2028 reiterated
items.quote: Business as usual is what my expectation is to deliver that INR1,400. If the cost pressures come in, they will get covered by price increases. So yes, we will deliver our commitment.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA expected below 1x by end of March 2027
items.quote: March end, we were at 0.94x net debt EBITDA. We are at 1.26 x net debt EBITDA at the end of September '26. But by the end of March, I will be below 1x net debt to EBITDA.

items.statement: Industry cement demand estimated to grow close to 10% YoY; UltraTech grew 13.8% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Industry estimates put cement demand to grow closer to 10% year-on-year. Our growth of 13.8% this quarter is comfortably ahead, which means that our presence in the market is continuously increasing.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook through March 2029 driven by urban housing, infrastructure, data centres, private capex, and semiconductor industry
items.quote: I think demand is what is the strongest support for the cement industry at the moment and for period ending till March '29 we should see very strong momentum in cement consumption.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA per ton improved despite fuel cost rising from INR 45 to INR 51.5 per bag; fixed costs per ton down 6% YoY
items.quote: have risen from INR 45 a bag to INR 51.5 per bag. That is the contribution of fuel cost Y-o-Y as the fuel rates climbed to about INR 2.09 per kcal. This is the West Asia crisis effect, which we can discuss separately. Third, other fixed costs per ton were 6% lower for us than the last year, even after absorbing new capacity because absolute fixed costs grew only 4%, well below the volume growth of

items.statement: Project pipeline growing with 100 announcements worth INR 13.4 lakh crores by early September including power plants, industrial parks, data centres, metros, RRTS
items.quote: I believe there were 100 announcements worth about INR 13.4 lakh crores by ear ly September, which include Tamil Nadu's INR55,000 crores power plant, INR65,000 crores Gorakhpur Industrial Park, Assam's INR50,000 crores 5- year infra program, Odisha's Coastal Highway, Metro 1 in Thiruvananthapuram and the Bawal-Behror RRTS, power, industrial parks, data centres, all are growing and all are cement i

items.statement: Commissioned 4.6 million tons in September (3.6 Mt greenfield at Petnikota, 1 Mt debottlenecking); domestic capacity now 204.7 million tons
items.quote: We commissioned 4.6 million tons of capacity in the month of September, taking our domestic cement capacity to 204.7 million tons, which includes the 3.6 million tons greenfield capacity at Petnikota in Andhra and 1 million ton of debottlenecking at 3 other units.

items.statement: Premium cement share 37%, blended cement share 67.3% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: 37% is my premium cement and blended cement would be 67.3%.

items.statement: UltraTech growing faster than industry and delivering higher profitability consistently
items.quote: if you were to look at UltraTech's performance quarter after quarter, compare it with the rest of the industry put together on one side and UltraTech on the other side, we have consistently grown at a pace higher than the industry and delivered profitability higher than rest of the industry.

items.statement: Pet coke at $180/ton; reduced pet coke share to 25% of fuel mix; domestic coal availability constrained as Coal India prioritizes power sector; industrial diesel at all-time high
items.quote: Pet coke prices have shot through the roof. They were trading around $180 per ton as I last checked. Pet coke, what we have done is we have reduced our dependence on pet coke since the last quarter. Today, we are down to about 25% of pet coke consumption in our overall mix. Coal power plants are being required to blend imported coal. Coal India is giving priority to the power sector, which tighten

items.statement: Green power at 47% of needs; 2 GW captive green capacity; thermal substitution rate 7.2% via AFR systems at 2 plants
items.quote: During the quarter, we also added 116 megawatts of renewable power, 10 megawatt of waste heat recovery. So our green power index keeps on rising, 47% of our power needs were met from non-fossil fuel sources. We have also achieved a unique status of having 2 gigawatts of green power for captive consumption as a manufacturing sector. We have commissioned AFR systems at 2 plants, taking our thermal s

items.statement: India Cements integration: targeting major shutdowns for kiln upgrades, WHRS, preheater height increase; expects fabulous quarter in Jan-Mar 2028
items.quote: India Cement s, where we clocked INR 500 per ton in their books will get a lot of cost improvement advantage now to take us to a 4-digit mark because we will be taking major shutdowns for India Cement s kilns, for upgradation, for attaching WHRS coolers, increasing the preheater, height, etcetera, which will result into, as promised and committed into the fiscal '28 January- March '28 quarter to b

items.statement: Raised INR 5,000 crores NCDs at 7.25% in Q2; net debt/EBITDA 1.26x at September 2026
items.quote: Yes. I had raised NCDs of about INR5,000 crores at 7.25%, which were there for 2 months. So my borrowings I have taken up. I think in hindsight, it was a fantastic decision because now nobody will get the money at 7.25%.

items.statement: Board reviews dividend distribution year-on-year based on performance; no structural payout ratio commitment
items.quote: I'll let the Board decide that at the end of the year. I can't take a decision on my own. But the Board has taken a decision to keep reviewing its dividend distribution year-on-year basis the performance of the company.

items.statement: Corporate guarantee given to UHG Holdings (41% UltraTech, 9% Grasim, 50% Hindalco) for aircraft/ships deployed in group business use
items.quote: So, end use for UHG, essentially that company will be buying aircraft and ships, which will be deployed in our business use. And UltraTech is 41% holding, 9% is held by Grasim, 50% is held by Hindalco. So, that company will be borrowing money for which we have given a corporate guarantee, which helps them get finer interest rates.

items.statement: Revised FY27 guidance: credit growth 14%+, deposit growth 12%+, CASA 42%+, ROA ~1.20%, GNPA below 2%, considerable NIM improvement
items.quote: Based on the mid-term review, we have reassessed our guidance as indicated in the last call. The revised guidance for FY 2026-27 would be credit growth of 14% plus, deposit growth of 12% plus, CASA to be 42% plus. There should be a considerable improvement in NIM, ROA to be around 1.20% and GNPA to be below 2%.

items.statement: Total business grew 19.4% YoY to INR 3.10 lakh crore; deposits up 16.3%, advances up 23.7% YoY
items.quote: This resilience in the domestic economy is also reflected in the Bank's business momentum with the Bank's total business growing by 19.4% Y-o-Y to INR3.10 lakhs crores as on 30th September 2026. The Y-o-Y growth across both deposits and advances has been healthy at 16.3% and 23.7%, respectively.

items.statement: RAM loans drove all net incremental credit growth; RAM contributed >60% of net incremental credit YTD; agri up 17% YoY, auto loans >25% YoY, housing loans double-digit YoY in Rest of India
items.quote: The entire net incremental growth during the quarter has been contributed by Retail, Agriculture and MSME loans, that is RAM. And this growth has been contributed by both Jammu, Kashmir, Ladakh and Rest of India in almost equal proportions to the ir share in the Bank's outstanding RAM loans. On a YTD basis, more than 60% of the Bank's net incremental credit has been contributed by RAM portfolio

items.statement: NIM compressed to 3.22% for H1; yield on advances flat at 8.55%; cost of deposits rose to 4.85%; expect NIM improvement from Q3 as yield rises and cost of deposits moderates
items.quote: Resultantly, the NIM has witnessed compression, being recorded at 3.22% for the half year but with the expected improvement across both yield and cost, the NIM should also improve.

items.statement: Annualized gross slippage ratio 0.4% for H1; gross slippages halved YoY to INR 234 crore; GNPA 2.23%, NNPA 0.51%, PCR 91.76% as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: has witnessed a notable moderation in slippages during the current fiscal, with Annualized Gross Slippage Ratio of just 0.4% for the half year, as Gross Slippages, in terms of absolute amount, have halved compared to the corresponding period last year. This reflects the resilience of our portfolio and the continued effectiveness of our underwriting and monitoring mechanisms. The asset quality metr

items.statement: Raising INR 1,000 crore equity and INR 500 crore debt capital; debt raise in Q3 FY27, equity timing flexible; CAR 16.57%, CET1 13.88% as of Sep 30, 2026
items.value: INR 1,000 cr equity, INR 500 cr debt
items.quote: Capital Adequacy Ratio has been recorded at 16.57% as on 30th September 2026 with CET 1 of 13.88%. The Bank is already in the process of raising both equity and debt capital to the tune of INR1,000 crores and INR500 crores respectively and will raise the capital at an opportune time to support its future growth.

items.statement: Yield on advances flat at 8.55%; cost of deposits increased to 4.85% due to Q1 CASA outflow; expect cost of deposits to moderate with positive CASA inflows and lower term deposit rates
items.quote: Yield on advances has remained broadly flat on a sequential basis, being recorded at 8.55% for the quarter. However, the increasing contribution of RAM segment to our incremental credit portfolio, coupled with the recent repo rate hike, is expected to supp ort an improvement in the yield from the third quarter onwards. The sharp outflow of CASA deposits during Q1 continued to weigh on our liabilit

items.statement: CASA ratio maintained at 41.97% after Q1 outflow; positive CASA inflows in Q2; signed MOUs with 20+ organizations for salary accounts; new 5-year MOU with J&K Govt expected tomorrow; strong UPI/QR merchant monitoring
items.quote: On the deposit front also, the bank has already achieved a YTD growth of around 7% against our guidance of 10% for the financial year with the growth in Term Deposits continuing to outpace the growth in CASA in line with the continuing industry trend. However, the gap between the growth in Term Deposits and CASA Deposits has narrowed down in this quarter as the bank has been able to record positiv

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 56.57% for Q2; operating profit INR 789 crore (+27% YoY, +12% QoQ); H1 operating profit INR 1,492 crore (+15% YoY)
items.quote: As a result, Cost-to-Income Ratio of the Bank for this quarter has also moderated substantially on both sequential and Y-o-Y basis, being recorded at 56.57% for the quarter.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance 14%+ but aiming for ~18% if retail growth continues; split 60% retail, 40% corporate; NIM to improve substantially but no specific number given
items.quote: Yes. The target for the year, which we had earlier set at a lower rate, we have revised it a little bit higher now at 14%. But I said 14% plus. So my aim is to reach to around 18% provided that we continue with the retail growth.

items.statement: ROA 1.07%, ROE 13.68% for Q2; H1 ROA ~1%; targeting 1.4% ROA in H2 driven by written-off recoveries, OTS scheme, non-fund income, treasury gains, forex, cross-selling
items.quote: On the back of improved profitability, RoA has jumped by 20 bps Q-o-Q, while RoE has jumped by more than 250 bps Q-o-Q and have been recorded at 1.07% and 13.68% respectively for the quarter.

items.statement: Credit cost run rate INR 70-85 crore/quarter expected to continue; no incremental credit cost expected; SMAs declining sequentially; ECL model near ready, Board review by December; ECL hit expected below industry average; INR 300 crore buff
items.quote: No, no, I do not expect any incremental credit cost. The SMAs have been in control. Sequentially also, we have been coming down. So obviously, the concern is ECL, and we have been working in a very focused way on that

items.statement: IRDAI commission reduction to be offset by volume growth; added SBI Life and HDFC Life; J&K underinsured with high potential
items.quote: The reason why I said that we will be able to jack up our income from third-party product selling is because we have added two more insurance companies for life, that is SBI Life as well as HDFC Life. And I expect the volumes to actually compensate for the commission difference that is going to come.

items.statement: Equity raise INR 1,000 crore, debt raise INR 500 crore; debt in Q3 FY27, equity at opportune time; approvals in place, readiness complete
items.value: INR 1,000 cr equity, INR 500 cr debt
items.quote: See, there are multiple factors for which we intend to raise capital. I'm not going into that. But if you ask me the quantum, I can mention that it is going to be INR1,000 crores of equity and INR500 crores of debt. Timings, I think the debt will be this quarter. And as I mentioned that the equity will be slightly dependent on the time when it is most conducive for our bank.

items.statement: Employee cost flat to slightly down for next 2 quarters due to retirements; FY28 cost to return to current levels as new hiring begins Q3/Q4 FY27
items.quote: First of all, I expect the employee cost to remain flat, perhaps will come down slightly for the next 2 quarters. If you look at very slight, but a slight dip from quarter 1 to quarter 2. And it is going to continue because we have retirements.

items.statement: Written-off recovery INR 25 crore this quarter; substantial pipeline for next 2 years; special OTS scheme approved for old NPAs and written-off accounts; non-fund income up 30-40% QoQ
items.quote: As I mentioned -- now see this bank has had a very good past say, 8 to 10 quarters on account of recovery in written -off accounts. Now recovery in written -off accounts at the moment in pipeline, which is very, very, I would say, hot pipeline is substantial at the moment

items.statement: Treasury gain INR 92 crore includes bond portfolio and unlisted stock revaluation; INR 100 crore+ stake sale (PNB MetLife/NSE) completed after Sep 30, to reflect in Q3
items.quote: It is not yet -- the transaction is completed, but the transaction happened after 30th of September. So that is also which is going to add to the bank's profit for the next quarter. So that is not included

items.statement: High-cost bulk deposits ~INR 3,000 crore taken in Q1 at ~8%; most already shed; benefit to flow through Q3 and Q4
items.quote: See, it was in the first quarter that we took some certificate of deposits, which was slightly at a high cost, around 8%. So that was the need. At that point of time, we had loan commitments which was already there. So we -- at that point of time, it was the need. Out of that, most of it is already shed. It is no longer in the books now.

items.statement: ECL implementation model almost ready, to go to Board by December; ECL hit expected below industry average; INR 300 crore buffer held; will disclose exact range in December
items.quote: See, base figure assessment is not what I want to mention at the moment. That is why I'm not saying. Otherwise, we have a fair assessment of the ECL requirement. We are ready.

items.quote: There is a INR41 crores from card business, loan processing charges of around INR18 crores -- INR19 crores, p enal charges of INR12.89 crores, che que return charges of INR4.57 crores, SMS charges INR6.42 crores, CGTMSE fee INR4.79 crores like
