items.quote: I just mentioned that I do not want to mention a particular number for NIM. But see, 25 bps improvement has already happened on repo, and I said 65% of my portfolio is linked to repo, which is already passed on. The next is we are in the process in the bank at the moment. We had been resorting to some high-cost deposits, which we have shed now, and we are no longer required to take any high-cost d

items.statement: Full-year capex guidance maintained at around INR 10,000 crores; better to assess after Q3 results
items.quote: I will still stick to INR 10,000, but it will be better to look at a full year number after the Q3 results. Plus minus INR10,000 crores

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA expected below 1x by end of March 2027 from 1.26x at September 2026
items.quote: March end, we were at 0.94x net debt EBITDA. We are at 1.26 x net debt EBITDA at the end of September '26. But by the end of March, I will be below 1x net debt to EBITDA.

items.statement: Ultravolt wires and cables business expected to reach matured performance by fiscal 2028; April-June 2027 quarter worth talking about
items.quote: My sense is April-June 2027 will be a quarter worth talking about. Right now, let us build the business.

items.statement: Industry cement demand estimated to grow close to 10% YoY; UltraTech grew 13.8% YoY in Q2 FY27, gaining market share
items.quote: Industry estimates put cement demand to grow closer to 10% year-on-year. Our growth of 13.8% this quarter is comfortably ahead, which means that our presence in the market is continuously increasing.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook till March 2029 driven by data centres, private capex, semiconductor, urban housing, metro projects, and government infrastructure announcements
items.quote: New opportunities which are surfacing, data centres coming up in a big way, private sector capex, practically, most of the industry is expanding capacities. Semiconductor industry, that's a new animal on the block, which is rising in a big way.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 net profit up 21% YoY; operating leverage benefited from 13.8% volume growth vs 4% fixed cost growth; fixed cost per ton down 6% YoY
items.quote: Despite increase in cost, the company has achieved an improvement in operating performance, higher capacity utilization on a higher base, higher or stable realizations, improvement in efficiency and a 21% increase in net profit.

items.statement: Fuel cost per bag rose from INR 45 to INR 51.5 QoQ (INR 6/bag impact); kcal cost increased to INR 2.09, now around INR 2.2; expect marginal impact in Q3, more in Q4
items.quote: Fuel costs have risen from INR 45 a bag to INR 51.5 per bag. That is the contribution of fuel cost Y-o-Y as the fuel rates climbed to about INR 2.09 per kcal.

items.statement: Operating leverage advantage to kick in next quarter; fixed cost per ton to benefit as volumes remain strong
items.quote: Yes, please. The operating leverage advantage will kick in.

items.statement: Pan-India trade prices stable QoQ in Q2, down 1-1.5% due to soft August; exited September 3% above Q1 average; prices rose 7-10/bag MoM in late September; October prices up substantially, 5% above Q2 average; further increases expected in n
items.quote: Prices fo r your benefit have risen substantially in the month of October and continue to stay high. My sense is that there is more price improvement that will happen in the near future, in the next couple of months, that is to say

items.statement: South region strongest momentum in prices, volumes and utilization; West (Mumbai) up 3-4%/bag in September; North steady; Central muted; East disrupted by rains but catching up from October
items.quote: South have been the strongest momentum in prices, volume and capacity utilization. South markets are transforming. Mark my words.

items.statement: Commissioned 4.6 million tons in September (3.6 Mt greenfield at Petnikota, Andhra + 1 Mt debottlenecking); domestic capacity now 204.7 million tons; North and South utilization >70%, West ~70%, Central and East ~60% due to monsoon
items.quote: We commissioned 4.6 million tons of capacity in the month of September, taking our domestic cement capacity to 204.7 million tons, which includes the 3.6 million tons greenfield capacity at Petnikota in Andhra and 1 million ton of debottlenecking at 3 other units.

items.statement: Next phase of organic growth beyond 240 million tons to be announced before end of FY27; North region a focus for incremental expansion
items.quote: We will come with our detailed plans before the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Premium cement share 37%; blended cement share 67.3% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: 37% is my premium cement and blended cement would be 67.3%.

items.statement: Ultravolt launched unique products (Class 5 insulation, e-beam technology) commanding premium; positioning at market parity with differentiation via product proposition
items.quote: we have launched unique products, which were not existing in the marketplace. T he classic is Class 5 insulation material or e-beam technology product. That nobody has. And that product is what is commanding a premium

items.statement: UBS network contributes >25% of trade sales; 6,500 stores currently, targeting 10,000 stores by FY28-29; Ultravolt signed up 1,500+ UBS channel partners, retail reach 80,000+ points
items.quote: It's a phenomenal number, more than 25% of trade sales is through UBS network.

items.statement: Pet coke at $180/ton (all-time high); reduced pet coke share to 25% of fuel mix; domestic coal availability constrained as Coal India prioritizes power sector; industrial diesel at all-time high impacting mining/transport costs
items.quote: Pet coke prices have shot through the roof. They were trading around $180 per ton as I last checked. Pet coke, what we have done is we have reduced our dependence on pet coke since the last quarter. Today, we are down to about 25% of pet coke consumption in our overall mix.

items.statement: Green power index rising: 47% of power from non-fossil sources; 2 GW green power for captive use; AFR systems at 2 plants, thermal substitution rate 7.2%
items.quote: 47% of our power needs were met from non-fossil fuel sources. We have also achieved a unique status of having 2 gigawatts of green power for captive consumption as a manufacturing sector.

items.statement: Corporate guarantee given to UHG Holdings (41% UltraTech, 9% Grasim, 50% Hindalco) for aircraft/ships purchase for group business use; helps obtain finer interest rates
items.quote: End use for UHG, essentially that company will be buying aircraft and ships, which will be deployed in our business use. And UltraTech is 41% holding, 9% is held by Grasim, 50% is held by Hindalco.

items.statement: India Cements integration: targeting 4-digit EBITDA per ton by Jan-Mar 2028 quarter via kiln shutdowns, WHRS coolers, preheater upgrades; currently at INR 500/ton
items.quote: India Cement s, where we clocked INR 500 per ton in their books will get a lot of cost improvement advantage now to take us to a 4-digit mark because we will be taking major shutdowns for India Cement s kilns

items.statement: Capacity utilization 71% in Q2 FY27 vs 66% YoY on higher base; could have sold more if capacity available
items.quote: Our capacity utilization was 71%, better than 66% last year on a higher base. We could have grown more. We could have sold more cement if additional capacity was available.

items.statement: West Asia crisis keeps fuel costs elevated (pet coke $180/ton); indirect risks: higher inflation, tighter monetary conditions, less fiscal room; no direct demand impact yet
items.quote: The indirect risks are higher inflation, tighter monetary conditions and less fiscal room if fuel does not come down in terms of costs. We are watching all the 3 elements.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu levy of INR 160/ton on India Cements already accounted for in Q2; no reversal or additional cost going forward
items.quote: It's already accounted for. There's no reversal in that.

items.statement: Medium-to-long-term AUM growth target of 16% to 18%
items.quote: I'm not changing our posture from a 16% to 18% medium to long-term AUM growth. That remains kind of pretty constant.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 1.3% to 1.7%
items.quote: We have given a zip code of 1.3 to 1.7 on credit cost. I do not see any near-term to long-term challenge to that front.

items.statement: ROA aspiration of 2.2% to 2.5% in medium term
items.quote: Our aspiration is to move as a franchise to a 2.2 to 2.5 ROA.

items.statement: GS2+GS3 at all-time low of 8.1% with sequential improvement
items.quote: Looking at asset quality, 8.1% GS2+GS3, this is pretty much all-time lows in terms of our GS2+GS3 numbers.

items.statement: Sequential fall in GS3 by 3 bps and GS2 by 7 bps in Q2
items.value: 3 bps GS3 decrease, 7 bps GS2 decrease
items.quote: We, in fact, saw sequential fall in GS3 by 3 bps, as well as GS2 which was a 7 bps decrease.

items.statement: Credit cost at 1.6% in Q2, within guided range
items.quote: And the credit cost has been within the zip codes that we've called out between 1.3 to 1.7. Our Q2 credit cost at 1.6%.

items.statement: Proactive collection augmentation in 282 drought-affected districts
items.quote: What we have done proactively is collection, augmenting collection in these locations. So, we do have our own collection as well as we lean on some collection infrastructure as and when required.

items.statement: Reduced funding in stressed drought-affected locations in Q2
items.quote: Proactively again in Q2, we have reduced some of the funding in some of these locations which are stressed.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to under 37% from above 40%
items.quote: I also must point out our cost-to-income, which was earlier above 40%, has now slid to under 37%.

items.statement: NIM challenged by rising cost of funds and fixed-rate book; loan income compressed by liquidity buffer and trade advance
items.quote: We will have to find mechanisms to grow the revenue pie while the CoF clearly sees a incremental trend.

items.statement: Cost of funds on upward trajectory due to rate hikes; 25 bps hike translates to ~10 bps repricing of floating book per quarter
items.value: ~10 bps per quarter on floating book
items.quote: 25 basis points if it's implemented on the floating book, I think this leads to almost 10 basis points of existing stock getting repriced within, you can say, reset frequency within a quarter.

items.statement: Incremental wheels loans to be priced higher; non-wheels floating book allows faster transmission
items.quote: At least the incremental assets that we book will come in at a higher rate. So, in this environment, we have to be responsible, pass on what we can, and as well as price in what we can.

items.statement: Liquidity buffer doubled year-on-year; management erring on side of caution
items.quote: Our liquidity buffer is pretty much doubled from last year, if you see in rupee value terms. We have very clearly erred on the side of being extra cautious in terms of liquidity buffers.

items.statement: Liquidity buffer dynamic; may reduce if environment improves
items.quote: if we see t he clouds thin out, Mahindra & we will clearly, we are sitting on a very high level and that can give us some gains if we don't see it increasing from here on for sure, the liquidity buffer, we do see possibly, optionalities of a reduction

items.statement: AUM grew 15% YoY to INR 1,56,000 crores; non-wheels share at 20%
items.quote: Overall lending AUM, which is at INR 1,56,000 crores now you have a 20% coming in from the non-wheels and 80% from the wheels.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 22% YoY; holistic growth across all asset categories
items.quote: Our disbursement growth has grown in a steady clip of 22%. And this 22% growth has come in from clearly our core business which is the wheels business as well as growth coming from the diversification agenda.

items.statement: Non-wheels lending business grew 52% YoY; core wheels grew 21%
items.quote: The core business grew 21% and the non-wheels business at 52% is a healthy sign in that direction.

items.statement: Trade advance elevated at 2.9% of AUM vs 2.3% last year to support festive growth
items.quote: The quantum of trade advance that we have deployed this year is clearly a clip above the normal.

items.statement: Growth across all vehicle segments: PV 28%, used 15%, CV/CE 16%, tractor 13%, 3W 32%, SME 13%, others 71%
items.quote: We have, actually the wheels business firing on all cylinders, passenger vehicle at 28%, used business at 15%, CV/CE at 16%, tractor at 13%, three-wheeler at 32%, SME at 13%, and our other businesses at 71%.

items.statement: Prime housing launched in August; early days but will be called out separately going forward
items.quote: What you will see also build up there, which I will carve out separately is our prime housing, which we started doing in August.

items.statement: AI-orchestrated disbursements at INR 1,663 crores; 75% back office covered by AI workflows; 12 regional vernacular bots in collections
items.quote: Glad to report that if you see the sequential swap-in benefits of the AI toolkits, it is adding material value to our disbursements, which are now 1,663 crores. On the operations front, 75% of our back office is now fully covered by enabled operation workflows.

items.statement: Headcount increase driven by growth plans in wheels, SME, mortgage; off-roll to on-roll migration for consistent performers
items.quote: With our renewed growth plans now, as you see, one of our core pillars are pivoting back to growth. Growth in the wheels business, growth in the SME business, growth in the mortgage business will require headcount.

items.statement: MRHFL merger with parent NBFC targeted for June-July 2025; appointed date April 1, 2027; lenders' approval received
items.quote: We are looking at a June, June of next fiscal as a possible end, end goal. But we will keep, keep stakeholders informed of, if any minor milestones in between come under any pressure.

items.statement: Insurance consultation paper could materially impact fee income; representations underway; too early to quantify
items.quote: The recent one being in terms of the new consulta tion paper on insurance. While it's early days, it can have a material impact if it is implemented suo moto as is. But we have been representing, and we also know that there are certain representations underway

items.statement: Monitoring drought in 3 states and 282 districts; tractor collections half-yearly; early days to assess impact
items.quote: We are also very carefully watching how the drought-related scenarios in the 3 states and the 282 districts are playing out. Our tractor business is very closely tied to the local economy.

items.statement: Festive season commerce lower than last year; tractor seeing more decline; rural growth still stronger than urban in H1
items.quote: I do want to kind of be, you know, the commerce is not as great as last year same time. We have seen some amount of departure from that.

items.statement: H1 consolidated ROA at 2.3%; PAT grew 68%
items.quote: As a franchise, our ROA is at a 2.3% and our PAT has grown 68%.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 18% with 16.2% Tier 1; well capitalized for growth
items.quote: From a capital adequacy standpoint, being a nearly fully secured underlying assets, at 18% capital adequacy with 16.2% Tier 1, we are very fairly decently capitalized for the next phase of growth.

items.statement: Bank borrowings 51% of liabilities; floating rate borrowings 45-48% mostly repo/T-bill linked; MCLR-linked borrowings lesser
items.quote: Generally, we don't give this breakup . B ut if you look at the floating rate which we have disclosed at around 45 % to 48%, I would say, largely it's linked to the repo and the treasury bills, and MCLR-linked borrowings are

items.statement: Priority sector lending assets (tractor, CV) used for securitization/on-lending to manage cost of funds
items.quote: We are one of the biggest suppliers of priority sector agri, considering the amount of loans that we have in underlying PSL assets, which is tractor, as well as CV, etc. So, we're able to even today offload a lot of those assets through co-lending, sorry, through on-lending, through securitization, etc.

items.statement: Growth plan to be presented in Q4 FY27; internal accruals to remain primary funding source
items.quote: We therefore intend to present our growth plan in Quarter 4 '27.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR278 crores; full-year remaining spend ~INR500 crores
items.quote: Capex during the first half was INR278 crores, of which about INR141 crores was spent in quarter 2, all funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Capex program INR3,000 crores; INR650 crores spent to date; FY27 balance ~INR500 crores
items.quote: The remaining balance, the balance amount to be spent during the year is around 500 crores. Out of that, INR400 crores is for Gorakhpur plant. INR 240 crores is planned for mines, approximately INR 170 crores are planned for solar projects and INR100 crores is planned for Kutch.

items.statement: Gorakhpur expansion to 1.23 mtpa operational by November 2026; ramp to 85-90% utilization by December 2026
items.quote: The enhanced Gorakhpur capacity is expected to be operational in November '26.

items.statement: Kutch rolling mill utilization 68% in Q2 FY27 vs 66% in Q1 FY27; structural improvement expected in H2
items.quote: At Kutch, rolling mill utilization, which we identified as a focus area in the last quarter, was 68% in Quarter 2, compared with 66% in Quarter 1.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 9.64% vs 16.19% Q1 FY27; compression from shutdowns and input costs
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR111 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 9.64%, compared with the INR185 crores and 16.19% in Q1 FY27, and INR135 crores and 12.91% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Captive iron ore mines targeted FY28 operational; expected INR2,000/ton EBITDA uplift once fully ramped
items.quote: Over the medium term, solar, the Gujarat debottlenecking, and captive mines, which we expect to add about INR2,000 per ton to EBITDA once operational, will lift our margins structurally.

items.statement: Solar plants (18 MW Siddhpur by Nov 2026, 60 MW Prayagraj by Q4 FY27) to save INR30-40 crores annually
items.quote: Together, these are expected to save INR30 to INR40 crores annually in power cost.

items.statement: Coal block awarded in Singrauli Aug 2026; due diligence ongoing; 2-3 years to operationalize; aims to replace imported coal at Gorakhpur
items.quote: Gallantt was awarded a coal block in Singrauli in August 2026, as disclosed to the exchanges. Together with our iron ore blocks in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, this means Gallantt now holds both of the key raw materials for steel making.

items.statement: Iron ore blocks exploration progressing; environment/forest clearances underway; FY28 target operational
items.quote: At the iron ore blocks, exploration is progressing, and the environment and forest clearances processes are underway. And FY28 remained our target for them to become operational.

items.statement: TMT prices up ~21% YoY in Sep 2026; coal cost impact ~INR2,500/ton; iron ore cost impact ~1%
items.quote: TMT prices in September were about 21% higher than a year ago.

items.statement: Coal price increase affected raw material cost by 4.5-5% of sales revenue (~INR2,500/ton); iron ore up 1% (~INR3,000/ton total raw material increase)
items.quote: So, if we say 5%, it's around INR2,500 per ton on the TMT prices. And there has been a 1% price increase on the iron ore front also. So, all put together, it's about INR3,000 a ton of price increase that we have seen in Q2 in the raw material side.

items.statement: Domestic finished steel consumption grew 7.5% YoY to ~85 mt in H1 FY27; construction season pickup expected
items.quote: Finished steel consumption in India grew 7.5% to about 85 million tons, ahead of growth in domestic production, even as the country remained a net importer of finished steel.

items.statement: Brand premium 5-6% in UP, 3-4% in Gujarat vs unbranded TMT; held via branding (Ajay Devgn, Janhvi Kapoor) and dealer network
items.quote: And if I talk about UP, we broadly command about 5% to 6% premium compared to any unbranded TMT which is coming in the market. And in Gujarat also, we command about 3% to 4% premium.

items.statement: Inventory rose INR118 crores in H1 FY27 due to shutdowns and stocking for new capacity; expected to normalize in Q3 FY27
items.quote: It increased basically due to two reasons. One is due to planned and unplanned shutdown in the unit for hookup of the new capacities being added, which got prolonged. And the second is that since we are adding these new capacities, we have increased the stocks at the plant to suffice the added capacities. So, in Q3, it would normalize automatically once this plant is operational within the next 15

items.statement: Net cash positive as of Sep 2026: borrowings INR592 crores (working capital only), cash & liquid INR426 crores + treasury INR266 crores; no term loans for projects
items.quote: Borrowings were INR592 crores, mostly working capital facilities, and we continue to carry no term loan for our project. Against this, we held about INR426 crores in bank balances and liquid investments, along with INR266 crores in short-term treasury deployment, so we remains net cash positive.

items.statement: Final dividend INR2/share for FY26 approved at AGM Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: Shareholders approved a final dividend of INR2 per share for financial year 2026 at the AGM held on 30th September 2026.

items.statement: EBITDA/ton Q2 FY27 INR6,150 vs INR8,010 Q1 FY27; decline from shutdowns and input costs
items.quote: EBITDA per ton was INR6,150, against INR8,010 in the previous quarter.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue INR2,292 crores (+7% YoY); EBITDA INR296 crores (12.91% margin) vs INR382 crores (17.85%) H1 FY26
items.quote: For the first half, revenue from operation grew 7% to INR2,292 crores, compared with INR2,141 crores in H1 FY26. EBITDA was INR296 crores, with a margin of 12.91%, compared with INR382 crores and 17.85% a year earlier.

items.statement: Growth plan depends on land acquisition and state incentives; timeline uncertain
items.quote: A project of this nature depends on land acquisition and incentives from the state government, and we are working on that.

items.statement: Digital/AI initiatives: vendor management, compliance portals, weighbridge integration with SAP to plug leakages; hard to quantify savings
items.quote: We have taken up a lot of initiatives in digitization, where broadly we are working on the plugging of the leakages, if at all they were happening. So, while it is difficult to quantify, there's a lot of activity in IT where in the current year, we have integrated multiple tools with our SAP.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 25% to 40% year-on-year
items.quote: Based on our assessment of market condition, real estate activity, infrastructure development, and progress of our operations, we continue to expect year-on-year revenue growth in the range of 25% to 40%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target around 18% and PAT margin approximately 10%
items.quote: We also remain focused on sustaining EBITDA margin at around 18% and maintaining a PAT margin of approximate 10%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 18.35% from 17.03% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 18.35% from 17.03%, representing the expansion of 132 basis points.

items.statement: H1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 16.85% from 16.62% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 16.85% to 16.62%, an expansion of 23 basis points.

items.statement: UAE order book reached approximately AED78 million in September 2026 with 6-9 months visibility
items.quote: Our UAE order book reached approximately AED78 million in September 2026, providing visibility for execution over the following 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: India order book around INR85 crores with 6-8 month execution timeline
items.quote: It is around INR85 crores.

items.statement: UAE tempering third line and fire-rated glass capex around AED20 million funded 60% internal accruals, 40% bank finance
items.quote: So, the tempering third line and the fire-rated and the other facilities to be required to make this operation is around in the range of AED20 million of our total investment in terms of capex.

items.statement: Taloja tempering utilization improved from 55% to 69%, IG glass from 24% to 40% QoQ
items.quote: On the product side, has been improved, from last quarter, it was 55% on tempering in Taloja, now it is 69%. On IG glass, it was 24%, now it is almost 40% in Taloja.

items.statement: Erode tempering utilization improved from 13% to over 24%, IG glass from under 5% to over 18% QoQ
items.quote: Similarly, in Erode, the utilization of tempering line was 13%, now it is more than 24%. And on IG glass, it was less than 5% in last quarter, now it is more than 18%.

items.statement: Peak utilization targets: tempering near 100%, IG and laminate over 85%
items.quote: More than 85% in IG laminates and tempering. Because tempering, in a way, the product is also used for the production of IG and laminate. So our tempering capacity should be utilized near to 100%, and our IG and laminate glass should be more than 80%, 85% on a peak level.

items.statement: Value-added products (fire-rated, bulletproof, railway-grade, digital printed) expected 5% of FY27 revenue, 15-20% in FY28
items.quote: We are expecting 5% in this year from the value-added products and next year 15% or 20%.

items.statement: Fire-rated glass trial production in Q3 FY27, commercial production targeted end of Q3 FY27
items.quote: The manufacturing line and associate technology has been imported and are being installed at our factory facility, with the trial production and approval progress towards the commercial production targeted to end of Q3 FY27.

items.statement: UAE facade division contributed to Q2 EBITDA; India expanding to Bangalore, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Gujarat projects
items.quote: And the another factor is the facade division in UAE, which has also contributed in this quarter in the EBITDA.

items.statement: UAE works on PDC terms, 25% on LC; India inventory blockage due to coated glass advance purchases
items.quote: Working capital, as the UAE market is more on the credit, so there the PDC concept still exists. Everything works on the PDC. But we are the company who is insisting on a LC terms, so our 25% business is still from the LC, where we get the LC from the customer and we get it discount to improve our working capital cycle.

items.statement: Long-term bank debt paid on EMI schedule; no prepayment plans currently
items.quote: As of now, the debts are more of like long-term debts from the banks, which are being paid on EMI system regularly. So right now, as such, nothing on that front to reduce debt or making a prepayments to the bankers.

items.statement: UAE COGS improved 3% due to product mix change, better vendor negotiation, efficiency gains
items.quote: Secondly, efficiency improvement in our Dubai operations that where the COGS has been improved to 3%.

items.statement: India real estate and infrastructure development driving demand for architectural glass
items.quote: Considering the potential in India real estate infrastructure development of high-rise residential and commercial projects, so that will definitely add up the revenue in our sales and the capacity utilization.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Middle East increased logistics and input costs but passed on to customers
items.quote: As of now, yes, we are doing well in spite of these geopolitical tensions over there. Of course, there is an increase in cost of some of the things because of logistic cost as shipment cost has been increased. So, input cost to certain extent has been increased, but which we are still passing on to the end users and the customers.

items.statement: Expect to reach INR600-650 crores peak revenue from existing infrastructure by FY28
items.quote: I think so we'll be able to reach in '28.

items.statement: Fire-rated glass expected EBITDA margins over 30% as value-added product
items.quote: Margins will be definitely more in terms of EBITDA, it is more than 30%, because it is a very value-added product.

items.statement: Fire-rated glass market size estimated above INR500 crores including India and UAE
items.quote: Market size, it is as of now, it is difficult to say. Approximately our understanding is above 500 crores, including India and UAE.

items.statement: UAE operating at ~90% IG glass capacity; third tempering line coming online in Q3 FY27
items.quote: As you rightly said that UAE, yes, definitely, we are working about 90% in capacity in terms of IG glass. And second line, we are also expanding in tempering capacities, which is coming in the quarter three.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated total income INR139.86 crores, up 33.14% YoY
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, total income stood at INR139.86 crores compared with INR105.04 crores in Q2 of FY26, registering a year-on-year growth of 33.14%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 consolidated total income INR259.29 crores, up 41.84% YoY
items.quote: For the first half of FY27, consolidated total income reached to INR259.29 crores compared to INR182.81 crores in H1 of '26, reflecting a growth of 41.84%.

items.statement: Full-year bookings guidance of INR40,000 crores; H2 bookings estimate INR22,500-25,000 crores; H2 collections target INR15,000 crores; H2 operating cash flow target INR7,000 crores; FY28 positive free cash flow and 20% reported ROE
items.quote: We only launched 1/3 of our expected annual launch pipeline in the first half of the financial year, and we're still able to deliver 43% of our annual bookings guidance, highlighting the continued strength of underlying demand in the sector.

items.statement: H2 FY27 bookings estimate INR22,500-25,000 crores; H2 collections target INR15,000 crores; H2 operating cash flow target INR7,000 crores
items.quote: We are especially focused on generating strong cash flows and expect INR15,000 crores of cash collection and INR7,000 crores of operating cash flow in the second half of the financial year.

items.statement: FY28 guidance: positive free cash flow and 20% reported ROE

Bangalore, we did just under INR1,600 crores, about INR1,000 crores in Pune, INR700-odd crores in Hyderabad and another INR800 crores in other cities during the quarter.

items.statement: 7th consecutive quarter with >INR7,000 crores booking value; 13th consecutive quarter with >INR5,000 crores booking value

items.statement: Delivered 2.5 msf in Q2; on track for 13.5 msf full-year delivery
items.quote: GPL delivered projects aggregating 2.5 million square feet in the quarter, and we remain on track for 13.5 million square feet of delivery in the full year.

items.statement: Q2 total income +38% to INR2,575 crores; EBITDA -72% to INR171 crores; net profit -62% to INR154 crores; H1 total income +13% to INR3,912 crores; EBITDA -53% to INR717 crores; net profit -50% to INR504 crores; decline due to back-ended deli

items.quote: So that's how the line-by-line consolidation happened, whereby bulk of the profits were already accounted for in the past. And that's why you see that cuteness whereby the sales and cost of sales are almost equal because the bulk of the profit was accounted in the earlier days.

items.statement: Prices holding up; North markets <1% price increase; South and Mumbai ~2% increase; rest ~0.5%; Noida Godrej Crown Residences saw massive price jump tripling cluster profit, 88% sold out
items.quote: Generally, we've not pushed pricing high in North markets, and we focused more on end user sales so that the quality of sale is higher. So it's like less than 1% price increase in some projects across South and Mumbai have seen most projects seeing 2% sort of a jump in price and again, 0.5% or so in rest of the portfolio.

items.statement: Focus on end-user sales for quality; sales team restructuring for sustenance focus; launch vs sustenance mix historically 60-40 but can flip based on approvals
items.quote: I mean time -- I mean, this has been the historical trend, right, that we've been at 60-40 sort of a mix of it. But I think the way probably I would sort of emphasize is that from an annual guidance perspective, you can almost assume that we would always continue to achieve that.

items.statement: Q2 collections +31% YoY to INR5,318 crores; H1 collections +25% to INR9,666 crores; Q2 operating cash flow +300% QoQ and +33% YoY to INR1,584 crores; H1 operating cash flow INR1,983 crores
items.quote: Godrej Properties also reached its highest ever second quarter and first half collection with collections growing by 31% in the quarter to INR5,318 crores and by 25% in the first half to INR9,666 crores.

items.statement: H2 FY27 collection target INR15,000 crores; operating cash flow target INR7,000 crores; expect free cash flow positive in H2 and Q4
items.quote: We are especially focused on generating strong cash flows and expect INR15,000 crores of cash collection and INR7,000 crores of operating cash flow in the second half of the financial year. This will allow us to both invest for continued growth while also being free cash flow positive for this period.

items.quote: During the last quarter, we added 1 new project with an estimated saleable area of approximately 1.1 million square feet and expected booking value of about INR6,000 crores. With this, GPL has added four projects with an estimated salable area of about 9 million square feet. And an expected booking value of about INR15,500 crores in the first half of the financial year, which has gotten us to abou

items.statement: Exiting 5-6 remaining JVs naturally as projects end; moving toward 100% owned portfolio; Orris settlement completed; Mahalunge JV exited in Q1 FY26
items.quote: So Puneet, Orris was a case where the partner has invoked arbitration. So like I said, there will be certain JVs, which we will be exiting. like in the past, apart from Orris, we exited a JV in Mahalunge, so there will be -- there are some more few JVs, 5, 6 JVs still left. Those will see the exit, not necessarily getting into a dispute and exit, but definitely by naturally a project coming to an

items.statement: BD focus markets: Bangalore, Mumbai (South, Western suburbs, Thane), Noida, Gurugram (Golf Course Extension, SPR); opportunistic in Kolkata, Ahmedabad; Chennai likely next group housing market but not priority for next 2 years
items.quote: So I would say the opportunities are quite massive, Pritesh. And the good thing for us is that because we are pan-India, they can almost pick and choose where we feel the valuations are sort of very exciting and where the inventory added can be equally or faster moving than that.

items.statement: NCR GRAP/NGT bans do not restrict launches; marketing office/sample apartment restrictions mitigated as already ready; construction schedules factor historical adverse periods
items.quote: I think from a launch perspective, there's never been any restrictions in even the worst of times in NCR. So that's sort of always been mitigated. Of course, if you do a MOSA as we call it marketing office sample apartment experience center, those can get prohibited. But fortunately, we had already planned for them and those are fully ready.

items.statement: Macro risks (oil at $115, equity markets) not changing sales playbook; product-market fit and process rigor drive consistent growth; sustenance sales 83% YoY growth proves market supportive
items.quote: If you see what was very exciting for us is that we took the challenge of driving high quality of sales in the most difficult bucket, which is sustenance and that was at 83% Y-on-Y growth. This is clearly reflecting that the market is supportive, provided you have the right strategy and you have the right product mix to deliver on the promise that customers expect from you.

items.statement: Market share ~5% of industry; industry size INR9-10 lakh crores; target 15-20% presales growth in FY28 to ~INR50,000 crores; 40% 5-year CAGR in bookings if top-end guidance met

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance 13-14%, advances growth 18-20%, CD ratio around 82% over next two quarters
items.quote: Going forward, as per our guidance, we expect deposits to grow at between 13% to 14% and advances to grow at 18% to 20 %. So overall we expect that the CD ratio will be around 82 % over the next two quarters.

items.statement: RAM advances target 65% by March 2027 and 70% by March 2028
items.quote: As we have said earlier, our guidance is that the RAM advances percentage could be around 65% for the current year, and we will take it up to 70% by March 2028 (FY 2027-28).

items.statement: Gross NPA below 2% by March 2027, Net NPA guidance 0.65%, recovery and upgradation Rs.1,000 crore+
items.quote: We continue to expect the gross NPA to be below 2% by the end of March. Net NPA, we have given a guidance of 0.65%, we are already at 0.61%. We’ll now continue to reduce it further. On recovery and upgradation, we have given a guidance of Rs.1,000 crores

items.statement: Business target Rs.3 lakh crore by end FY27 and Rs.4 lakh crore by end FY29
items.quote: The bank is in the pivot of now reaching a Rs.3 lakh crore business by the end of this financial year and Rs.4 lakh crore by the end of FY '29.

items.statement: Corporate credit pipeline ~Rs.20,000 cr (Rs.12,000 cr pipeline + Rs.8,000-9,000 cr in-principle sanctions)
items.quote: On the corporate credit side, we already have a pipeline of around Rs.12,000 crores, and in-principle sanctions of around Rs.8,000 crores to Rs.9,000 crores. So overall around Rs.20,000 crores of pipeline we have already created.

items.statement: Branch expansion targeting 300 potential centres in top 200 districts; recruiting at LBO, PO, CSA levels
items.quote: We have identified the top 200 districts which account for 80% of the country's banking business . We are expanding them to those areas where we are not present so far. We have already found out 300 potential centres. The branches will get opened as the premises get finalized, as we appoint more and more workforce at various levels.

items.statement: Capital raise planned via QIP; approvals and merchant bankers in place; awaiting right market opportunity
items.quote: We have the necessary approvals for capital raising, and we have already interacted with investors. We have appointed merchant bankers for the same and we would just like the right opportunity to go to the market and raise some funds. So, we are exploring all the avenues to raise capital, primarily through the QIP route.

items.statement: TWO book Rs.7,344 cr; recovering ~10% annually (Rs.247.88 cr so far this year)
items.quote: We continue to hold almost Rs.7,344 crores of TWO book and if you look at the results over last few years, we have been recovering around approximately 10% of the book. This year also, so far the recovery has been almost Rs.250 crores, to be precise Rs.247.88 crores.

items.statement: ROA 0.88%, ROE 13.21%, cost-to-income ratio marginally declined
items.quote: Return on assets has increased to 0.88% and return on equity has also increased to 13.21%. The cost-to-income ratio has also marginally declined in Q2.

items.statement: GIFT City branch expected live by November end; forex trade module to kick in during Q3
items.quote: our GIFT City branch is now just around the corner . It should be live and kicking 4 around November end. We are also more or less ready with the forex trade module, which should kick-in during this

items.statement: Digital journey since Nov 4, 2024: ~40,000 proposals sourced digitally worth ~Rs.8,000 cr; sanction rates 50% vehicle, 40% home loans
items.quote: Since the inception of our digital journey, from 4th of November 2024, we have sourced approximately 40,000 proposals digitally to a tune of approximately Rs.8,000 crore & the sanction rate is really wonderful. It's around 50% in vehicle loan and 40% in home loans.

items.quote: We are, of course, awaiting for the SIF clearance to come in from SEBI. Once we get that, of course, we'll be in the market to launch our ideas.

items.quote: For H1 FY27, Operating Profit grew by 28% YoY, Profit After Tax grew by 12% YoY.

items.quote: Yes, market volatility does impact the investor sentiment. We are seeing now HNI investors slowly taking exits from large -caps.

items.quote: The reasons for offshore AUM overall has been that because owing to, the rupee depreciation for the last one year or so, there has been decline in flows from FPIs into India.

items.quote: We are looking overall for a 100 bps improvement in our gross margin, and we stay committed to that.

items.quote: We are now pivoting this business from a no-loss strategy to a pivot towards growth, and we are feeling more excited and more confident about this business.

items.quote: In the last-mile delivery business, our revenue for Q2 is INR68 crores, compared to INR88 crores in Q2 F '2 6, down by 23% as part of our conscious choice to move towards a more profitable portfolio.

items.quote: Mostly in contract logistics, we have put capex and also in our 2x2 joint venture where we do car carriers for our auto and tractor business for Mahindra, we have added capex. So, mostly on contract logistics and 2x2.

items.statement: Contract logistics shifting mix toward warehousing over transportation for better margins
items.quote: We are trying to improve more warehousing compared to transportation, because warehousing has bet ter margin than transportation.

Apart from that, there was a big issue last quarter on the manpower cost, which is still playing out. That has not been passed o ut fully.

items.statement: Domestic market supportive with lower dimer acid imports improving realizations and margins

items.statement: US exports delayed due to high freight costs; Europe cosmetic demand slowing due to economic issues

items.statement: New novel technology product (fatty acid derivative) expected to launch in Q3 FY27 after Diwali, import substitution with export potential
items.quote: As you know, we have put up a small capacity plant and which we expect to commence in October-December quarter. After Diwali, we expect it to start.

items.statement: Chinese dumping reduced due to export incentive cuts; rupee depreciation also helped

items.statement: Working capital cycle 90-100 days for domestic sales, higher for exports; expected to remain at current levels

items.statement: No current plan to reduce debt; operating cash flow utilization to be decided after business stabilizes at higher levels
items.quote: So, once the business stabilizes at higher levels, we would think appropriately to utilize to the best interest of shareholders.

items.statement: Realization improved to Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27 from Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26
items.quote: So, Quarter 2, the realization was Rs. 135 a kg, which was around Rs. 130 a kg in Q1 FY27. And in Q2 FY26, it was Rs. 106.

items.statement: Government unlikely to raise import duties again due to high inflation and farmer MSP support
items.quote: Currently, inflation is very high. We believe that government will not take any risk to increase the basic increase in oil rates.

items.statement: Middle East crisis and global macro uncertainties remain; Europe cosmetic demand slowing; US freight costs high
items.quote: we remain mindful of uncertainties arising from the ongoing Middle East crisis and broader global macroeconomic environment

items.statement: Food delivery margins expected to remain flattish over next 1-2 years
items.quote: Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards. That's what the operating principle is. It's hard to project or comment on margin trajectory every quarter but broadly, over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish.

items.statement: $1 billion Adjusted EBITDA guidance for FY29 maintained

items.statement: Steady state NOV per day per store could reach INR 11 lakh

items.statement: Blinkit store capex guidance of INR 2.5 crore is blended number accounting for tier 2 expansion
items.quote: That's a blended number, Abhisek. That guidance was given keeping in mind that a large part of our expansion will happen in Tier 2 cities.

items.statement: Bulk of new Blinkit store expansion will be in smaller cities (tier 2/3)
items.quote: Directionally, we've also mentioned in the letter that the bulk of the expansion of these new stores will be in smaller cities. items.statement: Plan to nearly double dark stores over next 6-7 quarters

items.statement: Competitive intensity in food delivery higher in Q2 vs previous quarters, partly driven by Zomato
items.quote: Generally, the competitive intensity last quarter in food delivery was higher compared to the previous few quarters, and partly also driven by Zomato.

items.statement: Food delivery investing aggressively in growth across new customer acquisition and frequency
items.quote: In both new customer acquisition as well as in driving frequency of our existing customer base, we have increased the amount of investments we have done consistently over the last few quarters, and that trend is likely to continue.

items.statement: Blinkit mature cities still growing rapidly, MTU multiple times Zomato's in those cities
items.quote: For example, in our mature cities, Blinkit MTU is already multiple times that of Zomato, and we don't see any plateau there yet. We don't want to speculate on how large the top markets can be but suffice to say that whether you look at NOV growth or MTU growth, the larger markets are still growing at a very rapid pace.

items.statement: Food delivery strategy prioritizes absolute Adjusted EBITDA growth over percentage margins
items.quote: We feel that we can drive more growth in absolute Adjusted EBITDA by investing more in growth rather than optimizing for margins. We've been doing that consistently for a few quarters now, and we will continue on that path until we see the outcomes.

items.statement: Blinkit indirect costs growing 15-20% QoQ, partly variable (tech server costs) and FX-impacted
items.quote: For example, technology server costs are below contribution. So, as the business scales, those costs will go up. And some of those costs are priced in dollars, so the exchange rate also doesn't help there.

items.statement: Blinkit Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion driven by operating leverage during expansion phase
items.quote: Broadly, what we should look at is the overall Adjusted EBITDA margin, and a lot of the improvement we see there is on account of operating leverage. Till the time we continue expanding, that is what will drive most of the margin expansion.

items.statement: Blinkit at steady state 90-95% 1P SKUs, no incremental working capital change expected
items.quote: Jignanshu, we are at that steady state now where about 90-95% is 1P, and we don't expect any more incremental working capital change on that account, if that was your question.

items.statement: Blinkit assortment in expansion cities is subset of metros, but harder-to-find products sell faster
items.quote: The assortment in our expansion cities is a subset of what we are selling in the metros. items.statement: NAOV stability driven by assortment expansion in tier 1 cities offsetting lower tier 2 NAOVs, not gourmet stores
items.quote: Most of the offset for the NAOV is assortment expansion in tier 1 cities, which leads to higher NAOVs in tier 1, and that balances out some of the lower NAOVs from tier 2 cities.

items.statement: Blinkit comfortable holding longer inventory for categories like air conditioners
items.quote: Look, we already sell air conditioners, and you can't keep just one week of inventory for air conditioners. So obviously, the holding period is much longer for those products, and we are comfortable doing that.

items.statement: Blinkit tier 2 markets show robust economics with extremely good paybacks and less competition
items.quote: What we have seen so far is that the economics are pretty robust. Paybacks are extremely good in these markets. The other point is also true that these markets are less competitive, and going in first does give one an advantage of locking in the early users of those markets.

items.statement: Quick commerce competitive intensity increased significantly over last 12 months (5-7 players), now more predictable
items.quote: We went through a period over the last 12 months where I would say the competitive intensity significantly increased in quick commerce, including new players entering and the market becoming a 5 / 6 / 7 player market. items.statement: New food delivery entrants surprising, "doesn't make sense to us at all either"
items.quote: It doesn't make sense to us at all either and we are equally surprised.

items.statement: Blinkit mature cities defined as operating 2-3+ years, include metros and top 15-20 cities, spread across regions
items.quote: Mature cities are cities which have been operating for more than 2-3 years now. They will include the metros and some of our older cities, which may not be metros but are in the top 15, top 20 cities. I don't want to name any specific city here

items.statement: Blinkit NOV share from top 8 cities reducing directionally
items.quote: It is reducing directionally.

items.statement: Dark.ai is zero-to-one bet; if it works could be global multibillion-dollar business, if not will kill it
items.quote: It's definitely nascent. We don't have a point of view on whether this could become big or not. If it works, it will become really big; it's more like a zero-to-one bet at this point. If it works, it's a global business and it will generate extremely high shareholder value over the next few years. But if it doesn't work, it's something we'll kill.

items.statement: Dark.ai currently in 'Others' segment, costs not meaningful; capex only if blockbuster response requires GPU infrastructure
items.quote: On your other question, this product has been in the works for about a year, and it's not monetized yet, so all the costs here are accounted for in our 'Others' segment. So they are already carved out. They're not very meaningful at this stage, and we don't expect the capex or cost to become meaningful, at least as of now, unless, of course, we receive a blockbuster response to this product. Then

items.statement: AI agent traffic on Zomato currently negligible, no blocking plan, investing in protocols to learn
items.quote: Right now, the traffic is negligible. While we keep doing this to make sure that we are also able to see what is happening, collect data and prepare ourselves in case this is something which gets traction, but so far there is no traction. So far, we don't even have a plan to figure out how to block them if we need to.

items.statement: Expects further commodity cost increase of 150-200 bps in Q3 FY27
items.quote: We expect a further commodity cost increase in Q3 in the range of around maybe 150 to 200 bps, depending upon where some of the major commodities do settle.

items.statement: Industry demand growth expected to taper to high single-digit or low double-digit in Q3 FY27
items.value: high single-digit or beginning of double-digit
items.quote: Now, we expect that even this Q3, it appears that we will see a very high single-digit or beginning of double-digit kind of growth.

items.statement: EV salience in SCV pickup expected to reach up to 20% by Q4 FY27
items.quote: I do see a potential of the EV salience reaching easily up to 20%.

items.statement: Q2 wholesales grew 42% YoY to 1,35,100 units with broad-based segment growth
items.quote: Q2 wholesales were at 1,35,100 units, up 42% year-on-year and up 24% sequentially.

items.statement: International business volumes grew 177% YoY driven by Indonesia order ramp-up
items.quote: international business was up 177%, close to 2.6 times over last year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin at 11.7%, down 90 bps YoY but flat sequentially despite commodity headwinds
items.quote: EBITDA was about ₹2,800 crores, up 31% at a margin of 11.7%. While EBITDA margin was down 90 basis points YoY, it held flat sequentially despite a commodity headwind intensifying further during the quarter.

items.statement: Commodity inflation impact of 590 bps YoY almost entirely offset by operating leverage, cost efficiency and improved realization
items.quote: To summarize, a 590 bps commodity headwind has been almost entirely offset by operating leverage, cost efficiency, and improved realization.

items.statement: Four pricing actions taken in FY27: ~1% in Jan, ~2% in Apr, 2.5% in Jul, 1-2% from Oct 1
items.quote: On pricing, as you are aware, we have taken already four pricing actions during the year, around 1% in January, around 2% in April, 2.5% in July, and then from 1 October, we have taken another 1% to 2% increase depending upon the segment.

items.statement: Indonesia order of ~70,000 units to be delivered over FY27 and FY28 at 4,500-5,000 units/month
items.quote: Indonesia order to a large extent will be delivered over two years, so this financial year and the next financial year. And currently, we are supplying at the rate of anywhere between 4,500 to 5,000 a month. The total order is almost of 70,000.
