items.statement: Standalone net cash at ₹11,300 crore as of Sep 30 vs ₹7,500 crore at Mar end; consolidated net cash at ₹15,900 crore
items.quote: With that, the net cash stood at ₹11,300 crores as at September 30 against ₹7,500 crores at March and ₹7,100 crores at June end, and this is after the dividend payout in Q1.

items.statement: H1 VAHAN market share at 36.2%, up 110 bps YoY; HCV share 55.7% (+50 bps), SCV pickup 27.6% (+130 bps), CV Passenger 41.1% (+500 bps)
items.quote: Overall, our H1 VAHAN market share stands at 36.2%, which is 110 basis points higher than the FY26 level, reflecting an improvement in overall market position on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Non-vehicular business ~20% of revenue; focus area to hedge CV cyclicality
items.quote: Our non-cyclical business, if you look at it on an overall basis, would approximately be around 20% of the revenue.

items.statement: Requested government review of steel safeguard duty via SIAM due to 40% YoY steel price increase
items.quote: We have certainly put forward our request to look at this and expect that this is seen favourably.

items.statement: Diesel price increases and interest rate hikes (25 bps) remain key monitorables for transporter profitability and demand
items.quote: I think on the headwinds, as I said in the beginning, diesel prices will continue to be a very important monitorable, as also the interest rates. I think a 25-basis point hike has already been taken.

items.statement: International business margin accretive but Indonesia LCV volume is ASP dilutive; non-Indonesia markets (Sub-Saharan Africa, Nepal, Sri Lanka) stabilized and growing
items.quote: So, our international business is certainly margin accretive. However, the Indonesia business is more related to the light commercial vehicle and below portfolio, and therefore it is more of ASP dilutive, right?

items.statement: Fleet utilization improved progressively through Q2; freight rates strengthened; transporter profitability recovered after initial diesel price pressure
items.quote: fleet utilization remained broadly stable to improving gradually during the quarter, indicating sustained operating intensity across the fleet. The freight rates also strengthened during Q2, providing support to transporter economics.

items.statement: No concerns heard from financiers on truck operator financial health; transporter profitability recovered during Q2 after diesel price impact
items.quote: With whatever interactions we have had, we have not heard of any concern in this regard. But of course, it's not that we have engaged with all the financiers of late, but most of them otherwise with whom we have engaged, I think they are in a good place.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% on value and 10% on volume, aiming to outperform industry by 2-3%
items.quote: If exports stay fine or exports revive from here, then around 15% growth on value and 10% on the volume side. Better than the industry, we will try to outperform the industry by 2% to 3% if the industry grows.

items.statement: Q2 utilization at 89%, H1 at 76%; expects FY27 utilization to reach 80-85% and peak of 92-93%
items.quote: As I told you, it is 76% right now. That will improve to around 80% to 85% utilization. Growth will come by improving utilization.

items.statement: No immediate large capex plan; maintenance capex of INR9-10 crores for FY27
items.quote: There is no capex plan right now. No large capex is coming up because, as I mentioned, utilization was 72% last year, and this year, the average is around 76% only.

items.statement: Current capacity 50.6 MSM; Q2 utilization 89%, Q1 63%, H1 76%; peak utilization 92-93%
items.quote: Right now, our capacity is 50.6 million square meters. Utilization was 72% last year. This year's utilization in the first half is 76%.

items.statement: Northeast plant started; Q3 utilization expected at 75%, Q4 at 85-87%; adds 6.4 MSM capacity next year
items.quote: The Northeast plant has started. There, in the last quarter, it was at 50% utilization. From this month onwards, in the third quarter, 75% utilization will come.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin driven by 21% average realization improvement (17% price hike, 3.5% product mix) and 89% utilization; expects better margins in Q3/Q4
items.quote: Our average realization improvement is 21%, of which, as I mentioned, 17-odd percent is on account of price hike, and the remaining 3.5% to 4% has come from our product mix.

items.statement: H1 average price hike of 17% (14% in Q1, 3-3.5% in Q2) vs 14% input cost increase; current gas price INR92/SCM, average 80-85
items.quote: Average we took it in Q1 itself. In Q1, we took around 14%, and added 3% to 3.5% in Q2. So, average price hike of H2 is 17%.

items.statement: No immediate price hike planned despite gas price rise to INR92; 3% leeway as price hikes (16-17%) exceed input cost increase (14-15%)
items.quote: No, we are not going to take one right now because, as I mentioned, our input cost increased by 14% to 15% versus the price hike of 17% we have already taken.

items.statement: Within GVT, shift to higher-value larger sizes (6x4, 8x4 feet) driving 3.5% realization improvement from mix
items.quote: Within GVT as well, higher margins as I mentioned, 18 different sizes and 20 different surfaces. Within that, the sales of high-value products are improving where margins are higher.

items.statement: Domestic GVT volume growth 14% YoY H1; exports declined 18% revenue, 18% volume due to container/freight issues
items.quote: Domestic GVT volume growth is 14%. Where we have our 82% GVT, in domestic, we are growing. Plus, exports are currently weak due to non-availability of containers and container freight.

items.statement: Export revenue down 18% YoY H1; freight rates declining (US from $7,500 to $5,500), availability improving; expects recovery from next month
items.quote: So, right now, freight has started declining. If we look in comparison to last month, for example, the US freight was around 7,000 to 7,500, which has come down to around 5,500 this month.

items.statement: Export mix stable at ~20% of revenue long-term; only branded exports, no white-label; industry exports down 40% vs company 18%
items.quote: If you look at our numbers for the last 4 years, our average is 80% domestic and 20% exports, 1% or 2% plus or minus. You can expect that going forward in the next 2 years to 3 years, our split is going to remain this only.

items.statement: IPO fresh issue of INR320 crores used for debt repayment; interest cost going forward almost zero
items.quote: Our IPO was of INR708 crores. INR320 crores was a fresh issue, through which we are going to do debt repayment. The interest cost, going forward, will become almost zero.

items.statement: Depreciation policy changed from WDV to SLM over 10 years (from 15 years); INR14-17 crores PAT impact
items.quote: Regarding depreciation, earlier we used to charge via the WDV method, which we have now shifted to the straight-line SLM method. If you look at this, around INR17 crores difference -- INR14 crores difference you can assume at the PAT level.

items.statement: Northeast plant benefits: GST (CGST+SGST), interest subvention on working capital and term loan, capital subsidy, freight advantage INR120 vs INR2-3 per meter
items.quote: In the Northeast, there is a benefit. Government benefit is there, so GST benefit is there, CGST and SGST both, and interest subvention is there.

items.statement: Domestic sales split: 72% retail, 28% project; 309 EBOs, ~2,000 MBOs
items.quote: 72% is retail, and 28% is project of domestic business.

items.statement: Average realization second highest among listed peers; 2-3% higher or at par on apple-to-apple product comparison
items.quote: On average realization, we are -- I think, the second highest in the industry, you can say, in a way, among those who are listed.

items.statement: Bathware 10% of revenue; expected to remain 10-12%; faucets outsourced, sanitaryware in-house; industry price hikes: faucets 25%, sanitaryware 17% YoY
items.quote: So bathware is 10% for us. Because the base is small, we are expecting additional growth there, larger than tiles. But I feel that in the coming years, this will remain at 10% to 12% only.

items.statement: Morbi gas (propane) average price: Q1 INR84.73, Q2 INR80.53, current INR92; Northeast uses coal gasifier
items.quote: In Q1, it was 84.73 in Morbi, and in Q2, 80.53. That was the average price for propane. In the East, it is all coal.

items.statement: No seasonality but H1 40-42% of revenue, H2 larger; export recovery dependent on freight normalization and geopolitical situation
items.quote: There is no seasonality as such, but our first half is slightly around 40% to 42%, and the second half is larger. Seasonality as such is not there, but between the first half versus second half, there is a gap.

items.statement: IST (Integrated Stone Technology) launched: first in Asia, full-body marble replica, ex-factory INR300/sqft vs natural marble INR4,000-6,000/sqft
items.quote: IST is the 100% replica of natural marble. If you polish IST, you will get the print underneath as well. IST is a completely different technology, and we are the first one to launch it in India.

items.statement: Simola divested: H1 FY26 revenue INR60 crores vs H1 FY27 INR9 crores; focus on bottom line over volume
items.quote: Last year in the first half, INR60 crores was accounted for, versus this year in the first half, INR9 crores has been accounted for.

items.statement: Targets ₹500 crore revenue over next five to seven years
items.quote: I am proud to say that we continue to progress towards our long-term strategy of becoming a ₹500 crore company over the next five to seven years.

items.statement: FY26 revenue grew ~12% YoY crossing ₹100 crore milestone
items.quote: I am pleased to share that FY 2025 –2026 was a year of strong progress for Sintercom, with the Company crossing the important milestone of ₹100 crore in annual revenue.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 sales grew ~18% YoY
items.quote: We have continued to see this growth momentum in the current financial year, FY 2026 –2027. During the first quarter, we registered year-on-year sales growth of approximately 18%.

items.statement: Received nomination for soft magnetic composite stator components for EVR electric motors
items.quote: During FY 2025–2026, we received a business nomination for the manufacture and supply of soft magnetic composite stator components for EVR electric motors intended for automotive and industrial applications.

items.statement: Tenneco export PPAP approvals delayed; some parts in serial production, rest under testing
items.quote: Samples have been submitted to the customer. However, PPAP approvals have been delayed on the customer's side, possibly due to tariff-related issues.

items.statement: Received Bajaj Auto approval to supply GPDN gears using rolling technology
items.quote: We have also received approval from Bajaj Auto to supply GPDN gears manufactured using rolling technology.

items.statement: Profit after tax more than doubled in FY26; strong PBT and EBITDA growth
items.quote: Our year-on-year sales growth was approximately 12%. We also witnessed strong growth in our profit before tax and EBITDA.

items.statement: Operating cash generation turned positive in FY26; inventory and receivables increased
items.quote: During FY 2025 –2026, we also made progress in improving our operating cash generation, which turned positive during the year.

items.statement: Improving working-capital efficiency and cash generation key priorities for FY27
items.quote: Improving working-capital efficiency, strengthening cash generation and maintaining financial discipline will therefore remain key priorities during FY 2026–2027.

items.statement: Focus on increasing high-value, technology-oriented products and diversifying into non-auto industrial segments
items.quote: Our overarching objective is to systematically increase the share of high-value, technology-oriented products within our portfolio, thereby diversifying our revenue mix and mitigating concentration risks.

items.statement: Early-stage co-development with customers to align engineering with product roadmaps
items.quote: Our strategic approach relies on early-stage co-development with customers, allowing us to align our engineering and manufacturing capabilities directly with their product roadmaps from the outset.

items.statement: Sees opportunity from L&T and EVR Motors collaboration for local electric motor development
items.quote: We have seen announcements of new investments by major companies in e-mobility and electrification, including the recent announcement concerning collaboration between L&T and EVR Motors for the development of electric motors locally in India.

items.statement: Will continue investing in skills, technical capabilities, leadership development and automation
items.quote: As we prepare for the future, we will continue to invest in skills, technical capabilities, leadership development and a culture of continuous improvement.

items.statement: Emphasises workforce development, professional ownership and safety culture
items.quote: Manufacturing is a capital-intensive but fundamentally people-driven enterprise. Advanced machinery and technology are critical, but it is the expertise, problem-solving capabilities and daily dedication of our personnel that translate these assets into shareholder value.

items.statement: Crossed ₹100 crore annual revenue milestone in FY26
items.quote: Crossing the ₹100 crore revenue milestone is a proud moment for the entire Sintercom family.

items.statement: Tenneco PPAP delays possibly due to tariff-related issues
items.quote: However, PPAP approvals have been delayed on the customer's side, possibly due to tariff-related issues.

items.statement: Approved material related-party transactions with Jignesh Raval, AJ Fibertek India and Miba Sinter Austria for FY27
items.quote: The third agenda item is the approval of the proposed material related-party transaction with Mr. Jignesh Raval during the financial year 2026–2027, to be passed as an ordinary resolution.

items.statement: PAT target of INR 1,100 crores plus by FY28 reiterated
items.quote: We remain confident in achieving our previously guided target of INR 1,100 crores plus PAT by FY28.

items.statement: Capex spend of INR 250 crores in Q2 FY27; FY27 total expected at INR 800-900 crores
items.quote: And we expect in this year to be around INR 800 crores to INR 900 crores of spend in total.

items.statement: Carbon Nanotube 200 TPA facility targeted for Q4 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: Our 200 TPA Carbon Nanotube facility remains targeted for commissioning in Q4 FY27.

items.statement: Super Speciality Carbon Black 6,000 TPA capacity targeted for Q4 FY28
items.quote: In Super Special ity Carbon Black, our planned 6,000 TPA capacity remains targeted for Q4 FY28

items.statement: LFP cathode active material 2,000 TPA initial capacity targeted for Q3 FY27; 40,000 TPA expansion planned for FY28 end
items.quote: Our LFP cathode active material s roadmap is also progressing well with the initial 2,000 TPA capacity targeted for commissioning in Q3 FY27

items.statement: Anthraquinone and carbazole full 5,300 TPA capacity targeted for Q4 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: In anthraquinone and carbazole, our in-house engineering team has enabled us to accelerate execution with full capacity 5,300 TPA now targeted for commissioning together in Q4 FY27.

items.statement: EBITDA per metric ton at INR 20,990 in Q2 FY27 vs INR 17,910 YoY; sustainable range guided at INR 20,000-24,000
items.quote: So overall, if you look, 17,910 was the EBITDA margin on corresponding quarter last year. And today, it is 20,990.

items.statement: New products (anthraquinone, carbazole, LFP) expected to be margin accretive from start of operations
items.quote: Yes, definitely, these products will start from the start only. They will add to the incremental margin.

items.statement: Carbon Black capacity utilisation at 88% in Q2 FY27; guided at 88-95% for coming quarters
items.quote: during the current quarter, we had a capacity utili sation of 88%. And we are looking forward at these levels only 88% to 90%- 95% capacity utilisation

items.statement: Export share increased from 26% to 33% of total sales YoY
items.quote: Corresponding quarter last year, we had 26% as export, today, we have 33%.

items.statement: Net working capital as % of sales improved QoQ from 41% to 37%; debtor days stable at 65 vs 63 last quarter
items.quote: If you look at the working capital, Q1 FY27, our net working capital as a percentage of sales was 41%, which has come down to 37% in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Capex to be funded entirely from internal accruals; net debt ~INR 500 crores against INR 1,500 crores capex over 2 years
items.quote: So INR 1,500 crores is over 2 years. So everything will be through internal accrual.

items.statement: Proposed demerger of Birla Tyres from Dalmia Bharat Refractories into Himadri, subject to approvals
items.quote: The Board has proposed the demerger of tyre business from Dalmia Bharat Refractories Limited into Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd, subject to the requisite statutory, regulatory, creditor, and shareholders' approvals.

items.statement: Birla Tyres trading revenue INR 140 crores with INR 1 crore EBITDA in Q2 FY27; on track for breakeven post-merger
items.quote: We do a trading sales from Himadri and we achieved a top line of INR 140 crores on which we have an EBITDA of INR 1 crores as a trading margin.

items.statement: Mining environmental clearance received; operations to start in Q3 FY27; targeting INR 500 crores annual revenue
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that we have received environmental clearance during the current month and the mining will be operational during the current quarter.

items.statement: LFP 2,000 TPA plant targeting 50%+ utilisation in year 1, 90%+ from year 2
items.quote: So for the year 1, we are targeting 50% plus capacity utilisation. And from the next year, it will be 90% plus.

items.statement: Silicon carbon anode capacity 10x energy density vs graphite (4,000+ vs 360 mAh/g); pricing far higher; capex announcement pending engineering completion
items.quote: The product is very high end of anode technology. So the normal anode has 360 milliampere per gram of capacity and silicon carbon has 4,000 plus.

items.statement: Anode samples supplied to leading domestic and global customers; feedback very encouraging
items.quote: We have already provided materials to leading domestic and global customers for their qualification process. Customers' feedback and engagements have been very encouraging.

items.statement: IBC is technology/EPC partner for cell manufacturers; Himadri materials auto-qualify; engaging diversified global OEMs and customers
items.quote: IBC is a technology partner for many companies who are setting up cell manufacturing capacities in India and globally. So for whom IBC is providing technology and EPC contract for cell manufacturing facility. In that Himadri product automatically qualifies.

items.statement: Raw material pass-through model with 9-10 days inventory; freight cost spike impacted margins due to higher export share
items.quote: We are only having 9 days, 10 days of raw material inventory in order to take care of this volatility.

items.statement: ROCE at 30% for H1 FY27; baseline target for all projects at optimum utilisation
items.quote: If you look at the current quarter also for half year, we have ROCE of 30%, and that is the baseline we want to maintain for all our projects at optimum capacity utilisation.

items.statement: Ardent Impex FZCO incorporated in Dubai Airport Free Zone as wholly owned subsidiary for global sales, marketing, trading and procurement
items.quote: During the quarter, we incorporated Ardent Impex FZCO in Dubai Airport Free Zone Area as a wholly owned subsidiary.

items.statement: Sicona completed acquisition of 100% of Advano in US, adding silicon anode IP, US pilot plant and R&D/cell-testing capabilities
items.quote: Sicona has also completed the acquisition of 100% of Advano in United States, adding valuable silicon anode intellectual property, a U.S.-based pilot plant facility and additional R&D and cell-testing capabilities.

items.statement: Sicona secured AUD 45 million funding from ARENA for next-gen silicon carbon anode technology
items.quote: Sicona has secured AUD45 million in funding from Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) to advance its next -generation October 22, 2026 Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd silicon carbon anode technology

items.statement: Geopolitical freight rate spikes and raw material price volatility cited as temporary margin headwinds
items.quote: Because of that, there has been some hit. So these are temporary phenomenon, which has -- short-term to medium-term business impact of the company.

items.statement: Durofresh brand launched; purity levels best in market; very positive consumer response
items.quote: It is performing very well. The purity levels are the best in the market, and we have got a very, very positive response from the consumers.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance revised to 1% to 2% YoY in constant currency for FY27
items.quote: We are revising our full year re venue growth guidance to 1% to 2%, reflecting softer-than-expected H1 performance and our updated assessment for the rest of the year

items.statement: Operating margin guidance maintained at 20% to 22% for FY27
items.quote: Our operating margin guidance is 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Q2 large deal wins at $5.2 bn TCV with 62% net new, second highest quarterly TCV in five years
items.quote: We won 19 large deals in Q2 with a TCV of $5.2 bn, which is second highest quarterly TCV in the last five years. Of this, 62% was net new.

items.statement: H1 large deal wins total $8.8 bn, up 28% YoY with 62% net new
items.quote: This takes H1's total large deal wins to $8.8 bn, which is a YoY growth of 28% with 62% net new.

items.statement: Net new $2 bn+ seven-year mega deal with financial services client expected to contribute over 1% growth in FY28
items.quote: This includes an entirely net new $2 bn plus seven year mega deal with a financial services client. Transition is expected to begin in the second half of Q4. This deal is expected to contribute over 1% growth for the company in FY28.

items.statement: Q2 operating margin at 21%, down 10 bps sequentially due to post-sales support and acquisition impacts
items.quote: Q2 operating margins were at 21%, decline of 0.1% sequentially.

items.statement: H2 margins to be impacted by compensation hikes, softer seasonality, AI productivity sharing and large deal ramp-up, partly offset by Project Maximus
items.quote: H2 margins will be impacted by compensation hikes, softer revenue seasonality, continued sharing of AI driven productivity benefits and ramp-up of large deals. These headwinds will be partly offset by initiatives under Project Maximus.

items.statement: Pricing pressure increased due to competitive intensity and AI productivity expectations across clients and industries
items.quote: If you look at what we ar e seeing today is a pricing pressure on the back of competitive intensity, which has increased in the la st couple of quarters

items.statement: At lower end of guidance, pricing assumed similar to slightly deteriorating; at upper end, improvement assumed
items.quote: at the lower end of the guidance, we have assumed similarto slightly deterioration on the pricing. At the upper end, we have assumed improvement

items.statement: AI-first revenue now 10.5% of total revenue with 29% sequential growth
items.quote: Q2 AI revenue is now 10.5% of total revenue with strong sequential growth of over 29%.

items.statement: Free cash flow at $928 mn, 113% of net profit; cash and equivalents at $4.7 bn with debt-free balance sheet
items.quote: Free cash flow generation was strong at $928 mn at 113% of net profit. We ended the quarter with cash and cash equivalents at $4.7 bn and a debt-free balance sheet.

items.statement: DSO improved to 64 days, down 7 days YoY; DSO including unbilled net of unearned at 77 days, down 10 days YoY
items.quote: DSO for the quarter was 64, down by seven days compared to DSO last year. DSO, including unbilled net of unearned was 77 days, down by 10 days as compared to last year.

items.statement: Interim dividend of Rs 26 announced, up 13% from last year
items.quote: The Board has announced an interim dividend of `26, an increase of 13% compared to last year.

items.statement: Compensation hikes rolling out effective October 2026 and January 2027
items.quote: As mentioned last quarter, we are rolling out compensation hikes to most of our employees effective October '26, with the next phase effective Januar y '27

items.statement: Utilization including trainees improved to 85.4%; excluding trainees decreased to 81.9% due to fresher intake
items.quote: Utilization, including trainees improved by 0.5%, sequentially to 85.4%, demonstrating continued oper ational focus. Utilization, excluding trainees decreased to 81.9% due to fresher intake

items.statement: Onsite mix reduced to 22.6%, down 0.7% in H1, reflecting sustained offshore shift for client cost reductions
items.quote: Onsite mix reduced further to 22.6%, reflecting our sustained efforts to help clients achieve cost reductions. For H1, onsite mix was down by 0.7%.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for the year expected in 29% to 30% range
items.quote: We expect effective tax rate for the year to be in the range of 29% to 30%.

items.statement: Subcontractor costs at elevated levels; reducing by 1% yields 15-20 bps margin improvement but will not go to zero
items.quote: If you are able to bring the subcontractor down by 1%, we have stated in the past, it gives you around 15 bps to 20 bps on margin. So yes, to that extent, there is opportunity, but it will never come down to zero.

items.statement: Yield on cash investments at approximately 6.9% in Q2
items.quote: Q2 yield on cash investment balance was at approximately 6.9%.

items.statement: EPS at Rs 19.32, up 8.7% YoY; H1 EPS at Rs 38.51, up 11.7% YoY
items.quote: EPS for the quarter stood at `19.32, up 8.7% on a Y-on-Y basis. H1 EPS stood at `38.51, a double-digit growth of 11.7%.

items.statement: Domestic agri-input demand hit by deficient rainfall, crop-mix changes, subdued farm economics and competitive intensity
items.quote: India's agri -input sector faced significant headwinds during the 2026 Kharif season amid deficient and erratic rainfall, crop-mix changes, subdued farm economics and heightened competitive intensity.

items.statement: Rabi outlook sensitive to winter rainfall, soil moisture and irrigation; reservoirs at 70% capacity vs 10-year avg 76.6%
items.quote: The outlook remains sensitive to winter rainfall, soil moisture and irrigation availability. IMD’s northeast monsoon forecast of 88–112% of the long- period average is relevant to southern peninsular India but does not guarantee adequate rainfall across th e country

items.statement: No extra channel inventory; placement only where water situation is certain
items.quote: We have taken a very conscious effort this year because this year, given there was a highly uneven rainfall distribution, we have gone with a more market-based approach, only place the product in the markets, where there's a demand water situation is certain.

items.statement: Q2 revenue flat at ₹858 cr vs ₹861 cr; 5% price growth offset by similar volume de-growth
items.quote: Our Q2FY27 revenue stood at ₹ 858 cr as against ₹ 861 cr for the same period last year resulting in an overall flat growth. Pricing growth of 5% was offset by similar volume de-growth.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA fell 18% to ₹126 cr; PAT down 17% to ₹85 cr
items.quote: Overall EBITDA for Q2FY27 stood at ₹ 126 cr, lower by 18% compared to ₹ 154 cr in Q2 of the previous year. Profit after tax stood at ₹ 85 cr versus ₹ 102 cr of Q2FY26, which is 17% lower than the same quarter of previous year.

items.statement: Crop Care revenue grew 4% to ₹788 cr on 6% price growth; Domestic B2C de-grew 1%; B2B grew 17%
items.quote: Crop Care revenue grew by 4% to ₹ 788 cr in Q2FY27 from ₹ 760 cr in Q2FY26 due to 6% price growth. EBITDA decreased by 2% to ₹ 126 cr in Q2FY27 from ₹ 129 cr in Q2FY26.

items.statement: Seeds revenue fell 31% to ₹70 cr on 26% volume decline; EBITDA turned negative
items.quote: Seed's Revenue de-grew by 31% to ₹ 70 cr in Q2FY27 from ₹ 101 cr in Q2FY26 due to 26% volume decline. EBITDA decreased to ₹ (0) cr in Q2FY27 from ₹ 25 cr in Q2FY26.

items.statement: H1 capex very low; H2 will be higher than H1; full year a little more than ₹50 cr
items.quote: H1, we may have a little bit higher number than that to prioritize some of the growth initiatives as well as some of the important sustenance capex initiatives. So I can say that broadly H2 will be more than H1, that way.

items.statement: New R&D centre in Navi Mumbai on track; likely commissioning April 2027
items.quote: We are also coming up with new R&D centre in Navi Mumbai, for which onboarding of various consultant on project as well as government liasoning has been completed. The project is running as per the plan, and likely commissioning is in Apr27.

items.statement: Inventory elevated vs last year (seed + crop protection); expect normalization by March; receivables under control; aim to generate free cash flow for full year
items.quote: At quarter end our inventory levels remain elevated in comparison to the same quarter of last year. We expect capacity utilisation to remain broadly stable, with growth driven by improved product mix, operational efficiencies and higher-value product offerings.

items.statement: Tried to pass on cost increases early in season but demand fell; had to roll back price hikes
items.quote: Now this year, in the beginning of the season, we did try to pass on some of the cost increases to the customer, but season did not take off as expected. In fact, demand went down. As a result, it became unrealistic to hold on to the cost increase which we are trying to pass on.

items.statement: Raw material procurement at higher prices due to war; supply chain disruptions and container delays of 2-4 weeks
items.quote: So, I think overall, I would say there's a 2-3 weeks, sometimes 4 weeks cumulative delay in the supply chain.

items.statement: Exports grew ~2.5% to ₹165 cr on 10% price growth; volumes hit by lower Pendimethalin demand in Europe, China pricing pressure, raw material constraints and shipping delays
items.quote: Exports (sub-category of B2B) topline grew by ~2.5% to ₹ 165 cr from ₹ 161 cr due to 10% growth in price. There was lower demand for Pendimethalin AI in Europe, coupled with pricing challenges from China market.

items.statement: Deliberately prioritized domestic over exports when war started; margins protected despite volume degrowth
items.quote: Part of the degrowth in the export market was deliberate, and we use that as an opportunity to improve the margin. As a result, our margins have not shrunk as much in export market as much as volumes.

items.statement: Chinese suppliers remain aggressive; smaller players facing working capital stress but not exiting; consolidation possible if valuations align
items.quote: China continues to remain very aggressive by being a very competitive supplier. Sometimes it is very puzzling, Sometimes you think your cost of production doesn't seem to justify and people sell at that price.

items.statement: New product launches contributed ~₹100 cr revenue in FY27 kharif; dropped ~₹100 cr old products over 4 years; added ~₹300 cr via 58 new products
items.quote: For example, this year, of the what you call launches, which I made in '27 in the kharif season, they have already significantly contributed to the extent of about INR100 crores.

items.statement: Herbicide prices already crashing in North India ahead of wheat season; excess supply persists in key segments
items.quote: Now wheat crop, you can already see pressure on the prices of herbicides. So obviously, we are not a large player, so it may not impact me. And that's why I said. So in every season, every crop, it depends on what your portfolio is, but there's a significant pressure on the prices of herbicide in Northern India already.

items.statement: Idea2Impact innovation platform received ~42 applications; 2 in pilot, 28 under review
items.quote: We had launched Idea2Impact innovation platform in Q4 of FY26 to establish an open innovation ecosystem to source, validate and commercialize agri-innovations. Till now we have received encouraging participation of ~4 2 applications, out of which 2 are in pilot stage and 28 under review.

items.statement: Cotton seed price increases capped by government; maize ethanol policy caps procurement price
items.quote: The only crop price increases are not possible is cotton because it is capped by the government.

items.statement: Cash and liquid balance of ~₹211 cr as of 30th Sept 2026
items.quote: We have cash and liquid balance of ~₹ 211 cr as of 30th Sept '26.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA grew 2% to ₹311 cr; PAT grew 6% to ₹210 cr
items.quote: H1FY27 EBITDA stood at ₹ 311 cr vs ₹ 304 cr of H1FY26, resulting in growth of 2%. H1FY27 PAT stood at ₹ 210 cr vs ₹ 197 cr of H1FY26, resulting in growth of 6%.

items.statement: Soil & Plant Health grew 22% to ₹74 cr on 15% price and 7% volume growth due to fertilizer shortage
items.quote: Soil & Plant Health (SPH) sub-category grew by 22% to ₹ 74 cr in Q2FY27 from ₹ 61 cr in Q2FY26, driven by price growth of 1 5% and volume growth of 7% . Demand for the inorganic manure increased due to short availability of traditional fertilizers and import dependent raw materials.

items.statement: CSM (B2B sub-category) revenue grew ~12x to ₹27 cr from ₹2 cr on PEKK volume rebound
items.quote: CSM (sub-category of B2B) Q2FY27 revenue displayed promising growth by lodging ~12x growth by registering revenue of ₹ 2 7 cr from ₹ 2 cr in Q2FY26 , driven by rebound in PEKK sales volumes.

items.statement: Revised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15-17% from 12-14%, Hotel segment 17-19%
items.quote: we are confident of exceeding our previously communicated FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance of 12% to 14% by 300 basis points. Accordingly, we are revising our full year growth guidance upwards to 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Management fee growth guidance of high teens CAGR, targeting INR1,000 cr in 2 years
items.quote: we remain confident of sustaining management fee growth at a high teens CAGR, supported by a strong pipeline of hotel openings and incremental contributions from newly added hotels.

items.statement: Plan to open 50 hotels in FY27, 30 in H2
items.quote: We are also on track to achieve our target of 50 hotel openings this year. That means 30 hotels are expected to open in the second half of this year.

items.statement: Portfolio at 670 hotels with 69,000+ keys, 390 operational, 94% pipeline capital-light
items.quote: taking our portfolio to 670 hotels with over 69,000 keys in operation or under development. With 390 operational hotels, we are on track to cross the 400 hotel milestone in November or latest before the end of Q3.

items.statement: Revised 700 hotel target expected before end of FY27, update by mid-November
items.quote: We will revert to all the investors by middle of November with a revised target of the 700 because we should get to that number definitely before the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Consolidated operating EBITDA margin 28.4% (+50 bps YoY), Standalone 38.9% (+400 bps YoY)
items.quote: Operating EBITDA grew 24% year -on-year to INR706 crores, yielding operating EBITDA margin of 28.4%, an expansion of 50 basis points.

items.statement: Double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands, occupancy up to 82% from 75%, domestic demand resilient despite geopolitical headwinds
items.quote: Despite these challenges, domestic demand remained resilient, supported by multiple large MICE events such as the BRICS Summit. We delivered double-digit RevPAR growth across all our brands

items.statement: Structural shift in domestic consumption, foreign tourist arrivals CAGR 3.9% vs domestic 11%, WTTC summit next year potential upside
items.quote: there is a structural shift when it comes to India, the consumer behavior has changed. The consumption is for now. And it's not for like 5 years from now, we will do this or 3 years from now, we'll do that.

items.statement: Asset management upgrades driving pricing power, Taj Palace Delhi room revenue up 132%, crossed INR100 cr monthly revenue
items.quote: A strong example is Taj Palace, New Delhi, where room revenue grew 132% in Q2 FY27 versus last year. In September, the hotel crossed INR100 crores in monthly revenue for the first time

items.statement: H1 capex 20-30% higher than annual average of last 7-8 years, continuous renovation of iconic assets
items.quote: if you look at our capex spend in the first half of this year is higher than what we used to spend annually. It's 20% to 30% higher what we spend annually on an average for the last -- for the preceding 7, 8 years.

items.statement: OHL merger announced, 25:117 share swap, 6-7% standalone revenue upside in FY28, effective April 1 2027
items.quote: The all-stock transaction with a share exchange ratio of 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares is expected to drive 6% to 7% upside in our stand-alone operating revenue in FY28.

items.statement: Brij, Atmantan, Clarks acquisitions integrated well, 75 signings for Ginger conversion, 30 already onboarded
items.quote: Clarks, which is the ANK, Pride brand, Clarks which has come part of the ANK, Pride transaction is also getting integrated with Ginger. And we have now -- I can say w e have completed 75 signings, close to 75 signings, out of which 30 have already sort of come on board as Ginger

items.statement: Consolidated domestic hotel RevPAR up 25%, Standalone RevPAR up 28%, Ginger EBITDA margin 40%
items.quote: This translated into market share gains with occupancy increasing from 75% in Q2 last year to 82% this year. Our continued focus on efficient revenue management and operational excellence enabled us to achieve 28% growth in stand -alone RevPAR and 25% growth in consolidated domestic hotel RevPAR.

items.statement: Ginger reached 100 operational hotels, targeting 150 by March FY27; Qmin 130+ outlets, Ama 400+ villas, Tree of Life 50+ resorts
items.quote: Ginger became India's first hotel brand. Yes, it became India's first hotel brand to reach 100 operational hotels and is on track to reach 150 by March 31, FY27.

items.statement: Gross cash reserves over INR4,350 cr, healthy balance sheet for investments and upgrades
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to be healthy with gross cash reserves of over INR4,350 crores. This provides us with the flexibility to contin ue investing in brand and revenue -enhancing initiatives

items.statement: International portfolio recovery expected in H2, London October double-digit growth, Pierre positive EBITDA, San Francisco 90% recovered
items.quote: The London property is coming back with a big bang. We see very good increase and a double-digit increase at least in the month of October as far as London is concerned.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia impacting airline capacity, airfares, TajSATS and international markets, fuel/power costs up
items.quote: Ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia resulted in elevated fuel prices, leading to reductions in airline capacity and higher airfares, which moderated travel demand, particularly in certain international and long-haul corridors.

items.statement: Paathya ESG on track: 41% renewable energy, 361 EV stations, 92 bottling plants, 54% water recycling, 83 skilling centers, 56k+ youth trained
items.quote: IHCL now uses 41% energy from renewable sources and has installed over 361 EV charging stations across 170 locations in India.

items.statement: OHL merger scheme filed with stock exchanges, appointed date April 1 2027
items.quote: The scheme of arrangement has been filed with the stock exchanges. And as I already mentioned, the appointed date remains at 1st April 2027.

items.statement: MICE structural growth driver, 95 wedding nights next year vs normal 65, corporate events throughout year
items.quote: the wedding calendar for next year is actually more of 95 wedding nights as opposed to normal 65-odd 60, 65 wedding nights. So there is clearly potential to sort of grow the social MICE business next year.

items.statement: Taj rated World's Strongest Luxury Hotel Brand by Brand Finance, India's strongest brand across sectors, 2 hotels with 3 Michelin keys
items.quote: Taj was rated by Brand Finance's World's Strongest Luxury Hotel Brand. And we are extremely delighted that this is happening again and aga in year after year, including Taj being recognized as India's strongest brand across all sectors

items.statement: Tier 2/3 supply growth 12% CAGR over 5-6 years across 300 cities, demand growth 15-20% met by unorganized supply, branded conversion opportunity
items.quote: a lot of these markets are facing at 15% to 20% demand growth on the room night side. And a lot of that is getting met through unorganized or unbranded sort of chains, right? So automatically, when you put up a quality supply, that shift will happen

items.statement: Select service brands scaling: Ginger 100 hotels, Qmin 130 outlets, Ama 400 villas, Tree of Life 50 resorts, Ginger EBITDA margin 40%
items.quote: Ginger became India's first hotel brand. Yes, it became India's first hotel brand to reach 100 operational hotels and is on track to reach 150 by March 31, FY27. Qmin now has over 130 outlets. Ama Stays & Trails has crossed 400 villas and bungalows and Tre e of Life has grown to a portfolio of over 50 resorts.

items.statement: FY28 expected to be better than FY27 mathematically with 50+70 hotel openings, OHL merger tailwind, TajSATS recovery, barring war/pandemic
items.quote: Those 50 hotels added this year, another 50 or 70 coming online next year with none of that coming at a risk with the international business hopefully recovering and this is all safe for war or pandemic or whatever. So if that happens, every sector, everybody starts suffering. But if that does not happen, then mathematically, it's not poss ible that we don't do better than this year.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 to be better than FY26, with H2 performance continuing to do well despite Middle East uncertainty.
items.quote: we feel comfortable that FY27 will do better than FY26. But there are some of these geopolitical uncertainties and that is a little out of control for us.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target is to improve by at least 160 bps in the medium term from current 14.4%.
items.quote: Our endeavor will be to improve by at least 160 bps in the medium term. However, the velocity of improvement will be to some extent dependent upon macro and geopolitical factors.

items.statement: North America order backlog grew over 50% YoY with strong deal momentum in Healthcare, Retail, Manufacturing and AI transformation deals.
items.quote: our total order backlog for the geography, if you do a year -on-year comparison, has grown by more than 50%.

items.statement: UK order book softened due to deferred decisions awaiting new government budgets and policy direction.
items.quote: few of the contracts that were to be decided have been put on hold or canceled, these are the orders in pipeline, and would be hopefully launched back after the budgets have been finalized.

items.statement: Middle East outlook remains uncertain with significant dip in performance versus plan.
items.quote: the overall outlook for Middle East continues to be uncertain. And we are closely observing the situation, especially the situation that is unfolding in Saudi Arabia.

items.statement: 12-month order backlog at $286.2M, down 7.7% QoQ but up 2.3% YoY in USD due to deferred starts and slower consumption.
items.quote: We closed the quarter with a 12 -month backlog of $286.2 million, a sequential decline of 7.7%, and YoY growth of 2.3% in USD and 10.4% in INR terms.

items.statement: North America backlog improved 7.8% sequentially and 47.9% YoY with 53 AI deals closed, ~45% of total order book.
items.quote: North America closed yet another quarter of healthy order book, as mentioned by Umang earlier, improving the total backlog position by 7.8% sequentially and 47.9% YoY.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 14.4%, down 100 bps QoQ due to 190 bps impact from salary hikes and ESOPs, partially offset by AI productivity and extra working days.
items.quote: EBITDA was down 100 bps sequentially, led by increments and ESOPs, which had a 190 bps impact, which was partially offset by AI-led productivity efficiency and additional working days.

items.statement: UK margin pressure of ~200 bps from sovereignty and security-cleared resource requirements increasing onsite mix.
items.quote: The reason for the low margin was primarily sovereignty ask, and security clear ed resource ask mainly in the UK territory. We have seen a drop in the margin in that particular segment. The impact of that is around 200 bps.

items.statement: AI transformation deals running at 40%+ gross margins, sometimes north of 50%; AI productivity deals more price aggressive with compressed margins initially.
items.quote: AI transformation or AI foundation kind of deals are running with a good margin of 40% plus gross margin and sometimes even running north of 50% plus gross margin kind of businesses.

items.statement: Sale of Chennai property completed, profit reflected in exceptional items, offset by workforce restructuring costs and old receivable write-offs.
items.quote: We completed the sale of property in Chennai, resulting in a profit, which is reflected in exceptional items. The profit was offset by workforce restructuring cost due to AI -led efficiencies and writ e-off of old receivables in the book.

items.statement: Collected $120M in Q2, DSO improved to 74 days (down 1 day), net cash and investments Rs. 582.7 crore after Rs. 50 crore dividend and Rs. 55 crore loan repayment.
items.quote: During Q2, we had another good collection quarter, wherein we collected $120 million from our customers, resulting in DSO of 74, a decrease of one day.

items.statement: Paid Rs. 55 crore loan repayment in Q2; net cash position increased by Rs. 36 crore despite dividend and repayment.
items.quote: During the quarter, we paid a dividend of Rs. 50 crore plus loan repayment of around Rs. 55 crore. Despite that, we were able to add almost Rs. 36 crore to our net cash and investments.

items.statement: Headcount reduced by 87 to 4,810 due to workforce restructuring and onsite/offshore mix change; LTM attrition down 1.2% to 15.2%.
items.quote: Total closing headcount is 4,810, a reduction of 87 due to workforce restructuring and change in onsite/offshore mix. Our last 12-month attrition rate is down for the second consecutive quarter by 1.2%, from 16.4% to 15.2%.

items.statement: Over 40% of deals in Q2 were AI deals across AI Transformation, AI Foundation, AI Productivity and Service-as-a-Software.
items.quote: more than 40% of our deals even in this quarter are AI deals and these deals are really helping shape Mastek towards the future of becoming a Data and AI organization.

items.statement: Added 18 new customers in Q2 vs 13 in Q1; two AI deals were net-new logos.
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 18 new customers, which was 13 in the previous quarter.

items.statement: UK NHS renewal is an H2 event; bidding for north of 100 million pounds deal with bridge contract covering next six months.
items.quote: the large contract that we are currently bidding for and competing for is north of 100 million pounds deal.

items.statement: Public sector grew 6.1% sequentially; Financial Services grew 15.3% sequentially.
items.quote: public sector business continued to show its strength by growing 6.1% sequentially, and private sector, namely Financial Services, grew by 15.3% sequentially.

items.statement: UK Financial Services grew over 16% in Q2; Healthcare & Life Sciences soft due to project right-shifting and recontracting gaps.
items.quote: Financial Services continues to be a very strong subsector within the UK business. Our Financial Services grew by more than 16% in the quarter.

items.statement: Subcontractor cost at 18-20% of revenue; may fluctuate +/-1% due to UK security-cleared resource demand but not structurally higher.
items.quote: Traditionally, our subcon cost has been around 18 % to 20% of our revenue, and that is exactly where it is even now. I don't see these numbers going up significantly.

items.statement: Utilization including trainees down 0.8% sequentially due to investment in domain resources.
items.quote: Utilization, including trainees, was down by 0.8% sequentially because of the investment we are making in domain resources.

items.statement: North America deal tenure average 18-24 months; UK-Europe deals typically 3-5 years tenured.
items.quote: As far as North America is concerned, average tenure would be around 18 months to 24 months in terms of tenure of these deals.

items.statement: AI revenue split disclosure to begin next quarter; horizontal reporting reorganized around Data & AI lens.
items.quote: we'll be starting to outline and present those numbers starting next quarter and onwards. So you will get a clear view of where those numbers are.

items.statement: Revised full-year volume growth guidance to 4-6% from 7-9% and EBITDA per ton guidance to INR 20,000-22,000 from INR 18,000-20,000; capex and net debt guidance unchanged
items.value: 4% to 6% volume growth; INR 20,000 to INR 22,000 per ton EBITDA
items.quote: In this dynamic environment, JSL revises its full -year volume growth guidance to 4% to 6%, from earlier 7% to 9% and EBITDA per ton guidance to INR20,000 to INR22,000 per ton, up from earlier INR 18,000 to INR20,000 a ton.

items.statement: Capex guidance unchanged at INR 2,400-2,600 crores and net debt guidance at INR 2,500-2,800 crores for FY27
items.value: INR 2,400 crores to INR 2,600 crores capex; INR 2,500 to 2,800 crores net debt
items.quote: The capex and net debt guidance range remains unchanged at INR2,400 crores to INR2,600 crores and INR2,500 to 2,800 crores, respectively.

items.statement: Long-term sales volume target of 3.5 million tons per annum by FY29 remains on track
items.quote: it is important to reiterate JSL's commitment to deliver on its sales volume target of 3.5 million tons per annum by FY29.

items.statement: Domestic demand remained healthy across automotive, railways, metros, lifts, elevators, and white goods supported by robust economic growth
items.quote: Domestic demand remained healthy across our key end -user segments, including automotive, railways, metros, lifts, elevators, and white goods.

items.statement: Domestic market grew 14% quarter-on-quarter in Q2 FY27 highlighting strong demand momentum
items.quote: Domestic demand remained robust across key end -use segments, with the domestic market growing 14% quarter -on-quarter, highlighting strong demand momentum in the country.

items.statement: Exports grew 20% QoQ and 36% YoY, accounting for 11% of total volumes in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Exports also registered a strong growth of 20% on quarter-on-quarter and 36% on year-on-year terms, accounting for 11% of total volumes in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Europe export share reduced considerably due to quota cuts; volumes compensated by growth in North America, Brazil, South Korea, Japan, Middle East, South Africa
items.quote: Europe share has reduced considerably, I will say, for two reasons, or not two, one major reason, that our quota without duty, what we can supply has been cut down drastically by the Europe.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA increased ~2% YoY to INR 2,762 crores; PAT rose ~9% YoY to INR 1,666 crores in H1 FY27
items.value: INR 2,762 crores EBITDA; INR 1,666 crores PAT
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA increased by around 2% year -on-year to INR 2,762 crores, while consolidated PAT rose by approximately 9% year-on-year to INR 1,666 crores.

items.statement: Revised EBITDA per ton guidance upward to INR 20,000-22,000 reflecting focus on value-added product mix
items.quote: EBITDA per ton guidance to INR20,000 to INR22,000 per ton, up from earlier INR 18,000 to INR20,000 a ton.

items.statement: Capex spend of INR 895 crores in Q2 FY27, total H1 FY27 capex INR 1,555 crores in line with guidance; all announced projects on track
items.quote: During the quarter, our capex spend was approximately INR 895 crores, bringing the total capex in this fiscal to INR1,555 crores, in line with our guidance.

items.statement: Cold rolling mills under commissioning; HAPL line commissioning to start by end of year or early next year; Maharashtra plant land acquisition slower than expected, needing another quarter or two
items.quote: Some of the cold rolling mills are now under commissioning. The commissioning process has started. HAPL line will start commissioning by the end of this year or the beginning of the next year.

items.statement: Chromeni plant running at ~85% utilization; Rathi at ~79% utilization; RVPL cold rolling equipment to be operational next year
items.quote: Chromeni is concerned, because that is where our biggest stakes were, and very strategic investment, and because it helps us in a lot of our balancing, because this is the plant where we do huge quantities or large quantities of the cold rolling, that we are now running at approximately 85% of utilization. Rathi is around 79% utilization.

items.statement: Q2 sales volume mix: 37% 200 series, 47% 300 series, 16% 400 series
items.quote: In Q2 27, going in the order of 200, 300, and 400, it was 37%, 47%, and 16%.

items.statement: Developed India's first high-aluminum stainless steel grade for catalytic converters and two new 400 series grades, one opening South Africa market
items.quote: Key achievements include the development of India's first high-aluminum stainless steel grade for catalytic converters and development of two new 400 series grades, one of which has opened up a new market in S outh Africa

items.statement: Quality Control Order suspended until March 28, 2027; Chinese imports surged to nearly two-thirds of prior full-year total in first four months of fiscal
items.quote: Since April 2026 f ollowing the suspension of the quality control order, imports of substandard products, particularly from China and of Chinese origin, have increased significantly.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty application timeline extended by DGTR to March 28, 2027; decision expected by December 31, 2026
items.quote: So far as our ADD application is concerned, for that the timeline has been extended by DGTR. I mean within the 1 year, they should have concluded, but okay now they have extended it by another 6 months, up to March 28th 2027.

items.statement: Board approved amalgamation of four wholly owned subsidiaries (Jindal United Steel, Chromeni Steels, JSL Super Steels, Rabirun Vinimay) into JSL to simplify structure and enhance efficiency
items.quote: The board approved the amalgamation of four wholly owned subsidiaries into Jindal Stainless Limited, a step towards simplifying our group structure and enhancing operational efficiency and governance as well.

items.statement: Amalgamation expected to yield tax benefits of INR 100-125 crores from brought forward losses of INR 400-500 crores; NCLT approval expected in ~12 months
items.quote: there are certain brought forward losses in those companies in the range of around INR400 crores to INR500-odd crores, which translate to close to around INR100 cores, INR125-odd crores from an actual tax benefits there.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt INR 3,121 crores at September 2026; net debt/EBITDA 0.55x, net debt/equity 0.15x; CARE Ratings upgraded long-term rating to AA+ Stable
items.quote: At the end of September 202 6, our con solidated net debt stood at INR3,121 crores, with a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 0.55x, comfortably below 1. And a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.15x.

items.statement: Industrial gas availability stable in Q2 with no recurrence of Q1 disruptions; transition to natural gas strengthened operational resilience
items.quote: On the operational front, industrial gas availability remained stable during Q2, with no reoccurrence of the challenges experienced in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Raw material costs in Q2 impacted by lagged effect of high nickel prices in Q1; nickel prices dropped in Q2 but contracts reflect Q1 pricing
items.quote: if you look at the movement of the pricing, this is also true that the n ickel was highest in quarter 1 in the recent quarters if we see. And then in quarter 2 it has dropped. So raw material, whatever the contracts you do, it also comes with a lag of time.

items.statement: Import surge of substandard Chinese 200 series products after QCO suspension hurting MSME players and public safety; industry representing to government for QCO reinstatement and ADD
items.quote: The domestic market co ntinued to face import pressure. Since April 2026 f ollowing the suspension of the quality control order, imports of substandard products, particularly from China and of Chinese origin, have increased significantly.

items.statement: Gas price volatility risk acknowledged; sharp movements could impact margins short-term but pass-through expected longer-term
items.quote: Yes, beyond the point if the things move, then the movement in the gas prices will also come, and if the sharp movement comes, it impacts the industry in the shorter run.

items.statement: Nickel business (Indonesia) EBITDA within guided range of USD 500-1,500 per ton in Q2; volatility acknowledged due to nickel price fluctuations
items.quote: we expect the guidance we had given a guidance of USD500 to USD1,500 a ton kind of a thing. It is within that range, this nickel facility.

items.statement: Promoters increasing stake in JSL seen as confidence in long-term growth strategy
items.quote: I think it should be considered as a very positive sign for the confidence of the promoters in the business, and that is the reason why the promoters are increasing the stake due to the long-term growth strategy into the business.

items.statement: Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions intensity reduced 12% vs FY26; published TCFD and TNFD reports reinforcing net zero commitment
items.quote: During the quarter, we reduced our Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions intensity by 12% compared with FY26 levels.

items.statement: Annual grey cement volume guidance of 23 million tons for FY27 maintained; confident of achieving target
items.quote: we are confident that the guidance which we gave at the beginning of the year of closing at 23 million tons, we are on track, well on track on that number.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA expected to peak at 2.25-2.35x by end of FY27, then decline toward 1.5x over 2-3 years
items.quote: net debt-to-EBITDA may reach, you know, say about 2.3 , 2.35 or between 2.25 to 2.35. That is the peak, which will be at the mostly at end of fiscal '27.

items.statement: Capex of INR3,500 crores in FY27; INR2,500 crores annually for FY28-FY30 for brownfield expansions
items.quote: capex would be in the range of INR2,500 crores yearly in the coming years.

items.statement: Paint business revenue guidance maintained at INR500-550 crores for FY27; FY28 expected to add INR150 crores on FY27 base
items.quote: we maintain our guidance for the year as a whole, because we have already reached a level of around INR250 crores in first half.

items.statement: Net debt expected to peak near INR6,000 crores at 50 million ton capacity
items.quote: It could peak up to closer to INR6,000 crores.

items.statement: JK Maxx paint plant of 75,000 KL approved at INR130 crores within overall INR600 crores paint business limit
items.quote: The Board also noted and approved the JK Maxx proposal, which was to put up a white cement -- a paint plant of 75,000 KL and with the overall cost of INR130 crores.

items.statement: Wall putty plant of 0.6 million tons commissioned at Nathdwara; total white cement and putty capacity now 3.65 million tons
items.quote: we have commissioned the wall putty plant at Nathdwara of 0.6 million tons. So that increases our total white cement and putty capacity to 3.65 million tons.

items.statement: Brownfield expansions of 5-6 million tons each planned at Muddapur and Panna for post-FY28 growth toward 50 million ton target
items.value: 5 to 6 million ton at each location
items.quote: It is around like 5 to 6 million ton at each location.

items.statement: Maharashtra and Karnataka water shortage impact minimal; UP election disruption possible but not before March; confident on 23 million ton guidance
items.quote: we do not foresee that any significant impact would be there. And whatever is our -- we are hopeful that we will achieve our annual target numbers in those regions.

items.statement: Fuel cost per Kcal was INR1.71 in Q2; expected to rise to near INR2 in Q4 with INR80-90 impact in Q3 and similar in Q4
items.quote: the total impact from 1.71 as a cost which was there on exit of how the things look and if they continue like that, the cost may go up to closer INR2. So, with that INR2 we may say, about half-half should come in which ~ JKcement PhillipCapital is an impact of INR80 -INR90 coming in this quarter and maybe similar amount in the subsequent, in the next quarter

items.statement: Power and fuel cost expected to increase by INR80-100 per ton in each of Q3 and Q4
items.quote: we should see power and fuel cost increasing by between INR80 to INR100 in each of the quarters.

items.statement: Cement prices increased by ~INR20 per bag from mid-September across trade and non-trade; further INR10-15 per bag needed to cover cost pressures
items.quote: there has been an overall increase in price of around INR20 per bag, both trade, non-trade combined.

items.statement: Packaging cost has peaked; no further increase expected unless rupee depreciates
items.quote: I don't think the packaging cost has already peaked out. I think we should not see any further increase in the packaging cost.

items.statement: Fuel mix in Q2: 55% Indian coal, 13% alternate fuels, balance petcoke; petcoke consumption reduced to 30-35%
items.quote: fuel mix was 55% Indian coal, 13% alternate fuels, and balance is petcoke.

items.statement: Premium products yield ~INR150 per ton extra profit; premium share increasing across all markets to improve trade mix and profitability
items.quote: premium products normally you get between about INR150 average extra profit.

items.statement: Market share maintained in North; gained share in Central India due to 6 million ton expansion completed in March 2026
items.quote: we have maintained our market share in the North and we have definitely gained market share in the Central India, the markets of Central India.

items.statement: Clinker inventory depleted in Q1 due to kiln maintenance; returned to normal levels in Q2 with some surplus due to seasonal volume decline
items.quote: clinker inventory has depleted in the previous quarter because we took maintenance of most of our kilns. So one is that we have reached to the -- I mean the normal clinker inventory, plus there is some surplus clinker.

items.statement: Gross debt INR6,255 crores, cash INR1,684 crores, net debt INR4,571 crores as of 30 Sep 2026; net debt/equity 0.63x, net debt/EBITDA 1.95x
items.quote: The net debt is INR4,571 crores as compared to INR3,370 crores. The net debt to equity is 0.63 and net debt to EBITDA is 1.95.

items.statement: Grey cement volumes grew 19.38% YoY to 11.3 million tons in H1 FY27; white cement volumes grew 19% to 10.32 lakh tons
items.quote: For the half year, the grey cement volumes have increased by 19% -- 19.38% at 11.3 million ~ JKcement PhillipCapital tons as compared to 9.49 million tons

items.statement: Bathinda project EC and CTE approvals expected within October 2026; work to start immediately upon receipt
items.quote: Yes, within this month, it should be there.

items.statement: Full-year cost of funds guidance at 10.5%; currently at 10% as of Q2 FY27
items.quote: if you remember in quarter 1, we gave our full year guidance of finishing our cost of funds at 10.5%. And we are currently at the end of quarter 2 or half year 1, we are standing at 10%.

items.statement: NIM guidance range-bound around 6% annualized; currently at 5.7% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Net Interest Margins will be range bound within the expectation which was provided, which was about 6% on an annualized basis. We are currently at 5.7%.

items.statement: Long-term ROE target 15-18% sustained annualized; ROA target 4-4.5% annualized
items.quote: On a long-term basis on our ROE framework, I think we'll target somewhere around the 15% to 18% range on a sustained annualized basis. On an ROA basis, we are at about 3.3%, 3.4% so anywhere between 4%, 4.5% is a good level on an annualized basis for us.

items.statement: App launch targeted by end of Q3 FY27 (around Christmas/New Year); metrics from Q1 FY28
items.quote: we are targeting the app to go live in quarter 3, which is ongoing right now by the end of this quarter 3 and probably start sharing the metrics on the strategy by quarter 1 of next fiscal year because we are targeting somewhere around -- releasing it around Christmas or towards the New Year's part of it

items.statement: AUM reached INR72,659 million as of September 30, 2026, up 33% YoY
items.quote: Assets Under Management reached INR72,659 million as of September 30, 2026 representing growth of 33% year-on-year.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 42% YoY to INR15,673 million in Q2 FY27; H1 FY27 disbursements INR32,982 million, up 77% YoY
items.quote: Disbursements increased by 42% year-on-year to INR15,673 million during quarter 2 and reached INR32,982 million for H1 financial year '27 representing 77% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Total Income up 24% YoY to INR2,773 million; Net Interest Income up 17% YoY to INR1,476 million in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Total Income for the quarter increased by 24% year-on-year to INR2,773 million while Net Interest Income grew by 17% to INR1,476 million.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing declined ~50 bps YoY to 10% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our Cost of Borrowing declined by approximately 50 basis points year-on-year to 10% reflecting the continued diversification of our liability franchise.

items.statement: Gross NPA 0.66%, Net NPA 0.46%, Collection Efficiency 98.3% as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: Gross NPA improved by 15 basis points year-on-year to 0.66% as of September 30, 2026 while net NPA improved by 19 basis points to 0.46%. Collection Efficiency stood at 98.3%.

items.statement: Credit cost declined to 0.4% in Q2 FY27 from 1.1% in Q2 FY26; H1 FY27 loan losses and provisions down 47% YoY to INR155 million
items.quote: Credit cost declined to 0.4% in quarter 2 financial year '27 compared with 1.1% in quarter 2 financial year '26. While H1 financial year '27 loan losses and provision declined by 47% year-on-year to INR155 million from INR295 million in H1 financial year '26.

items.statement: Total borrowings INR54,808 million as of September 30, 2026; Debt-to-equity 2.89x; Capital adequacy 30.7% (Tier 1 25.2%)
items.quote: Total borrowings stood at INR54,808 million as of September 30, 2026. Our Cost of Borrowing declined by approximately 50 basis points year-on-year to 10% reflecting the continued diversification of our liability franchise. Debt-to-equity stood at 2.89x while capital adequacy remained healthy at 30.7%, including Tier 1 capital of 25.2%.

items.statement: Raised ~INR294.9 cr via public NCD under INR900 cr shelf, INR124.47 cr via dual-rated unsecured private placement NCDs in Sept, and >INR177 cr via CP in H1 FY27
items.quote: We have successfully raised approximately INR294.9 crores through our public NCD issuance under the INR900 crores shelf program followed by INR124.47 crores listed dual-rated unsecured private placement of NCDs in September. We have also raised over INR177 crores through commercial paper issuances during H1 FY27

items.statement: BC network expanded to 1,690 touchpoints serving ~1.93 million customers across account opening, fund transfer, social security products and micro credit
items.quote: During Q2, the BC network expanded to 1,690 touchpoints and served approximately 1.93 million customers across services ranging from account opening, fund transfer to social security products and micro credit.

items.statement: Intend to progressively broaden product suite around core MSME/micro franchise via partnership-led, asset-light approach
items.quote: We, therefore, intend to progressively broaden our product suite around the core MSME and micro entrepreneurs franchise through an increasingly partnership-led and asset-light approach.

items.statement: Employee base declined 11% YoY in Q2 FY27 despite 33% AUM growth; prior quarter saw 3% YoY decline with ~28% AUM growth
items.quote: Despite 33% year-on-year growth in AUM and continued expansion of our network, our employee base declined by 11% year-on-year during the quarter.

items.statement: AI-enabled onboarding processed ~1.90 lakh applications; AI-driven outbound calling scaled to ~3 lakh calls daily; 25 live AI bots across organization
items.value: 1.90 lakh applications, 3 lakh daily calls, 25 bots
items.quote: During Q2, AI-enabled onboarding processed approximately 1.90 lakh applications while AI-driven outbound calling scaled to approximately 3 lakh calls daily. We now have 25 live AI bots across the organization.

items.statement: AI framework: 65,000 facial recognition matches, ~3.50 lakh OCR scans, 100% AI-assisted legacy maintenance, 100% core-driven test kit generation
items.quote: We have gone to about 65,000 facial recognition facial matches, about 3.50 lakh OCR scans. And we have moved to a 100% AI-assisted journey for our legacy maintenance and almost 100% core driven, 100% test kit generation for the cases.

items.statement: Rural demand muted in drought-affected pockets (Maharashtra, parts of Karnataka, AP, Telangana); tightened underwriting, moderated rural disbursements, stepped up collections

items.statement: Demand visible in mobility, machinery, movable asset financing in Maharashtra; healthy across mobility and agri in UP; opportunities in machinery/mobility in Haryana, Rajasthan; broad-based credit demand in Delhi NCR
items.quote: Despite seasonal backdrop, demand remains visible in mobility, machinery and other movable asset financing in Maharashtra supported by industrial and urban activity. items.statement: Uptick in credit offtake among MSME/SME borrowers across emerging markets driven by working capital and business expansion needs
items.quote: More broadly, we are seeing an uptick in credit offtake among MSME and SME borrowers across several emerging markets driven by working capital and business expansion needs.

items.statement: Co-lending with SBI and other banks status quo; compliant with circular, awaiting banks to complete CIF structure and CBS integration
items.quote: So we are pretty much status quo on the co-lending side of the business wherein that we are doing a little bit of co-lending here and there with all the banks. But most of -- we have complied, like I always say that we are in compliance with the entire circular. We are just waiting the go-ahead from the respective banks as to whenever they are able to comply with their side of the circular.

items.statement: Yield moderation in Q2 due to late-quarter fund deployment (denominator effect); yields to normalize in Q3/Q4; no product mix or competitive pricing changes
items.quote: it was mostly that yield factor was coming because a majority of the disbursement that took from the transition of quarter 1 to quarter 2 happened towards the end of the quarter of the quarter 2, which created a denominator effect temporarily affecting yields. Towards Q3 and Q4, yields will be back to normal. They will be normalized and we continue to maintain the same yield levels across our prod

items.statement: Target 40-50% of customer acquisition via consumer-facing app by end of 3-year strategy (FY30); small chunk in FY27 if app stable
items.quote: But by the end of this 3-year strategy, we can definitely expect anywhere between 40% to 50% of acquisition coming directly from this consumer-facing app because we will maintain that growth to risk ratio that we maintain across all the products and franchises.

items.statement: Management expects consolidated EBITDA margin to be maintained above 15% for FY2027.
items.quote: we should be maintaining our margin -- more than 15% should be maintaining our margin. So that is what we estimate at this stage.

items.statement: Consolidated unexecuted order book stands at over INR5,500 crores as of 30th September 2026.
items.quote: As of 30th September 2026, our consolidated unexecuted order book stands at more than INR5,500 crores.

items.statement: EPC solar and BESS order book is over INR3,300 crores; T&D order book is over INR2,200 crores.
items.quote: Of this, more than INR3,300 crores from EPC of solar and BESS and balance of more than INR2,200 crores from T&D vertical.

items.statement: Added 1.7 GW peak of new orders in Q2 FY2027.
items.quote: our order book has strengthened during the quarter with the addition of 1.7 gigawatt peak of new orders.

items.statement: Domestic solar EPC order pipeline exceeds 30-35 GW; international pipeline around 9 GW.
items.quote: the order pipeline, which we are following is more than 30, 35 gigawatt domestic and international.

items.statement: India installed over 20 GW solar in H1 FY2027; no sector slowdown observed.
items.quote: by H1, we have already achieved more than 20 gigawatt. So, there is no slowdown as such in this particular sector.

items.statement: Solar EPC margins better than T&D; consolidated margin expected above 15% for FY2027.
items.quote: This solar EPC is giving better margin as compared to T&D. And the solar, the way these orders are in hand, and we are likely to execute, we should be maintaining our margin -- more than 15% should be maintaining our margin.

items.statement: T&D (APSPL) EBITDA margin currently 9-10%, expected to improve in coming quarters.
items.quote: Margin profile as of now is around 9% to 10%. That is going to improve because -- that we should be improving in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Expanding manufacturing with additional Azamnagar facility of 1 lakh metric tons capacity for T&D.
items.quote: We are expanding our manufacturing capabilities through the additional facility of Azamnagar with a capacity of 1 lakh metric tons.

items.statement: Executed 456 MWp in Q2 FY2027; H1 FY2027 execution at 1,345 MWp.
items.quote: we executed 456 megawatt peak of EPC projects in the Q2 FY2027. That takes our total solar EPC execution for the H1 FY2027 to 1,345 megawatt peak.

items.statement: APSPL acquisition funded ~75% by debt; plan to reduce leverage over upcoming quarters.
items.quote: we have taken the financing loan. But definitely, with the group initiative or the way we progress in the upcoming quarter, we'll see how we can reduce the debt, which we have taken.

items.statement: No constraints on bank guarantees or non-fund-based limits for future bidding.
items.quote: We are not facing any kind of constraints with respect to the banks. We have limits, et cetera, available for us to go for the new projects or maybe for the bidding to the new projects.

items.statement: Significant repeat orders from long-associated customer groups in solar EPC.
items.quote: there are a lot of orders which are coming from the repeat customers.

items.statement: Solar EPC to remain core growth driver, supported by T&D and BESS integration.
items.quote: the solar EPC will be the key driver for the growth of this company because that will be further supported to the T&D.

items.statement: India's battery storage requirement estimated at 208 GWh by 2030; pipeline building with 144 GWh BESS projects >1 MWh as of May 2026.
items.quote: The CEA estimates India's battery storage requirement at around 208 gigawatt hours by 2030, and the project pipeline is building up with this.

items.statement: Green Energy Corridor Phase 3 approved with INR1.86 lakh crore outlay for 135 GW RE evacuation and 50 GWh BESS by FY2032-33.
items.quote: the Union Cabinet recently approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase 3 scheme with a total outlay of around INR1.86 lakh crores.

items.statement: Q2 solar execution impacted by developer-side land handover delays; not a recurring issue.
items.quote: because of some land portion handover delay, this has been a case in this quarter. But this is one of the case which we have faced during this quarter only.

items.statement: APSPL acquisition contributing revenue; order pipeline over INR20,000 crores; FY2026 revenue ~INR2,000 crores.
items.quote: they also have around more than INR20,000 crores worth of order pipeline, which the company is following. Last year, they have achieved around INR1,995 crores.

items.statement: IPP portfolio at 82.82 MWp; O&M portfolio at 1.5 GWp, strengthening recurring revenue.
items.quote: Our operational IPP portfolio stands at 82.82 megawatt peak and O&M portfolio has reached to 1.5 gigawatt peak.

items.statement: PM Surya Sarovar Yojana approved targeting 5 GW floating solar with 2-hour storage co-location.

items.statement: Deposit growth target of around 25% YoY linked to nominal GDP growth of ~10%
items.quote: Our target is to grow in the range of 25% year-on-year. But it will depend on the market and the overall condition.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of close to 90 bps for the year with current six-monthly credit cost around 73-74 bps
items.quote: our six -monthly credit cost is arou nd 73 bps or 74 bps (81 bps including CGFMU premium). We have given a guidance of close to 90 bps, so we have enough room for any kind of vulnerabilities or one
