items.quote: Then on credit cost, we have said that long term, you should expect 90 basis points to 100 basis points of credit cost on a through-the-cycle basis.

items.statement: Cost-to-assets ratio expected to improve YoY on full year basis
items.quote: We expect cost to assets ratio to improve YoY on a full year basis.

items.statement: ROA outlook of 1.8% maintained despite insurance fee income headwinds
items.quote: We have been guiding for this 1.8% ROA outlook consistently.

items.statement: NIM declined 9 bps QoQ to 5.8% due to higher investment book share and seasonality; loan spreads stable
items.quote: Sequentially, margin declined by 9 bps to 5.8% driven by higher share of investments to total assets and seasonality. Sequential loan spreads remained broadly stable with decline in loan yields (by 9bps) being offset by 7 bps decline in cost of funds.

items.statement: 30% of loan book is floating rate; 25 bps repo hike transmission over next 3-4 months
items.quote: ~30% of our book is floating rate and 70% is fixed rate. So this 30% floating rate book, the recent repo hike that has happened of 25 basis points, that'll get transmitted over the next 3 to 4 months.

items.statement: Deposit rate tenure elongated from 18 months to 36 months peak rate to help NIM
items.quote: what we have d one is we had elongated our deposit rate retail deposit tenure, the peak rate from 18 months to 36 months. So that should also help

items.quote: On a daily average basis, CA balances grew 61% YoY whereas SA balances were up 24% YoY.

items.statement: Deposit rate premium of 80-100 bps over peers to continue; not driven by market optics
items.quote: So, I think 80-90, or maybe 100 bps premium to other banks, we want to be on that strategy only, because we haven't seen any rates coming down because of FCNR deposits.

items.statement: Loan portfolio grew 25% YoY and 7% QoQ; secured assets grew 26% YoY; unsecured grew 23% YoY
items.quote: Loan portfolio grew 25% YoY and 7% QoQ, against banking sector credit growth of 19%. Secured assets, which remain the foundation of our lending franchise, grew by 26% YoY and 5% QoQ. Unsecured businesses grew 23% YoY and 8% QoQ led by microfinance and personal loan.

items.statement: Wheels book crossed ₹50,000 crore, grew 27% YoY and 6% QoQ to ~₹51,000 crore
items.quote: Wheels book crossed the 50,000 crore milestone this quarter and grew 27% YoY and 6% QoQ to reach ~51,000 crore

items.statement: Mortgage book (MBL + affordable housing) grew 12% YoY; targeting 20% growth by next year; not chasing affordable housing aggressively
items.quote: we are really focusing on our mortgage business, and we are hopeful that with the distribution we have across c ountry, we should touch in the range of 20% by next

items.quote: Largely, some of the districts or states might be facing challenges due to drought or high oil prices, but the data has not shown any kind of stress till now. Yes, fingers crossed. Let's see how quarter three behaves because whatever will be there will come in the quarter three. I do not expect any surprises in quarter four, to be honest.

items.statement: AI platform driving ~5% of total disbursements with ~50% operating cost savings; scorecard models delivered ₹500 crore+ unsecured disbursements; Agentic AI LOS for Gold Loans disbursed 2,500+ loans
items.quote: Our Cross Lead Platform, together with Voice AI, enabled ~5% of our total disbursements in Q2; Importantly, this automated customer coverage led to ~50% operating cost savings Voice AI led disbursements. Additionally, the score card-led underwriting models delivered ₹500 crore+ disbursements in unsecured loans during the quarter. Agentic AI LOS for Gold Loans is showing promise with over 2,500 loa

items.statement: Senior leadership strengthened: Anil Agarwal joined as Senior Executive Group Head for Commercial & Institutional Banking; Amol Padhye assumed Chief Risk Officer role
items.quote: We also strengthened our senior leadership team, with Mr. Anil Agarwal joining as Senior Executive Group Head, to lead our Commercial & Institutional Banking business and Mr. Amol Padhye formally assuming the role of Chief Risk Officer.

items.statement: Received SEBI approval for UPI Sponsorship Services under ASBA framework for IPOs and public issues
items.quote: During the quarter, Bank also received SEBI approval for providing UPI Sponsorship Services under the ASBA framework for IPOs and Public Issues.

items.statement: ICRA upgraded credit rating outlook to Positive from Stable; long-term rating reaffirmed at AA
items.quote: On 1st October, ICRA Ratings upgraded our credit rating outlook to Positive from Stable, while re-affirming our long-term rating at AA.

items.statement: RoA improved to 1.7% vs 1.4% YoY; RoE improved to 16.1% vs 12.4% YoY
items.quote: RoA for the quarter improved to 1.7% vs 1.4% in Q2 last year and RoE improved to 16.1% vs 12.4% in Q2 last year.

items.statement: Insurance fee income consultation paper poses headwind to ROA; offset by forex, credit card, trade finance fee growth and operating efficiency
items.quote: Clearly, there will be some headwind from this insurance fee income consultation paper, right? It remains to be seen what is the final shape in which this is ultimately passed, but irrespective of that, there will be some impact, right? What I want to add is there are other line items within the other income line which are growing on a secular basis.

items.statement: Belgaum clinker line trial runs started ahead of schedule; commercial production expected in Q4 FY27
items.quote: I'm happy to mention that we have recently lit our new clinker line at Belgaum and commenced trial runs ahead of schedule. This additional capacity will help us deepen our presence in our stronghold markets of Karnataka and Maharashtra. As I couldn't think of a better time to bring this capacity online, we look to commence commercial production ahead of the peak demand season in Q4.

items.statement: Pune and Kadapa expansions on track for FY28; total capacity to reach ~67 MTPA
items.quote: Our expectations at Pune and Kadapa are also progressing as planned and are expected to come during financial year '28, taking our total capacity to around 67 million

items.statement: Central India (Jaypee) assets targeting 35-40% utilization by end FY27
items.quote: I'm confident that we are on track to achieve a 35% to 40% utilization of these assets by end of financial year '27.

items.statement: Cement demand grew high single digit YoY in Q2 supported by government capex and low rainfall
items.quote: Cement demand has als o remained robust, growing in high single digit on a Y-o-Y basis during this quarter. This was supported by continued government capex spending, along with relatively low rainfall in several parts of the country

items.statement: H2 volume growth expected in line with industry (~7-8%)
items.quote: I think we should look at second half volume growth in line with the industry. I would just put it at that. I think we have maintained that position. Internally, we are trying to chase aggressive targets. But for you to pick a number, let's take industry growth as the number that we are chasing.

items.statement: EBITDA/t ex-Central fell to INR 746 in Q2; reported EBITDA/t INR 698 including ~INR 50/t Central dilution
items.quote: Putting it all together, the decline in realization by about INR 49 per ton, combined with cost increases of approximately INR259 per ton on an ex-Central basis, resulted in an EBITDA per ton declining to INR 746. On a reported basis, EBITDA per ton stood at INR 698, reflecting a dilution of roughly INR50 per ton due to Central plants.

items.statement: Central India EBITDA dilution expected to widen to INR 100-125/t in Q3 FY27
items.quote: We expect this dilution to increase to about INR 100 to INR 125 per ton in quarter 3 as Rewa commences commercial production before it progressively reduces as Central operations scale up.

items.statement: Targeting Central India breakeven by Q4 FY27 and Dalmia-standard EBITDA by FY28
items.quote: In my last call, I mentioned that we are targeting to be near to breakeven in Central assets by end of FY27. And we are aspiring to reach Dalmia standard level EBITDA by end of FY28.

items.statement: Variable cost up ~INR 200/t in Q2 ex-Central; fuel +INR 100/t, raw materials +INR 30-40/t, adverse mix +INR 50-60/t
items.quote: Variable costs increased by around INR 200 per ton. Higher fuel costs alone contributed around INR 100 per ton, while inflation in key raw materials added another INR30 to INR40. During the quarter, we also saw a meaningful change in the regional mix with lower volumes in East, resulting in an additional adverse impact of INR 50 to INR60 per ton.

items.statement: Further fuel cost impact of ~INR 75/t expected in Q3 FY27 at petcoke >$180/t
items.quote: With external cost pressures persisting and petcoke prices remaining above $180 per ton, we expect a further cost impact of around INR75 per ton in quarter 3.

items.statement: Fuel cost per kcal at INR 1.66/million kcal in Q2; expected to rise ~INR 0.20 in Q3
items.quote: So I think we have reported a cost as roughly INR 1.66 per million kilocal. And we expect this to go up by roughly INR0.20 in quarter 3 basis the outlook that we have in front of us right now.

items.statement: Cement prices up ~INR 15/bag in South and East vs Q2 average; positive momentum seen in Sep-Oct
items.quote: We are already seeing cement prices inching up steadily with prices in the South and East currently around INR15 per bag higher than Q2 average. This should provide some support in offsetting the rising cost pressures.

items.statement: Premium product share rising; Weather365 launch getting exceptional response, accelerating rollout
items.quote: Premium product share continues to increase, and we expect this trend to deepen over coming quarters as we continue to drive this initiative of premiumization. Our recently launched premium offering, Weather365, has received an exceptional response from th e market, prompting us to accelerate its rollout into newer

items.statement: Phasing out Konark brand to sharpen premiumization focus
items.quote: Konark, which has been a cornerstone of our portfolio and a trusted brand for decades, is now getting phased out as we sharpen our focus on premiumization. This marks an important milestone towards reinforcing our brand positioning and building a stronger, more unified Dalmia brand.

items.statement: MMDR Act amendment removed mineral bearing land tax in Assam/Meghalaya from Aug 22; Tamil Nadu still applying it
items.quote: following the recent amendments to the MMDR Act, the mineral bear ing land tax is no longer applicable with effect from August 22. These payments have been discontinued in Assam and Meghalaya from that date, while they continue to apply in Tamil Nadu

items.statement: MMDR amendment reduced contingent liabilities by ~INR 198 Cr to INR 931 Cr (~5% of net worth)
items.quote: amendment to the MMDR Act has also resulted in a significant reduction in the contingent liabilities by roughly INR198 crores, and the liabilities now stand at INR931 crores. Dalmia Bharat Limited. October 26, 2026 Consequently, contingent liabilities as a percentage of the net worth have declined to almost 5%, which is among the lowest in the industry

items.statement: Organic capex INR 909 Cr in Q2; H1 spend ~INR 1,420 Cr
items.quote: During the quarter, our organic capex stood at INR909 crores, taking our H1 spend to roughly INR1,420 crores.

items.statement: Committed to maintaining leverage below 2x Net Debt/EBITDA sustainably; currently at peak due to acquisition and lower EBITDA
items.quote: Guided by this, we remain committed to maintaining leverage below 2x on a sustainable basis, which will create a strong financial foundation for the Dalmia's next phase of growth.

items.statement: Renewable energy share reached 52% in Q2; capacity scaled from 63 MW to ~450 MW over 5 years
items.quote: Over the last 5 years, we have scaled our RE capacity from 63 megawatts to roughly 450 megawatts today, significantly increasing the RE share to 52% in quarter 2.

items.statement: Impaired 97 MW thermal capacity in Q2 as RE transition accelerates
items.quote: In line with this transition, we have impaired around 97 megawatts of thermal power capacity this quarter, where operations have been discontinued.

items.statement: Near-term risks from rising inflation, potential rate hikes, and crude >$100/bbl keeping petcoke >$180/t
items.quote: Having said that, rising inflation and potential onset of rate hike cycle pose near-term risks. But I believe India's growth story is much bigger than the near-term challenges we see today.

items.statement: Central India strategic rationale: large population, infrastructure projects (Ken-Betwa, Noida Airport), brownfield expansion potential
items.quote: Both MP and UP have almost 25% of India's population living here. And I think there are going to be huge investments here. The Ken-Betwa River linking projects is almost INR40,000 crores plus. The Noida Airport and the build-out of the industrial corridor there is going to be huge.

items.statement: Targeting 20% year-on-year volume growth in H2 FY27
items.quote: So, sir, our infrastructure and our team is geared up to deliver 20% volume growth consistently. And that is still our target.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton target range of Rs 7,000-7,500 for FY27
items.quote: Sir, our thought process is that we should maintain our margins at about Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 7,500. That has been our goal for this year.

items.statement: Cumulative operating cash flow target of Rs 800 crore over FY27 and FY28 combined
items.quote: As communicated earlier, we are targeting cumulative operating cash flow generation of approximately Rs. 800 crores over FY '27 and '28 combined.

items.statement: Near-term ROCE target of 25%
items.quote: We have consistently maintained that our near-term objective is to achieve 25% ROCE.

items.statement: Indicative annual capex of Rs 200-225 crore
items.quote: Our indicative annual capital expenditure remains in the range of Rs. 200 crores to Rs. 225 crores.

items.statement: Sanand greenfield facility capex of Rs 150 crore excluding land
items.quote: Sir, we are looking at about Rs. 150 crores of CapEx there apart from land.

items.statement: Overall capacity to increase from 6.8 lakh tons to 8.3 lakh tons by end of next year
items.quote: With these expansions, we expect our overall manufacturing capacity will increase from 6.8 lakh tons and reach approximately 8.3 lakh tons by the end of next year.

items.statement: Adding 60,000 tons brownfield at Dadri and 90,000 tons greenfield in southern Gujarat
items.quote: We will add 60,000 tons of capacity at Dadri as a brownfield expansion. Further, we are also progressing with our planned greenfield facility in southern Gujarat with approximately 90,000 tons.

items.statement: IHT-OHT capacity to reach 15,000 tons within this year
items.quote: So, hopefully, within this year, we will be able to increase our total capacity of IHT-OHT to about 15,000 tons.

items.statement: Steel cord capacity target of 2 lakh tons from current 20,000 tons
items.quote: So, sir, our goal is definitely 2 lakh tons. There is no changing that goal.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA per ton at Rs 8,150 including Rs 200 inventory gain
items.quote: Sir, I would say inventory gain would be maybe Rs. 200 a ton in this. So, not more than that.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA per ton target of Rs 8,000-10,000+ as specialty wires ramp up
items.quote: In the long run, yes, we would definitely look at Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 10,000. Rs. 10,000 or higher than Rs. 10,000 kind of range once our specialty wire numbers also start coming in.

items.statement: IHT-OHT specialty wires generating Rs 15,000-20,000 EBITDA per ton
items.quote: So, the whole of specialty-wire segment, I think, on an average, for IHT-OHT, we can take about INR 15,000-20,000 per ton kind of EBITDA number, which we already see us generating.

items.statement: Bead wire EBITDA per ton estimated at Rs 12,000-15,000
items.quote: Bead wire, yes, I think generally this is a good range to consider for bead wire, Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 15.,000 is, I think, good enough.

items.statement: LRPC EBITDA per ton at Rs 5,000-8,000 but currently not profitable due to excess capacity
items.quote: Sir, LRPC generally gets around Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 7,000 or Rs. 8,000 a ton. But that also varies quite a lot. Right now, LRPC is not a good product for us because there is excess capacity in the country.

items.statement: Healthy demand across automotive, infra, agriculture, power and general engineering sectors
items.quote: We continue to see healthy demand across the various industries we serve. One of our biggest strengths of Bansal Wire has been our diverse presence across sectors such as automotive, infra, agriculture, power and transmission, and general engineering.

items.statement: Positive medium to long-term outlook for steel wire industry in India
items.quote: We remain positive about the medium to long-term outlook for the steel wire industry in India, supported by increasing industry activity, infrastructure development, and growing demand for specialized wire products.

items.statement: Low carbon wire share at 55% of volumes (lower end of 55-60% range) improving blended EBITDA
items.quote: So, actually, in last quarter, although our estimates or our strategy is that low carbon should be about 55-60% of our total volumes, last quarter, our low carbon was about 55%. So, lower end of 55-60% range. Because of that, at the lower end, our blended EBITDA is better.

items.statement: Steel cord: first trial order received, second expected in 10-15 days, third customer samples approved
items.quote: Steel tyre cord, we got our first trial order last quarter, and we are expecting that we will receive another trial order within the next 10-15 days, hopefully. So, yes, that is that. I think that is from another customer. So, we will have at least two customers who have given us a trial order.

items.statement: Steel cord commercialization possible within FY27 from at least one of three customers
items.quote: So, because of that, I feel confident that out of these three developments, at least one of them should be able to click within the next six months, if not sooner.

items.statement: Acute wire rod shortage as suppliers diverted production to TMT; some supplier breakdowns
items.quote: So, in the last 1.5-2 months, a lot of our raw material suppliers have diverted their production from wire rods to TMT, creating a shortage in wire rod. And there have also been some breakdowns in raw material at our suppliers end, creating some shortages in the whole industry.

items.statement: Gas prices at 2.5x regular levels but passed on to customers; availability now stable
items.quote: Prices definitely are still increasing. Right now, it is almost 2.5x our regular price that was earlier in this situation. But it has increased gradually. So, that has also been passed on to our customers.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating cash flow of Rs 339 crore, close to full-year guidance
items.quote: On the cash flow side, we generated operational cash flow of Rs. 218 crores during the quarter and Rs. 339 crores in the first half, reflecting our continuous focus on generating healthy cash flow from the operation and improving the working capital cycle.

items.statement: Debt reduced by 40% in H1 FY27 to Rs 300 crore with 0.2x debt-to-equity
items.quote: Right now, if you see even last quarter's result, in the first six months itself, we have reduced our debt by 40%. So, our total debt today stands at about Rs. 300 crores with about 0.2 debt-to-equity.

items.statement: Steel cord pricing at Rs 130-140 per kg
items.quote: The steel cord average pricing should be about Rs. 130-Rs. 140 a kg as of now.

items.statement: Raw material shortages may cause temporary volume hits but not expected to hamper annual targets
items.quote: Yes, that is true. But I mean, through these years, we faced such issues before. And this is temporary. This I do not see as a long-term glitch in our system.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth expected to outperform H1 levels (27% revenue, 34% EBITDA), beating prior 15%/20% guidance
items.quote: We therefore expect to keep outperforming for the full year as well, similar to the H1 delivery.

items.statement: Management revises FY27 guidance upward to match H1 growth rates of 27% revenue and 34% EBITDA
items.quote: We are saying that we are revising our 15% and 20% upwards given the fact that H1 delivery has beaten our initial estimates for the full year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 61.4% in Q2 FY27, up 340 bps YoY; H1 margin 60.9%, up 310 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for this quarter clocked in at INR 2,445 million, growing 39%, with margins at 61.4%, which is 340 basis points above the same time last year.

items.statement: India standalone EBITDA margin 69.5% in Q2 FY27, down 340 bps YoY due to investments in people, marketing, commissions
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 69.5% versus 72.8% in the previous yea r. It is down 340 basis points. Obviously, this has been driven by certain investments that we made from an employee leadership standpoint plus additional marketing plus commission expenses

items.statement: Issued 4.35 million reports in Q2 FY27, up 26% YoY; India volumes up 19% YoY
items.quote: We issued 4.35 million reports in the quarter. That is 26% more than the same quarter last year. In India, the volumes grew 19% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Investing in capacities, geographies, technology; recently started Italy operations, preparing Saudi Arabia, set up Botswana entity in September
items.quote: Our priorities, as articulated during the Investor Day, remain unchanged. We invest in capacities, geographies, and technology, selective bolt-on acquisitions, and return surplus cash.

items.statement: Large Indian growers doubling reactor capacity in 3 years; IGI scaling lab capacity and service for festive peak
items.quote: Large Indian growers are adding reactors and are doubling their capacity in 3 years. Supply is at its base and not at its peak.

items.statement: ARP INR 891 in Q2 FY27, up 4% YoY; 2% from AGL consolidation, 2% from higher LGD mix (54% vs 52%)

items.statement: Sampann revenue up 57% in Q2; dry fruits and cold-pressed oils ARR over INR1,000 crores
items.quote: Sampann, strong quarter, revenue up 57%, driven by strong volume growth as well. Dry fruits and cold -pressed oil now combined ARR of INR1,000 crores plus.

items.statement: RTD volume up 34%, revenue up 47% in Q2
items.quote: RTD, having reset the entire business, has now started delivering strong results, volume up 34%, revenue up 47%.

items.statement: Capital Foods domestic up 18%, Organic India domestic up 9%; combined domestic up 24%
items.quote: If I put both together, 24% top line growth.

items.statement: International business revenue up 7%, constant currency down 2% in Q2; UK down 8%, US coffee up 6% constant currency
items.quote: International, overall, negative 2% in constant currency, lapping a high base, but overall revenue of 7%.

items.statement: Starbucks revenue up 15%, 5th successive quarter of same-store sales growth, 7 stores opened, total 505
items.quote: Starbucks, as I mentioned, had a very strong quarter. It's a fifth successive quarter of same -store sales growth, 15% top line. We had calibrated store openings to get our new business model in place.

items.statement: Non-branded business grew 9% constant currency; soluble volume up 21%
items.quote: Non-branded business grew 9% on an elevated base of last year. Robusta and Arabica prices continue to soften, impacting realizations, but margins continue to be healthy for the plantations business as well. The soluble volume grew 21%.

items.statement: Growth businesses now contribute 38% of India business revenue
items.quote: Growth businesses up 40%, now contribute to 38% of India business.

items.statement: HoReCa channel at INR200-225 crores run rate with 10,000+ outlets
items.quote: So HoReCa is roughly at a INR200 crores, INR225 crores top line run rate, and we are upwards of 10,000 outlets right now.

items.statement: AI deployment across sales, operations, procurement, consumer insights, trade spend optimization
items.quote: We've started our significant transformational journey with AI with about 1,600 / 1,700 salesmen, which we have on date as of now with an objective by December to reach 100% of our salespeople operating.

items.statement: Tea pricing increased 8-10% from Q1 to cover inflation; current weekly inflation 2-3%
items.quote: We have taken pricing roughly, I would say, between Q1 to now, you would have seen roughly around 8% to 10% pricing, which is in line with the inflation that we've seen in tea.

items.statement: Salt price increased from INR30 to INR32 in May, then to INR34 in October
items.quote: We moved from INR30 to INR32 for the orange bag in May. October first week, we moved another Rs. 2. So the INR32 has become INR34.

items.statement: Robusta and Arabica coffee prices softening, impacting non-branded realizations
items.quote: Robusta and Arabica prices continue to soften, impacting realizations, but margins continue to be healthy for the plantations business as well.

items.statement: 22 new product launches in Q2, 36 in H1 focused on health, wellness, convenience, premiumization
items.quote: We had 22 new product launches in Q2, total 36 for the first half, as I said, focused on differentiated propositions in health and wellness, convenience and premiumization.

items.statement: Launched Tata Salt Plus, Gold Reserve tea, Chakra Select, Kanan Devan Gold, Tata Lyfe alkaline, Tata Spring Alive water
items.quote: We've launched Gold Reserve, which is at a higher than gold. We've launched Chakra Select, which is at a lower than Chakra, trying to grow penetration and market share down south. And we've launched the Kanan Devan Gold, which is at a 1 notch higher than Kanan Devan.

items.statement: Salt market share at 39.8-39.9%, growing share
items.quote: Our market share is now close to 40%, 38.8% -- sorry, 39.8%, 39.9%. So, we are growing market share as well.

items.statement: Sampann categories mostly #1 or #2 on quick commerce platforms
items.quote: Actually speaking, if you look at it, Sampann across the portfolio all our categories are either mostly Number 1 or a few of them are Number 2 positions across platforms.

items.statement: US coffee gained share for 8 successive quarters; entered significant new accounts
items.quote: U.S. coffee, I think eight successive quarters of share gain. Commodities are starting to ease off, especially U.S. coffee, where now coffee i s trending at, 3.10, 3.15 versus the 3.30, 3.50 of last year. So around that piece, we remain confident of growing, a; b, distribution expansion. We've gotten into significant accounts now in the U.S. as well

items.statement: AI automation deployed for invoice validation and payment
items.quote: We've already started automation with invoice validation and payment.

items.statement: A&P-to-Sales at 5.5% for Q2, 5.8% for H1; total A&P+visibility ~6.3-6.5%
items.quote: In terms of the businesses, overall, our A&P -to-Sales for the quarter was 5.5% and for the -- first half was 5.8%. Just a perspective here is we've reclassified visibility separately and A&P separately. That's why this number you will see separately. Visibility is knocked off from revenue up top. In the ballpark, we are in the same number of about 6.3% to 6.5% i n total A&P-to-Sales

items.statement: Tea industry volumes down ~6% per third-party data; competitive intensity not a spoilsport this year
items.quote: I think if I look at overall third -party numbers, it's about negative 6% is what the number shows. So in that perspective, I think we are in a not too bad space.

items.statement: Mundra port strike (10 days) and shipping disruptions impacted international business in Q2
items.quote: Mundra, there was a port strike for roughly around 10 days. So shipping got disrupted a bit apart from the fact that now a lot of shipping is getting diverted instead of going through the Middle East, it's going all the way around.

items.statement: Management will operate the business in the medium term within an EBITDA frame of 21% to 24% and grow volume at least 1.5x to 2x the market growth rate.
items.quote: I can only say that we will operate the business in the medium term within an EBITDA frame of 21% to 24%. And within that frame, we will keep investing in the brand to grow the volume and gain market share.

items.statement: Short-term EBITDA margin guidance of 21% to 24% is suspended due to volatile raw material and currency environment.
items.quote: We are not giving a guidance for the next few months because it's unprecedented in terms of the raw material price movement, right?

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin was approximately 15%, down from 26% in Q2; 9-month EBITDA margin was approximately 21%.
items.quote: EBITDA was INR262 crores, down 19% year-on-year and 47% sequentially. This translates to an EBITDA margin of approximately 15% for the quarter.

items.statement: Management emphasizes margin per liter as true measure; margins per liter are steady to slightly higher and fully absorbed cost inflation.
items.quote: While unit profitability margin remains intact. In this time of extreme volatility, for us, margin per liter is a true measure. And on that basis, we have fully absorbed cost inflation. Margins are steady to slightly higher.

items.statement: Overall volumes may remain soft in the short to medium term; rural and industrial growth engines expected to grow ahead of market.
items.quote: Overall volumes may remain soft in the short to medium term. However, our growth engines, rural and industrial continue to grow, and we expect these to grow ahead of the market.

items.statement: Industrial business added close to 400 net customers in the last 9 months, driving double-digit volume growth.
items.quote: In the full year and9 months that has followed, we have added close to 400 customers net, and that helped us generate new business as well as drive the top line growth.

items.statement: Early pricing actions taken in anticipation of raw material inflation helped moderate margin impact; pricing strategy is diverse across channels.
items.quote: The pricing actions that we took early in the year in anticipation of the raw material inflation helped moderate the impact on margins, and we have held market share across categories.

items.statement: Raw material bill increased 60-plus percent in Q3; COGS as percentage of sales up 61% year-on-year; adverse currency movements added pressure.
items.quote: However, the operating environment has been unprecedented with a 60-plus percent increase in raw material bill in the quarter that went by.

items.statement: Base oil prices remain volatile; Group 2 and Group 3 base oils predominantly used; PAO used in fully synthetic 0W and 5W products.
items.quote: We have predominantly Group 2, Group 3 are the base oils that are predominantly used. Beyond that, there is something called PAO, polyalphaolefin.

items.statement: Historical capex range is INR 100-150 crores annually; will continue investing in growth drivers (rural, industrial) and plant innovation.
items.quote: Historically, we spent about INR100 crores to INR150 crores, and we spend them on key business drivers of ensuring that innovation in the plant and capacity in the plants is maintained.

items.statement: Plants running at 70% to 80% utilization; range maintained for the full year with seasonal flexibility.
items.quote: I think we've commented on this in the past as well, that our plants run at around 70% to 80% utilization. We are in that same thing.

items.statement: Launched Magna CTX circulating oils, Hysol 35 XBB and Hysol 61 XBB boron-free metalworking fluids; localized products for better raw material cost control.
items.quote: We have also launched Magna CTX, a range of circulating oils designed for demanding industrial lubricant applications. We have also localized a lot of our products, and this is in pursuit of getting better control on our raw material costs.

items.statement: Expanded distribution to approximately 167,000 outlets including 46,000 rural; Auto Care in 50,000 stores; service ecosystem includes 870 Castrol Auto Service centers, 37,000 bike workshops, 16,000 multi-brand workshops, 1,000+ Rural Servic
items.quote: We expanded our national footprint to approximately 167,000 outlets, including 46,000 of those outlets, which are in rural small town India.

items.statement: Fast Scan platform verified mechanics increased 24% year-on-year to 180,000.
items.quote: Fast Scan platform has now got verified mechanics, mechanics who have confirmed their identity to Castrol, which is up almost 100,000 to 180,000, which is 24% more than last year at the same time.

items.statement: Stonepeak acquisition of global Castrol business from BP announced Dec 2024; licensing across 50+ countries progressing; SEBI filing for DPS in India to follow completion.
items.quote: The deal was announced back in December '24, and we were clear then that this is going to take time. Castrol has global operations across many, many countries. I think, the number of countries goes beyond 50.

items.statement: Industrial business delivered double-digit volume growth in Q3; 9-month volume growth tracking ahead of estimated 3-4% market growth.
items.quote: And in industrial, as you would have seen in our press announcement, that has continued to deliver strong volume growth, and in the September quarter, we have grown by double digit in that segment.

items.statement: Operating environment remains volatile and inflationary; crude oil fluctuated $80 to $115; margin recovery timing uncertain until volatility subsides.
items.quote: We expect the operating environment to remain volatile and inflationary. Overall volumes may remain soft in the short to medium term.

items.statement: Cooling solutions for data centers in pilot phase; two formulations recently NVIDIA-certified for direct-to-chip cooling; not a substantial revenue contributor yet.
items.quote: About 1.5 months back, 2 of our latest products are certified by NVIDIA, which means that data centers which are going to bring in NVIDIA chips and which will look into direct-to-chip cooling, we would have products which have been certified to use in those data centers.

items.statement: Maintains 50%+ earnings CAGR for next 3-4 years and expects to achieve INR300 crore EBITDA in FY27
items.quote: Although we have maintained that the business model is capable of generating 50% plus earnings CAGR for the next three , four years.

items.statement: Expects blended EBITDA margin to improve to 6-7% from current 4-5% over next 9-12 months
items.quote: So we expect that our business should be generating sustainable EBITDA of 6% to 7% going forward, which right now is 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Targets 25+ service centers by 2030, potentially 30-35; 8 operational now, adding 5-6 per year
items.quote: We have become more aggressive in acquiring new land parcels and our target is to have 25 plus service centers by 2030. But as the ramp up is better than expected, we believe that we may achieve this number slightly early and we may increase the number of service centers to 30, 35 by 2030.

items.statement: HR coil processing volume 206,000 tons in Q2 FY27, up 16% QoQ; profiles volume ~40,000 tons, up 20% QoQ
items.quote: So if you see in the second quarter, we have done a volume of 206,000 tons, which is up 16% on Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: Service center EBITDA ~INR2,000/ton; profiles INR4,000-5,000/ton; solar structures INR3,000-4,000/ton, all stable QoQ
items.quote: So, EBITDA per ton, if you see, I mean, for service center business, it is around like INR2,000 per ton plus minus, and it's been like stable Q -o-Q.

items.statement: Backward integration of coated steel in Raipur (9-12 months) to add 2-3% to blended EBITDA margin
items.quote: So right now we are buying coated steel from the market, but as our first backward integrati on plant will start in next 9 months to 12 months in Raipur, it will inch up our EBITDA margin by 2% to 3%.

items.statement: Solar order book >50,000 tons with ~1-year visibility; quarterly run rate ~11,000 tons
items.quote: We have order book of more than 50,000 tons currently. Okay, we were waiting to book orders, because steel prices were going u p.

items.statement: Working capital days stable at 18 days; inventory 14-15 days; operating cash flow above EBITDA in H1
items.quote: We have had a very strong cash flow generation, operating cash flow generation in the first half with working capital days stable at 18, which helped us generate operating cas h flow above our EBITDA

items.statement: No debt for capex; funding INR1,500 crore future capex from internal cash flows and INR700 crore cash on books
items.quote: We may need another INR1,500 crores for the capex. So that should be funded from internal cash flows and the cash on books.

items.statement: CRCA sheets sell at INR2,000-3,000/ton premium over HR coil; pre-galvanized sheets also planned
items.quote: So over HR coil, it is sold around INR2,000 to INR3,000 per ton higher.

items.statement: Launching CRCA sheets (1,000-2,000 tons/month per center), pre-galvanized sheets (2,000-3,000 tons/month), welding rods, wire mesh, binding wires
items.quote: So we think that each service center can generate 1,000 tons to 2,000 tons per month of CRCA sheets.

items.statement: ~1,200 dealers/distributors; top 100 PEB companies buying from service centers; online channel launching in 6 months
items.quote: We have almos t 1,200 dealers and distributors to whom we have started servicing.

items.statement: Targets 25% ROC, potentially >30% at full capacity utilization; service center investment INR70-80 crore for INR70-80 crore monthly revenue at 3-4% EBITDA
items.quote: We are pretty confident that the ROC profile we should be able to maintain around 25% which is our target in the coming years. And once these capacities are fully utilized, we may have superior ROC also beyond 30%.

items.statement: Macro risks: steel prices up 25-30% in 6-7 months, high ocean freight, weak sentiment; mitigating via low inventory, no debt, high churn
items.quote: Steel prices specifically, they shot up by 25%-30% in the last 6 months, 7 months. And this is one that when the base commodity prices move with such a spike, okay, it does impact the end demand

items.statement: No specific regulatory changes mentioned; business model focuses on organized service centers in industrial clusters
items.quote: What we feel is that there is gap of a good service center, credible service center, pan -India service center, formalized organized service center in every industrial cluster in India.

items.statement: Dubai service center volume stagnant QoQ; margins slightly better due to steel scarcity; expansion decision after port crisis resolves
items.quote: Dubai also I mean is doing fine in terms of volume is stagnant Q -o-Q. But yes, because of scarcity of steel, margins are slightly better.

items.statement: Building team and tech stack for online sales channel (SG Buildkart subsidiary); no management changes mentioned
items.quote: We have already started investing in the team building and tech stack. We believe that in 6 months we should be ready with this.

items.statement: Evaluating contract manufacturing opportunities; decision expected by next earnings call
items.quote: So our team is constantly evaluating. I am sure we should be able to have something concrete in the next earnings call.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance upgraded to more than 25% and EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 11% to 12%
items.quote: Now based on the strong demand in domestic and overseas markets, we are hopeful to grow in the current year by more than 25% and in next 3 to 4 years by 20% CAGR.

items.statement: FY28-31 revenue CAGR guidance of 20% supported by working capital and cash flow availability
items.quote: Definitely, the CAGR, which we highlighted on the basis of the working capital available and the cash flow available, we will grow at a 20% CAGR in future.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating margin improved to 11.09% and EBITDA margin to 11.73% versus 11.46% in H1 FY26
items.quote: During H1, operating margin has improved to 11.09% and EBITDA achieved is 11.73% against 11.46% in the same period previous year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 operating margin flat at 9.97% versus 9.88% in Q2 FY26; EBITDA margin 10.62%
items.quote: During Q2 FY '26-'27, operating margin is almost at par at 9.97% against 9.88% previous year same period. EBITDA in this quarter is INR 401crores against INR311 crores last year, which margin EBITDA margin over net sales was 10.62% in this quarter.

items.statement: Total order book INR 5,185 crores (Wire & Cable INR 4,927 crores + EPC INR 258 crores) with INR 991 crores export orders
items.quote: Total order book at the moment in Wire and Cable segment is INR 4,927 crores, EPC INR 258 crores. And out of this order book, around INR 991 crores are export orders.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR 402 crores (Sanand INR 333 crores); cumulative Sanand capex INR 1,876 crores; additional INR 200 crores in H2 FY27; INR 600 crores annually for next 3-4 years
items.quote: During H1 FY '26-'27, company has incurred a capital expenditure payment of INR 402 crores, out of which Sanand capex is INR 333 crores. Till 30th September '26, total capex payment incurred for Sanand is INR1,876 crores. Another INR 200 crores approximately will be spent in balance 6 months of FY '26-'27. Company is expected to incur capital expenditure of approximately INR 600 crores annually fo

items.statement: Total metal consuming capacity ~183,000 MT/year; Sanand Phase 2 EHV/HT commercial production by end March 2027; H1 FY27 utilisation: Cable 77%, House Wire 64%, Stainless Steel 91%, Communication 43%
items.quote: At present, company is having total metal consuming capacity of approximately 1,83,000 metric ton per annum, including both copper and aluminum. The planned commercial production of Phase 2 of extra high-voltage cable and HT cable in Sanand will commence by end of March '27.

items.statement: Strong demand across data centres, power T&D, renewables, thermal, EV infra, railways, metros, urban infra, housing, commercial; export demand strong from USA
items.quote: There is a good demand and demand growth of our wires and cables in data center, power, T&D, renewable energy like solar and wind and also even the thermal power projects now coming up in a big way, electric vehicles infrastructure, railway electrification, metros, urban infrastructure as well.

items.statement: Export sales Q2 FY27 INR 493 crores vs INR 472 crores; export order book INR 991 crores with ~50% from USA; expect substantial export growth in coming quarters
items.quote: Export sale in this quarter is INR 493 crores against INR 472 crores last year. We have very good order book position from overseas market, particularly United States. We are quite hopeful that in coming quarters, exports will grow substantially.

items.statement: Natural hedge via 3-4 month institutional order book and 3-3.5 month factory/transit inventory; retail prices revised twice monthly based on metal movement
items.quote: We have the mechanism under the natural hedge because we are carrying 3 to 4 months institutional order book, and we are carrying 3 to 3.5 months inventory in factory and in transit. So our inventory and order book is under natural hedge.

items.statement: Sales mix: B2C distribution 59%, B2B institutional 26%, exports 13%, domestic EPC & stainless steel 2%
items.quote: Sales through B2C sale against distribution network is 59% and contribution of export is 13% and balance 2% is domestic EPC and domestic stainless steel wire.

items.statement: EPC segment winding down; expect INR 5-7 crores quarterly EBIT loss for next 1-2 quarters; EPC revenue now 1-1.5% of total
items.quote: EPC, since we are closing down, so now whatever left-out job is there because the new job in EPC is not there, so small, small closure issues will be there. So it will be -- like in the first quarter also, there was a INR 5 crores loss, in second quarter, INR 8 crores.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target around INR700 crores, EBITDA INR126 crores, PAT INR70 crores
items.quote: And for FY27, we are targeting revenue of around INR700 crores, EBITDA of INR126 crores and PAT of INR70 crores.

items.statement: PCMB business to contribute 8% to 10% of FY27 revenue
items.quote: We expect the PCMB business to contribute 8% to 10% of the FY27 revenue, which is as per the guidance given earlier this year.

items.statement: Completed INR45 crores capex in H1 FY27 out of INR100 crores planned across FY27 and FY28
items.quote: We have completed INR45 crores of capex in H1 out of INR100 crores planned across FY27 and FY28.

items.statement: Plan to invest approximately INR250 crores over 3 years at new Andhra Pradesh integrated recycling complex
items.quote: We plan to invest approximately INR250 crores over 3 years at this facility, which will involve tyre recycling, plastics recycling, pyrolysis and a recovered carbon black plant at this location.

items.statement: Expect to incur about INR100 crores capex in Andhra Pradesh within FY27 and FY28
items.quote: I do expect that we will incur a capex of about INR100 crores in Andhra within '27 and '28.

items.statement: MRP expansion of 3,500 tonnes per annum on track for commissioning in Q3 FY27, taking total MRP capacity to 20,000 tonnes per annum
items.quote: Our 3,500 tonne per annum micronized rubber powder expansion is on track for commissioning in Q3 of FY27. It will take our total MRP capacity to 20,000 tonnes per annum, making us the world's largest producer of MRP.

items.statement: Recovered Carbon Black production starts in Q3 FY27, commercial sales expected in Q4 FY27
items.quote: The recovered Carbon Black production starts in Q3, and we expect commercial sales to commence in Q4.

items.statement: PCMB capacity now 18,000 tonnes per annum after adding 12,000 tonnes at Gannaur
items.quote: Its capacity is now 18,000 tonnes per annum, and we expect the PCMB business to contribute 8% to 10% of the FY27 revenue.

items.statement: Oman plant ran at 90% utilization in H1 FY27
items.quote: Internationally, our Oman plant ran at 90% utilization in H1 and its EBITDA margins improved to 11.5% from only 6.4% in FY26.

items.statement: South Africa Phase 2 crumb line of 9,000 tonnes per annum under commissioning, delayed by 3-4 months
items.quote: The 9,000 tonne per annum crumb line, which is part of our Phase 2 at South Africa is now under commissioning. This has got delayed by 3 to 4 months due to supply chain disruption.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia plot allotted for 24,000 tonnes per annum tyre recycling plant, construction expected to begin in H2 FY27 subject to geopolitical situation
items.quote: In Saudi Arabia, a plot has been allotted for a 24,000 tonne per annum tyre recycling plant. We expect to begin construction in H2 of FY27, of course, subject to the geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Acquired 40 acres land in Andhra Pradesh for integrated rubber and plastics recycling complex
items.quote: I am pleased to inform that we have completed acquisition of 40 acres of land in Andhra Pradesh for an integrated rubber and plastics recycling complex.

items.statement: Consolidated Q2 EBITDA margin 18.8%, PAT margin 10.9%; H1 EBITDA margin 20.4%, PAT margin 12.2%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 18.8% against 18.0% and PAT margin 10.9% against 9.8%. H1 revenue grew by 25% to INR313 crores, while EBITDA grew by 50% to INR63 crores and PAT grew by 60% to INR38 crores. EBITDA margin stood at 20.4% and PAT margin stood at 12.2%.

items.statement: Pyrolysis and rCB business expected to operate at similar EBITDA margin profile as core business around 18%
items.quote: We expect the overall tyre pyrolysis and the rCB business to operate at similar margin profile as our core business, which is around 18% EBITDA.

items.statement: Tyre crushing volumes grew 30% year-on-year to 86,000 tonnes in H1 FY27
items.quote: In H1 FY27, tyre crushing volumes grew 30% on a year-on-year basis to 86,000 tonnes.

items.statement: MRP and reclaimed rubber production rose 19% supported by steady demand from tyre industry
items.quote: Production of MRP, micronized rubber powder and reclaimed r ubber rise by 19%, supported by steady demand from the tyre industry

items.statement: Successfully passed on price increases to customers in recent months; operating at optimal capacity utilization with low inventory
items.quote: We h ave been able to -- we've taken some price increases in the last few months and customers have accepted it and given to us. We are operating at optimal capacity utilization. We are also carrying very low inventory

items.statement: Recovered Carbon Black pricing at least 30-35% cheaper than virgin carbon black with stable pricing
items.quote: There is, there is. See, virgin carbon black pricing is completely driven by the crude oil pricing, whereas this being a sustainable raw material is having quite stable pricing, not that much of fluctuation, and it is at least 30%, 35% cheaper than the virgin carbon black as of now.

items.statement: Renewable energy met 40% of power needs in H1 FY27; renewable capacity rose from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW; solar power savings approximately INR2.37 crores
items.quote: I am pleased to inform renewable energy met 40% of our power needs in H1 as our renewable capacity rose from 1.23 megawatt to 4.48 megawatts and the solar power savings have touched approximately INR2.37 crores.

items.statement: Panipat plant land may be acquired by Haryana government; representation pending; compensation would more than offset book value; no material negative impact on operations
items.quote: In our Q2 filings, we have informed our shareholders that our Panipat plant land may be acquired by Haryana government. While our representation to the state government is pending against this acquisition, we wish to clarify that if this land is eventually acquired by the state government, our compensation due to us more than offset the book value of this plant.

items.statement: Imported feedstock for pyrolysis not permitted as per current policy; using domestic procurement only
items.quote: No, you're right. As of today, for Pyrolysis business, imported feedstock is not permitted.

items.statement: Debt fell to INR111 crores from INR121 crores at end of FY26; interest coverage improved to 9.91 from 7.49; net debt to equity at 0.32%
items.quote: Our balance sheet also strengthened further. Debt fell to INR111 crores from INR121 crores at the end of FY26. Our interest coverage improved to 9.91 from 7.49 and net debt to equity at 0.32%.

items.statement: CARE Ratings upgraded credit rating to CARE BBB stable for long-term facilities and CARE A3+ for short-term facilities
items.quote: CARE Ratings also has upgraded our credit rating to CARE BBB, stable for long-term facilities and CARE A3+ for short-term facilities.

items.statement: PCMB business revenue more than tripled to INR27 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our Polymer Composites & Masterbatch business more than tripled its revenue to INR27 crores in H1 with 12,000 tonne per annum capacity added at Gannaur.

items.statement: Vision 2029 targets: revenue INR1,000 crores, revenue CAGR above 25%, profitability CAGR above 33%, EBITDA margins above 18%, ROCE above 30%, expand from 8 to 10 locations
items.quote: We remain focused on our Vision 2029, which is to achieve revenue of INR1,000 crores, revenue CAGR above 25% and profitability CAGR above 33%, EBITDA margins above 18% and ROCE above 30%.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia construction delayed due to geopolitical situation; waiting for stability before releasing advances or work orders
items.quote: We are just waiting for the situation there to Tinna Rubber & stabilize to some extent. Like I said, the land is already allotted. We know who the contractors will be. We have not yet made any advances or released any

items.statement: Domestic formulations growth guidance maintained at high single-digit for FY27 despite Q2 headwinds
items.quote: High single-digit is what I had promised. We are going to work very hard for it. Let us work for it and see.

items.statement: Regulated markets export growth target of 20%+ for next 1-2 years
items.quote: Yes. That is the target.

items.statement: International formulations expected to deliver decent double-digit growth for FY27
items.quote: I feel this business will definitely go to a good, decent double-digit, if not more.

items.statement: R&D spend capped at 5% of topline, currently at 4% YTD
items.quote: And we had said that it will not go above 5% of topline. I think on YTD basis, we are at 4%.

items.statement: Capex for physical assets limited to Rs 25 crore for FY27
items.quote: But actual CAPEX for land etc. is not more than Rs. 25 crores, I think this year. Less than that.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 9.2% in Q2 FY27 vs 9.1% YoY and 8.8% QoQ
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA to net sales for the quarter is 9.2% at Rs. 464 million compared to 9.1% at Rs. 431 million. And for the immediately preceding quarter, EBITDA is 8.8% at Rs. 410 million.

items.statement: Gross margins impacted by ~30% increase in COGS, raw materials, freight, solvents in Q2 FY27
items.quote: this quarter, our GCs have got impacted to the extent of almost 30% increase in COGS, RMPM, and freight and other handling, solvents, etc.

items.statement: Regulated markets revenue grew 21.1% YoY to Rs 1,109 million in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Revenues from regulated markets for the quarter grew by 21.1% at Rs. 1,109 million as against Rs. 915 million.

items.statement: Added 16 CNG stations in Q2 (total 723); connected 39,574 PNG households (total 11.81 lakh); expanded steel pipeline to 16,305 inch-km
items.quote: We added 16 new CNG stations during the quarter, taking the network to 723 CNG stations, connected 39,574 new household connections, taking PNG household connections to 11.81 lakhs, expanded our steel pipeline network to 16,305 inch-kilometers.

items.statement: Added ~900 industrial/commercial customers in H1 FY27 (1.4x FY26 full year); total base 10,864
items.quote: We have seen a strong momentum in the industrial and commercial connections, added approximately 900 customers in H1 FY '27, taking that base to 10,864. That is approximately 1.4x the numbers added during the entire FY '26.

items.statement: Natural gas costs increased 43% YoY due to higher Brent, LNG prices, currency depreciation and domestic gas availability changes
items.quote: Q2 FY '27 witnessed significant gas cost pressures with natural gas costs increasing 43% year-on-year amid higher Brent and LNG prices, currency depreciation and change in the domestic gas availability.

items.statement: Calibrated pricing approach; do not pass entire cost to consumers; long-term contracts help manage cost pass-through
items.quote: On this CNG price revisions, while we don't pass on the entire cost to customers, we do take a calibrated approach. Whenever there is any pressure on the gas cost because of the current situation, whether it is war situation, whether it is the fluctuation in the crude or Brent or LNG prices, we do evaluate from time to time.

items.statement: APM gas ~25% of portfolio; ~40% of remaining 75% linked to Henry Hub/Brent markers; HPHT gas varies 5-10% monthly; spot gas reduced from ~15% to 7-8% after term agreement
items.quote: Out of this 70%, around 40% is linked to various markers like Henry Hub, like Brent -linked contracts, which includes spot also. That is the answer to your first. On HPHT, it keeps on varying. While government is supporting us in terms of offering that gas to CGD sector, that keeps on varying depending upon the production cycle for HPHT because it is a high -pressure, high-temperature gas well whe

items.statement: Targeting 80-90 CNG stations in FY27 (vs 68 in FY26); similar or more aggressive pace for FY28; H1 added 21 stations, 70 under construction
items.quote: So our CNG stations, last year, we added some 68 CNG stations. This time, we are targeting close to 80 to 90 CNG stations. We are very much into our execution plan in terms of investment and in terms of all the procurement activities. That's very well on tar get side.

items.statement: H1 FY27: ~70,000 household connections, 900 industrial/commercial connections, 21 CNG stations added; 70 stations under advanced construction
items.quote: So this year, we are talking about close to around 70,000 households have been connected in H1. 900 new commercial and industries have been connected and 21 CNG stations have been added in H1. And there is a construction of around 70 CNG stations right now, which is under advanced stage where the equipment procurement has already been started.

items.statement: EV charging: 5,513 points across 225 cities, 63 MW capacity; focus on B2B charging with group captives (Adani Cement, Ports, Logistics) to improve utilization
items.quote: In e -mobility, we have installed 5,513 EV charging points across 26 states and union territories, covering 225 cities with installed capacity of 63 megawatts.

items.statement: EBITDA margin pressure from gas cost volatility; pursuing long-term contracts and opex/capex management to recover margins; CNG volumes growing 17-18% vs industry 20%
items.quote: Now these temporary issues, whether it is West Asia crisis, whether it is volatility in the Brent or all other markers, so these are temporary in nature. So that is why we are engaging into getting into long-term contracts wherever we see it makes sense for us to have better EBITDA margins.

items.statement: CBG plant at Barsana producing 5-6 tons/day (cow dung + paddy straw); targeting 2x in 5-6 months with Thermax as technology partner; evaluating more projects cautiously
items.quote: Currently, we are producing around 5 to 6 tons, which we are taking it to double in next 5 to 6 months. Investment is already being committed. And even the technology tie -up has already been taken care. So we are working towards that.

items.statement: Targeting >2 lakh PNG household connections in FY27; each connection adds ~0.4 SCMD volume
items.quote: No, we are very much focused on increasing the domestic penetration, and we are aiming at closing more than 2 lakh connections this year. That is a very sizeable number, if you see. And in terms of volume growth, per capita on an average is around 0.4 SCMD of the volume.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue up 34% YoY to INR2,102 crores; H1 FY27 revenue up 31% to INR3,999 crores
items.quote: Q2 FY '27 revenue increased 34% year -on-year to INR2,102 crores. EBITDA rose 12% year-on-year to INR340 crores and PAT increased 3% year-on-year to INR167 crores.

items.statement: Joint venture IOAGPL network: 1,185 CNG stations, 14.31 lakh PNG households, 12,925 industrial/commercial connections, 29,156 inch-km pipeline
items.quote: Along with our joint venture partner, IOAGPL, our Pan -India network reaches 1,185 CNG stations, 14.31 lakh PNG household connections, 12,925 industrial and commercial connections, which are connected with a strong pipeline network of 29,156 inch-kilometer.
