items.quote: So we should see somewhere Q1 of next year time frame, more normalizing. But also at the same time, we are growing at 50%. So more FAIs, our first article. So we'll have to bring in. So I think we'll end up maintaining as we have guided about 120 days is what we want to shoot at, and that's where we ought to be around, in and around that number.

items.statement: Borrowings increased INR1,576 million in H1; net debt to equity 0.5x vs 0.2x at March end; planning INR800 crore term loans to support capex
items.quote: Borrowings increased by INR1,576 million to fund capacity expansion and capability enhancement across aerospace and consumer. As a result, net debt to equity stood at 0.5x compared to 0.2x at March end.

items.statement: Promoter group committed INR6,500 million preferential warrants; external equity fundraise still possible in FY28 to support 2031 growth trajectory
items.quote: We see the significant capital requirement is going to be there still for our growth, what we have seen laid out in aerospace itself. And because we have given an overall guidance of 4 to 6x growth in 2031. So that does require capital requirement.

items.statement: Proposed amalgamation of three wholly-owned subsidiaries not approved under fast-track route; evaluating next steps; no material impact on operations
items.quote: The scheme was not approved under the fast-track route on technical grounds, and we are evaluating the appropriate next steps. This is an internal restructuring matter and has no material impact on ongoing business operations.

items.statement: Reenah Joseph joined as CFO with nearly 2 decades experience across corporate finance, capital markets, M&A and investor relations
items.quote: I would like also to welcome Reenah Joseph, who has joined us as our Chief Financial Officer. Reenah brings in nearly 2 decades of experience across the corporate finance, capital markets, M&A and investor relations.

items.statement: Consumer ramp slower than expected due to longer qualification cycles, supply chain constraints, weather-related logistics disruption; recalibrating profitability timeline
items.quote: The direction has been right. Our processes are maturing and our customer relationships are deepening, but the ramp has taken longer than we expected and raw material shortages in toys has slowed it further. We are, therefore, recalibrating the milestone.

items.statement: Aerospace portfolio expanded to 5,978 products, added 238 parts in Q2 (up 4% sequentially)
items.quote: We added 238 parts in the quarter, up 4% sequentially, taking us to 5,978 products. Every new part widens our engagement with the customer.

items.statement: FY27 AUM growth guidance 25-30%, credit cost 3.5-4%, NIM 14.25-14.75%, opex 8.25-8.75%, ROA 4-4.5%
items.quote: At the start of the year, we guided for AUM growth of 25% to 30%, credit cost of 3.5% to 4%, net interest margin of 14.25% to 14.75%, and operating expenses of 8.25% to 8.75%, yielding a return on asset of 4% to 4.5%, and these are return on total assets.

items.statement: 3-year vision targets 28-33% AUM CAGR and ROA 4-4.5%
items.quote: Beyond this year, our focus remains on building a stronger and more sustainable lending franchise in line with the 3-year vision that we had shared in July, which essentially targets 28% to 33% AUM growth CAGR, return on assets of 4% to 4.5%.

items.statement: Steady demand in core micro-MSME segments; festive pick-up expected in H2
items.quote: The grassroot micro-MSME segment in India is showing a steady momentum supported by government initiatives for increasing formalization, and we continue to see this constructive demand in our markets for working capital across our core segments.

items.statement: Q2 NIM 15.6% vs guidance 14.25-14.75%; upside from lower rate hikes and rating upgrade
items.quote: Net interest margin was 15.6%, comfortably above our full-year guidance of 14.25% to 14.75%.

items.statement: Blended cost of borrowing fell 15 bps to 10.63%; incremental cost 10.04%
items.quote: The overall blended cost of borrowing also, not only the incremental cost, but blended cost overall has declined 15 basis points to 10.63% in Q2 FY27 as compared to 10.78% in quarter 1.

items.statement: AUM INR 7,597 cr, up 26% YoY and 4% QoQ; disbursements INR 1,403 cr, up 10% YoY and 15% QoQ
items.quote: Our assets under management stood at INR7,597 crores, which is up 26% year-on-year and 4% quarter-on-quarter, keeping us within our full-year guidance of 25% to 30% growth. Against this backdrop, our disbursements for Q2 FY27 stood at INR1,403 crores, up 10% year-on-year and 15% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: H1 FY27 disbursements INR 2,622 cr, up 15% YoY; 49,000 new borrowers added in Q2
items.quote: This took our first half FY27 disbursements to 2,622 crores, which is 15% up year-on-year. Historically, the first half year typically accounts for around 40% of our annual disbursements.

items.statement: 30+ new branches to open in Q3 FY27; 35-40 new branches and 30-40 splits planned for FY27
items.quote: In quarter 3, 30-plus new branches will also become operational, and this will further add fillip to our disbursements, and this is as per plan.

items.statement: GNPA 4.20% (-30 bps QoQ, -70 bps YoY); PAR X 6.94% (-7 bps QoQ, -109 bps YoY); target PAR X <6.5% by year-end
items.quote: Our GNPA has now declined for seven consecutive quarters and stood at 4.20% as of September 2026. This is 30 basis points lower than the last quarter and 70 basis points lower year-on-year. PAR X stood at 6.94%, which is down 7 basis points sequentially and 109 points year-on-year from the 8.03% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Credit cost 3.82% (-21 bps QoQ, -119 bps YoY), within guided 3.5-4% range; expect to trend toward 3.5% by year-end
items.quote: On the credit costs, our credit costs for the quarter came in at 3.82%, which is an 21 basis points improvement from 4.03% in quarter 1, and 119 basis points year-on-year. We are now within our FY27 guided range for credit costs where we had guided for 3.5% to 4%.

items.statement: Collection efficiency: non-OD 99.2%, Bucket 1 52.8%; large states Bihar, UP, Rajasthan performing well
items.quote: Collections remained healthy, with overall non-OD collection efficiency at 99.2% and Bucket 1 collection efficiency at 52.8%.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 41%; sufficient for ~2 years growth without fresh equity; bank borrowing share up to 35%
items.quote: With a capital adequacy of 41%, as we mentioned last quarter, our current capital is sufficient to support our growth for around the next 2 years without needing fresh equity.

items.statement: Borrowed INR 1,100 cr in Q1 and INR 1,200 cr in Q2; no funding challenges despite rate hikes
items.quote: If I look at the quarter one and quarter two, our borrowings are actually going up. So, quarter one, we borrowed near to INR1,100 crores; quarter two, we've borrowed closer to INR1,200 crores.

items.statement: Opex ratio fell 32 bps to 8.61% QoQ; cost-to-income 49%; AUM per employee up 18% YoY to 0.67 cr
items.quote: The operating expense ratio, which fell down to 8.61% in quarter 2 versus 8.93% in quarter 1, so in a single quarter, we have seen a 32 basis points reduction in operating expense ratio. This is the reason our cost-to-income has reduced to 49%.

items.statement: Insurance commission impact absorbable via 50 bps opex improvement, 10-25 bps credit cost drop, 25 bps funding cost benefit next year
items.value: 50 bps opex, 10-25 bps credit cost, 25 bps funding cost
items.quote: Roughly 50 basis points in OER, 25 basis points in interest rate, and another 10 basis points to 25 basis points in credit costs. This is much more than the impact of the interest rate on our books.

items.statement: Cattle portfolio 25-28% of AUM; underwritten with high-yielding cattle (4-6 min) and strict verification; performing better than rest of book
items.quote: We still don't want to aggressively grow the cattle book, because cattle book is very easy to grow, but we believe that we want to still maintain that diversification, which is diversified into multiple states, and hold ourselves in the 25% to 27%, 28% range.

items.statement: Gold loan pilot planned in select branches in existing cities; targeting 20% existing customers with gold loans; North India focus initially
items.quote: On gold loans, we realize that our existing micro-enterprise customer, almost 20% of them have some gold loan either before we lent to them or even after we lent to them. So, that's a market that we want to retain and increase our share of wallet with the customer.

items.statement: MFI overlap 8-9% at borrower level, 30-32% at household level; FOIR includes all household liabilities
items.quote: If you look at a individual primary borrower level, the MFI overlap would be about 8%-9%. But because in the loan structure, we do add co-applicants, would be female member of the family, so when you look at a group level or at a family level, the MFI exposure or people who would have an MFI loan would be in the range of about 30-odd percentage to 32-odd percentage.

items.statement: Dominant in hypothecation loans with pricing power; no significant competition; mortgage foreclosure rising to 22-23% due to vintage
items.quote: We don't believe that we'll have to do that. Yes, the benefit that we might have passed on to the customer will not happen that early. And as I mentioned, that we clearly see a 50 basis points operating expense ratio addition accretion in the next year, 10 to 25 basis points credit costs, and 25 basis interest cost benefit, so these will, in a way, work for us without having to reprice our loans.

items.statement: Loan officer productivity 4.85 loans/month vs 4.2 last year; target 5 loans/month for FY27
items.quote: This year, we had targeted a productivity per loan officer for the hypothecation loan at about five loans per month, which was 4.2 files in the previous financial year. Right now, for the last quarter, we had a productivity of 4.85 compared to last financial year quarter 2, where the productivity was hovering at about four files also.

items.statement: Employee growth budgeted 12-15% for FY27; hiring focused on collections, credit, and new branches; 5-7% more staff in H2
items.quote: For this financial year, we had budgeted for an employee growth between 12% to 15%. Now, most of the employee count goes into three verticals. One is on the distribution side, which is ideally addition of new branches as well as splitting of new branches that will happen in the second part of the financial year.

items.statement: Monitoring draft insurance commission recommendations; no CGFMU or Nat Cat insurance for drought protection (only INR 200-300 cr under CGFMU)
items.quote: We have, in any case, looked at various ways of insuring our book, including the available CGFMU schemes, etcetera. And since our loss rate is not very high and it's not very volatile, we find that insuring the entire book is not a preferred option, because that will end up not being accretive to our ROA.

items.statement: Slowed disbursements in drought-affected districts in Maharashtra, Karnataka, MP (18% of AUM); monitoring non-OD collection and bounce rates
items.quote: Together, these states account for about 18% of our AUM, and we have consciously slowed our disbursements in some of these districts, as we believe that in lending discretion should be a better part of valor.

items.statement: Mortgage PAR X up ~1% QoQ to ~6%; identified slippages in MP and Gujarat branches; tightened credit policies
items.quote: On the mortgage front, we have seen that PAR X has jumped by about 1% in the last one quarter, but still the PAR X levels of mortgage today are trending at about 6%, lower than the hypothecation loan, which should be the case, and significantly better than the overall industry averages that we are tracking.

items.statement: ROA 4.0% in Q2 vs 3.7% in Q1; H1 ROA 3.89%, ROE 12.32%; target ROE high teens to low 20s at 4.5x leverage
items.quote: These improvements have resulted in the ROA, and return on total assets, improving to 4% in quarter 2 compared to 3.7% in quarter 1.

items.statement: PPOP INR 198 cr (+54% YoY, +11% QoQ); PAT INR 87 cr (+151% YoY, +16% QoQ); H1 PAT INR 162 cr (+148% YoY)
items.quote: Pre-provision operating profit grew to a 54% year-on-year and 11% quarter-on-quarter to INR198 crores. This translated into stronger profitability, with profit after tax of INR87 crores, which is up 151% year-on-year and up 16% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Mutual fund quarterly average AUM at INR 13.14 lakh crore, up 10% YoY
items.quote: Our mutual fund quarterly average AUM stood at INR 13.14 lakh crore s, registering 10% Y -o-Y growth compared to INR 12 lakh crores in the same quarter last year

items.statement: Active equity QAAUM grew 9% YoY to INR 8.99 lakh crore
items.quote: As on September 30, 2026, our active quarterly average AUM was INR 8.99 lakh crores, reflecting 9% year-on-year increase

items.statement: Passive QAAUM at INR 4.15 lakh crore, up 11% YoY, largest passive manager
items.quote: On passive front, we remain the largest passive asset manager with quarterly average AUM of INR 4.15 lakh crore, up by 11% year-on-year

items.statement: AIF QAAUM at INR 7,437 crore, up 27% YoY
items.quote: Our AIF platform continues to scale well, with QAAUM at INR 7,437 crores, reflecting 27% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: SIP AUM rose to INR 2.07 lakh crore with 15% YoY growth
items.quote: Our SIP AUM rose to INR 2.07 lakh crore s with a 15% year -on-year increase

items.statement: Monthly SIP inflows steady at about INR 3,900 crore
items.quote: Monthly SIP inflows continue to remain steady at about INR 3,900 crores.

items.statement: Nearly 2/3rd of SIP inflows from B-30 markets
items.quote: Our strong presence across Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities is reflected in the healthy B-30 contribution, with nearly 2/3 rd of SIP inflows originating from these markets

items.statement: Gross margins across equity, debt, liquid, passive remained stable; gross yields expanded YoY
items.quote: Gross margins across equity, debt, liquid, and passive strategies remained stable during the quarter, and there has been a continued expansion in gross yields on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Equity yield ~62-63 bps, debt yield ~34-35 bps, liquid yield ~11-12 bps in Q2 FY27
items.value: 62-63 bps equity, 34-35 bps debt, 11-12 bps liquid
items.quote: In Q2 FY27, equity yield would be closer to about 62-63 bps on an average, our debt yields are in the range of about 34-35 bps and liquid around 11-12 bps.

items.statement: Invested in cloud infrastructure, AI-driven systems, and new data center going live in couple of months
items.quote: We are also coming up with our own data center, which is going live in a couple of months. Some of these costs would get moderated as we move our cloud instance to an on-prem instance.

items.statement: Appointed dedicated business head for AIF practice; significant hiring in Q2, moderation expected in Q3
items.quote: To further strengthen and deepen our AIF capabilities, we have also added a dedicated business head for the AIF practice, bringing sharper focus to product expansion and institutional engagement.

items.statement: Recurring employee cost ~60% of Q2 increase; one-time costs 30-40% to moderate
items.quote: The cost structure which was one-time will go down by 30-40%. So, 60% will be kind of recurring.

items.statement: Revenue neutral from April 1 under new SEBI pricing methodology; no distribution commission change
items.quote: we already clarified in last quarter that 1 st April onwards, we are revenue neutral in terms of new pricing methodology of the regulator. So that has been already factored. There is no change in

items.statement: Launched 5 new products in Q2 including 1 SIF; Magnum Equity Ex-Top 100 Long Short Fund among largest in category
items.quote: During Q2, we launched five new products, including one SIF, further strengthening our overall product suite. Among the filed offerings, both the Magnum Equity Ex-Top 100 Long Short Fund, and SBI Balanced Hybrid Fund saw stronger investor responses.

items.statement: SIF market share ~16%+; 2 of 6 SEBI-approved SIFs launched; more Cat II and Cat III AIFs planned
items.quote: We have about 16%-plus market share in that segment and continues to grow. We have only launched two funds till now and we still have 4 more to go out of the total 6 SEBI-approved options.

items.statement: SBI channel contributes ~20% of net inflows, stable vs last quarter
items.quote: So SBI channel contributes to around 20% of the net inflows, which is also like the same level as AUM, similar in the last quarter as well.

items.statement: 94% transactions digital; InvesTap has 4.3M registered users; 1.4M+ monthly digital transactions
items.quote: Today, 94% of our transactions are done digitally, supported by stronger adoption across InvesTap, Mitra, and partner platforms. InvesTap h as grown into one of the largest digital investing apps in the industry, with over 4.3 million registered users. Monthly digital volumes now exceed 1.4 million

items.statement: Industry QAAUM at INR 87.5 trillion, up 13% YoY; monthly SIP inflows at record INR 32,490 crore
items.quote: Mutual fund quarterly average AUM expanded by 13% year-on-year and 5% sequentially as on 30th September 2026, touching INR 87.5 trillion at the end of September 30. Monthly SIP inflows continued to show strength despite market volatility and touched all -time record high of INR 32,490 crore s in September'26

items.statement: Industry unique customers at 6.3 crore, up 11% YoY
items.quote: Industry continued to have a positive new customer addition, reaching up to 6.3 crores unique customers, an increase of 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: SEBI proposed mutual fund-only PMS effective April next year; SBIMF building fund selection team
items.quote: I think my understanding is that this kicks in April next year. And before that, we will be able to put a team together. And of course, this is a product solution that we will be part of in coming days.

items.statement: Investor sentiment shifting to safety; SIPs and hybrid schemes seeing higher demand amid volatility
items.quote: In the last quarter, when the market has been volatile and not meeting anyone's expectations, there is a safety feeling coming back to the customer's mind. This is why the SIP inflows are growing. Although markets are quite volatile and I think you can also look at point-to-point NIFTY is coming down with YTD correction of 8.2%, SIP flows are still increasing.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating revenue INR 2,336 crore (+12% YoY); operating profit INR 1,797 crore (+11% YoY); PAT INR 1,566 crore
items.quote: For H1 FY27, operating revenue reached to INR 2,336 crores, up to 12% from INR 2,089 crores in the same period last year. Operating profit rose to INR 1,797 crores, compared to INR 1,626 crores in H1 FY26, an 11% increase. Profit after tax came in at INR 1,566 crores in H1 FY27.

items.statement: Distribution network: 136,000 partners including 125,000 IFAs, 10,000 national distributors, 96 banking partners, 23,000+ SBI branches, 297 own branches; covers 98% pin codes
items.quote: We continue to maintain one of the largest distribution networks in the industry, supported by nearly 136,000 distribution partners. This includes over 125,000 independent financial advisors, over 10,000 national distributors, and over 96 banking partners, including State Bank of India, supplemented by 23,000+ SBI branches and 297 SBI Funds Management branches. This extensive reach enables us to s

items.statement: AIF business building private equity and private credit teams; will become significant top-line and bottom-line contributor in coming years
items.quote: We are looking at the private equity and private credit space more closely by building a team of few selected individuals. We have already filed with the exchange that we have appointed a new head of alternate in our company and building a strong team to drive alternatives in both private equity and private credit. I cannot give exact numbers right now, but in the coming years, this will be one of

items.statement: No capital allocation to AIF as subsidiary yet; starting as own division for some years
items.quote: We are not looking at capital allocation like a subsidiary kind of thing. We are starting with our own division for some years. On ce it is a full-fledged kind of business unit, then we will think of a substantial capital allocation

items.statement: FY27 leasing target of 6.5 million sq ft, representing 30% growth over FY26
items.quote: We had set ourselves a very ambitious leasing target of 6.5 million square feet for this fiscal year 2027, representing a 30% growth to the previous fiscal 2026.

items.statement: FY27 development target of 6 million sq ft, with nearly 50% achieved in H1
items.quote: We delivered six new buildings spanning 1.8 million square feet, taking our total development completions to 2.7 million square feet in the first half, having already achieved nearly 50% of our fiscal 27 development target, and very confident that we are on track to deliver the 6 million square feet this fiscal.

items.statement: Contracted revenue run rate crossed INR1,000 crores
items.quote: So that's what I put in my INR1,000 odd crores, the INR1,004 crores of revenue guidance that we are giving on a contracted basis is effectively on the 94% occupancy that we have on our stabilized assets.

items.statement: In-city portfolio to deliver ~6 million sq ft over next 3-4 years at 2x-3x rental premium to big format parks
items.quote: We expect this portfolio to deliver approximately 6 million square feet over the next 3 to 4 years, while also benefiting from the rental levels that are typically 2x to 3x of those of the big format parks.

items.statement: Value-added services ecosystem to contribute 5-10% of future revenues over time
items.quote: Over time, I believe these businesses can contribute anywhere between 5% to 10% of the revenues -- our future revenues.

items.statement: Demand for Grade A industrial/logistics space remains extremely robust driven by flight to quality, industrialization, and consumption
items.quote: Demand for grade A industrial and logistics spaces remains extremely robust, driven by the three structural mega trends that we discussed on our first quarter earnings as well. First, the flight to quality, second, the industrialization, and third, the

items.statement: Industrial customers accounted for >80% of H1 FY27 leasing, up from ~2/3 in FY26
items.quote: Importantly, more than 80% of our first-half leasing came from industrial customers, which again underscores the strength of this particular segment.

items.statement: Leased 2.5 million sq ft in Q2 FY27 across 14 transactions; 4.4 million sq ft in H1 FY27 across 27 transactions
items.quote: Your company leased 2.5 million square feet in the second quarter alone across 14 unique transactions and we onboarded eight new customers to our family.

items.statement: Re-leased 1.2 million sq ft in H1 FY27 at 12% spread
items.quote: We've also improved 1.2 million square feet of re-leasing at a very healthy 12% spread, which further re-emphasizes the continued rental growth that we are seeing in institutional-grade real estate.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 81%, sustained above 80%
items.quote: EBITDA margins continue to remain strong at 81%.

items.statement: Operational area ~31.5 million sq ft; stabilized occupancy 94% excluding ~1 million sq ft recent completions
items.quote: Today we stand at about 31.5 million square feet of completed assets, give or take. Of that, our stabilized occupancy is nearly 94%.

items.statement: Fully paid land bank supports ~30 million sq ft future development (29 million sq ft precise)
items.quote: Today, we have further development potential of nearly 30 million square feet, 29 million to be precise.

items.statement: Weighted average in-place rent ~INR27/sq ft; incremental big format park rents INR30-35/sq ft; in-city rents 2x-3x big format
items.quote: Today we are already at about INR27 of weighted average range across our portfolio. Incrementally, we are seeing this at anywhere between a INR30 to INR35 range on a big format parks.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR2,765 cr as of Sep 2026 from INR4,967 cr at Jun 2026 post-IPO
items.quote: We have now brought it down to INR2765 crores as at the end of September, which when compared to was at INR4,967 crores as at June 30th, 2026.

items.statement: Refinanced INR635 cr facility at 71 bps lower cost; avg debt cost ~8.2%
items.quote: during this quarter, your company refinanced an existing INR635 crore s facility, resulting in a 71 basis point reduction in borrowing

items.statement: Raised INR1,650 cr in Dec 2025 and INR2,600 cr in Aug 2026 via IPO to repay INR4,000 cr debt
items.quote: We had raised about INR16 -- INR1,650 crores in December of the previous year. We raised INR2,600 crores in August this year. The intent was to repay our INR4,000 crores of debt.

items.statement: Contracted revenue run rate INR1,004 cr; pro forma cash PAT H1 FY27 INR248 cr
items.quote: On a pro forma basis, and after reflecting the benefit of lower interest cost from the deleveraging, the cash PAT for H1 stood at INR248 crores.

items.statement: Onboarded 8 new customers in Q2 FY27; 17 new customers in H1 FY27; >40% leasing from existing customers
items.quote: We signed 27 new leases in the first half, of which about 10 were with our existing customers, but we also onboarded 17 new customers.

items.statement: Customer base diversified across geographies (Europe, US, Asia, India) and sectors (renewables, EVs, auto, data centers, semiconductors, aerospace, defense)
items.quote: We're seeing customers onboarding from Europe, we're seeing Indian customers, we're seeing American customers, we're seeing Asian customers.

items.statement: CWC litigation sub judice; last hearing Jan 2026; court allowed continued development
items.quote: The last hearing on this actually happened in Jan 2026. Since then matters continue to be deferred. One good point was that at the last detailed hearing in Jan 2026 that had occurred, the court had very clearly said that in the interim, they are not -- they are not stopping any further development that we are doing on these assets.

items.statement: Q3 leasing closures may slow due to festivities (Diwali) and global year-end shutdowns
items.quote: Third quarter typically sees a little bit of slowdown with the festivities, both Indian and international, Diwali coming up and you'll obviously see a shutdown in the global markets from mid-December to early January.

items.statement: Rooftop solar potential 150-200 MW on 30M sq ft; currently 38 MW operational/under implementation
items.quote: 30 million square feet today effectively allows me to build anywhere between 150 megawatt to 200 megawatt. We've even allowed to play out the entire roof spaces. But given the constraints that we have regulatory and in terms of open accesses, today we are at about 38 megawatt of operational capacity which are

items.statement: Lease expiry profile: ~700,000-800,000 sq ft remaining in FY27; ~2 million sq ft in FY28; WALE ~6.5-7 years
items.quote: In the fiscal '27, the 6 more months to go, we're looking at about 7,000, 800,000 square feet of more expiries coming up. The next fiscal we have a little bit over 2 million.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR of 40-45% expected for FY27, FY28, FY29 vs FY26 base
items.quote: So, for FY27, '28 and '29, we expect a CAGR growth of between 40%-45%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth of 40-45% year-on-year versus March 2026
items.quote: For FY27 we expect a growth between 40-45% when compared to March 26.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expansion of 80-120 bps over next 4-6 quarters
items.quote: Over the next 4-5 quarters, we expect about 80-120 bps increase in our EBITDA margins over a period of next 4-6 quarters.

items.statement: Gold price assumed constant at Rs 50,000 per gram (24-karat) for revenue guidance
items.quote: Estimating a 40% to 50% revenue CAGR growth for the next two years, we have taken the gold price to be constant at a rate of 24-karat rate of Rs. 50,000.

items.statement: Hyderabad manufacturing facility commenced operations in September 2026, spread across ~6,700 sq ft
items.quote: One of the key developments during the period was the commencement of our in-house manufacturing facility in Hyderabad in September 2026. The facility, spread across approximately 6,700 square feet, marks an important step in strengthening our internal manufacturing capabilities.

items.statement: Hyderabad facility capacity: 1.5 tonnes annually at single shift, up to 2.5 tonnes at double shift
items.quote: Our current manufacturing facility at a single shift basis can manufacture about 1.5 tonnes annually. And working at a double shift, it can go up to 2.5 tonnes annually.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing volume ramp-up: Q1 13%, Q2 21%, Q3 ~40%, Q4 ~50% of total volume
items.quote: In the 1st Quarter a total of 65 kgs which is 13% of our total volume has been processed in the facility. In the 2nd Quarter this has expanded to 167 kgs which is about 21% of our total volume processed. In the 3rd Quarter we expect this percentage to be close to 40% and in the 4th Quarter we expect it to be around 50%.

items.statement: Long-term target in-house vs outsourced manufacturing mix of 65:35
items.quote: As a company in the long run we feel the ideal ratio to be 65%-35% wherein 65% of the goods to be manufactured in-house and 35% of the goods to be outsourced.

items.statement: Sales office opened in Vijayawada; second sales office planned in Chennai in December (Q3); third in Bangalore in April-May
items.quote: With the success that we got in Vijayawada, we plan to replicate the same by opening an office in Chennai in the month of December and another office in Bangalore in the month of April-May.

items.statement: Shift from invoice sales to job work due to retail customers exchanging old gold instead of cash purchases, driven by gold price rise and PM's appeal
items.quote: As you say, our company has seen a slight fall in the sales through invoice basis because of the fact that the customers at the retail level have shifted their purchase from cash purchase to old gold. So, as our customers, mean as our clients who are th e retailers are getting more of old gold and not cash, they are forced to purchase in the form of job work through us

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 7.24% (down YoY) due to higher plain gold and 18K mix; H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 7.95%
items.quote: For the 2nd Quarter of the Financial Year 2027, revenue from operations grew 25% YoY to INR 626 crores. EBITDA stood at INR 45 crores, registering a YoY growth of 17% with EBITDA margins at 7.24%.

items.statement: Job work realization fell ~11% YoY (Rs 202 to Rs 178/gram) due to SKU mix shift to plain gold, not pricing change
items.quote: If we compare our Rs. 202 in the 2nd Quarter of last fiscal year, my job work, my realization has come down to 178. So, this is about 11% fall. So, this is mainly because of shift towards more of plain gold sales and not studded jewelry sales.

items.statement: AI platform monetization will reflect in marketing services revenue line

items.statement: Lender resuming DLG after six quarters may relate to RBI guidelines allowing offset against credit losses
items.quote: our sense is it may also have to do with certain RBI guidelines with respect to, they can offset that against credit losses and so on.

items.statement: EBITDA expected to continue expanding next quarter despite DLG drag; absolute EBITDA to grow quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: we don't think that we're looking at EBITDA going down next quarter. We do think EBITDA will continue to go up next quarter despite this drag.

items.statement: Higher capex in first half will increase depreciation in FY28; investments driven by strong payback on engagement, retention, financial services revenue
items.quote: with the lag in FY28 and so on, there will be more depreciation, but it is all being done for a specific purpose, which is higher engagement, higher retention, higher financial services revenue.

items.statement: Sales team additions are for same Soundbox category; new hires undergo training and retention jobs before deployment

items.statement: Believes upwards of 10 million of 16 million device merchants are good-quality and creditworthy; lending threshold based on aging and minimum daily earnings (~Rs 500/day)
items.quote: I personally see on a base of 16 million, we believe that upwards of 10 million are definitely good-quality merchants.

items.statement: Indirect expenses target to grow at less than half of contribution margin growth over 3-4 quarters; free cash flow to track EBITDA with capex guidance next quarter
items.value: less than half of revenue growth
items.quote: our indirect expenses, including higher expenses in marketing and sales and service and cloud expenses, et cetera, should over a three to four quarter period, grow at less than half of revenue growth, right?

items.statement: Merchant loan ECL range largely unchanged; personal loans are distribution only; cautious underwriting with over a dozen lending partners of 3-5 years tenure
items.quote: on a merchant loan, we do give ECL data. It is largely unchanged in terms of the range that we get. Personal loans, of course, is a distribution business only.

items.statement: Eligible GMV mix not changing dramatically; small merchant business growing very fast; online business growing fast post-embargo; enterprise improving via EMI/DCC offerings
items.quote: the mix is not changing dramatically because obviously where Paytm has unique strengths is in the small merchant business, which is growing very, very fast.

items.statement: Depreciation YoY not up much; higher capex in H1 for engagement, retention, financial services monetization; payback visible on service costs and capex
items.quote: we have done more capex in the first half than we did previously. So with the lag in FY28 and so on, there will be more depreciation.

items.statement: AI models built in-house, not rented; enables precise customer acquisition targeting; CFO invited to Cursor global council as 4th most optimum coding model user globally
items.quote: Our models are made by us. Our models are not third-party. This is a very important sentence. We are not renting intelligence from outside. We make our own models.

items.statement: Online payment business growing fast after August 2023 embargo lift; enterprise business improving via EMI, DCC, greater distribution; gaining share across board
items.quote: Online, as you know, we were under embargo until August of last year. Starting at the beginning of this year, we are seeing good hunting opportunities.

items.statement: PCTL used for overseas venture investments (UAE, Luxembourg); not for device refurbishment capex; PAT jumped 7x YoY to Rs 84 crores but operations not significant
items.quote: PCTL is an entity through which we make investments in some foreign ventures. So, for example, we had announced the setting up of a business in the UAE. We have announced the subsidiary in Luxembourg.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expected to remain soft and trail FY26 levels; EBITDA margin guided at 25-30% for FY27 with scope for improvement in Q4
items.quote: To sum up, we expect FY27 revenue will remain soft and to trail last year's levels. This reflects cautious client spending amid global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin to remain in guided range of 25% to 30% for FY27 with scope for improvement in Q4 as recent wins ramp up
items.quote: Hence, we expect the EBITDA margin to remain in our guided range of 25% to 30% for FY27 ,with a scope for improvement in Q4 as the recent wins ramp up.

items.statement: Revenue impacted by cautious spending environment and ramp-down at a couple of large enterprise clients
items.quote: Our revenue was impacted by a cautious spending environment and a ramp down at a couple of large enterprise clients.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 25.7% down from 30.3% QoQ and 30.4% YoY due to revenue decline offset by cost optimization and AI productivity
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 9.7 crores with a margin of 25.7% compared to 30.3% in the last quarter and 30.4% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Secured market wins across diversified sectors including banking in South America, UK, Europe, global ports, and education in Australia; three Q2 wins in banking
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured market wins across diversified sectors , and our key technology offerings include banking in South America, banking in the U.K., banking in Europe, global ports, and education industry in Australia.

items.statement: IT services contribute 98.4% of revenue; geographical mix: North America 59%, India 20%, Europe 6%, Australia 4%, rest of world 11%
items.quote: In terms of business mix, IT services continue to be our core business, contributing 98.4% of revenue. Our geographical mix remained diversified, with 80% of revenue coming from overseas markets.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contribute 50% of revenue; BFSI client count around 11-12; one Middle East client increased business; North America clients returning with AI requirements
items.quote: Our top 10 clients contributed 50% of the revenue.

items.statement: Debt-free balance sheet with cash and bank balance of INR 17.6 crores as of 30th September 2026; focus on disciplined working capital management and cash conversion
items.quote: On cash and balance sheet, we continue to remain a debt -free balance sheet, maintain a debt -free balance sheet with a cash and bank balance of INR 17.6 crores as of 30th September 2026.

items.statement: Board declared second interim dividend of INR 1 per share, taking H1 total interim dividend to INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT)
items.quote: The Board has also declared a second interim dividend of INR 1 per share, taking our total interim dividend for H1 to INR 5 per share, which is about 72% of our H1 profit after tax.

items.statement: Headcount reduced ~10% from 550 to ~495-500; 100% engineers Claude certified; AI enabling 2-3x productivity per person; minimal hiring this year
items.quote: You can say adjustment plus a few resources they left because they got other opportunity. And we were able to manage those losses with the help of AI. So , this year, even we have not done recruitment, I can say compared to last year, 5%- 10% maximum.

items.quote: So in Australia, we have opened a sales office, particularly for local client contracts and bidding purposes. Employees' complete team is based out in India only.

items.statement: AI-led productivity improvements and cost optimization offset revenue decline; rationalized headcount and deployed AI extensively across delivery

items.statement: Revenue per employee and utilization key focus for H2; deploying engineers across platforms using AI to raise output per person
items.quote: A key priority for H2 is to drive higher utilization and revenue per employee by deploying our engineers across platforms, using AI to raise output per person, and filling capacity from our existing team before adding new hires.

items.statement: FY27 revenue softness reflects cautious client spending amid global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty; client-specific ramp-downs and billing seasonality to influence near-term performance
items.quote: Going ahead, client -specific ramp-downs, macroeconomic uncertainty , and billing seasonality will continue to influence the near -term performance.

items.statement: Achieved Select Partner status in both Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI Partner Networks; upgraded to Frappe Bronze Partner in India; 100% engineers Claude certified

items.statement: Management does not provide forward-looking revenue or EBITDA forecasts but sees sustained growth momentum and healthy order pipeline
items.quote: We don't give the forecasting and the you know I would say forward looking numbers but what we are seeing in the market today is there is a sustained growth momentum for us.

items.statement: Demand remains healthy across all industry segments except healthcare compliance
items.quote: we work across multiple industries, I have mentioned BFSI, manufacturing, logistics, HR we have seen growth across all the segments, so it is hard to put a ﬁnger to a particular industry, we are growing well across all our clients

items.statement: Seven consecutive quarters of >6% sequential operating revenue growth; healthy order pipeline and demand
items.quote: One important factor is seven quarters of sequential operating revenue growth of 6 percent, over 6 percent quarter on quarter for last seven quarters.

items.quote: we have got a Claude Select Services partner status from Anthropic and we have more than a dozen certiﬁed cloud developers and a couple of forward deployed engineers who are certiﬁed with us

items.statement: Macro environment (Trump government) and visa norms not materially affecting business due to offshore-heavy model (<50 onsite employees out of ~1,900)

The ships are not coming there. And this is one aspect that we are watching, and we'll see the best that we can do in this period.

items.statement: Fujairah contributed INR250 crores EBITDA in FY26, INR134 crores in H1 FY26
items.quote: year, FY26, it was INR250 crores. This was primarily, I would say, 11 months of full operation and March, it was like temporarily down -- from March onwards, the downfall commenced

items.statement: Fujairah reported EBITDA loss of INR16 crores in H1 FY27 due to fixed overheads
items.quote: Escalations and all in Middle East, Fujairah Terminal contributed virtually no EBITDA during this period. And in fact, we have reported EBITDA loss of around close to INR16 crores in H1 on account of this international operations, primarily because of the fixed overheads sitting in the P&L.

items.statement: Cash position INR1,693 crores as of September 2026
items.quote: As of September 2026, we maintained a cash position of INR1,693 crores, underscoring one of the strongest balance sheets in the sector.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of INR6,400 crores invested in mutual funds and FDs, drawn down as capex spends
items.quote: No, because we have invested the funds which we have raised net of, I mean, INR6,400 crores was something which we realized net of all the charges, and that has been invested in mutual funds and fixed deposits. And as and when the capex spend keeps happening, drawdown will be happening from that fund.

items.statement: Finance cost INR108 crores in Q2 FY27 vs INR99 crores YoY
items.quote: Consolidated depreciation was INR175 crores, and finance cost was INR108 crores in the current quarter, as compared to INR149 crores and INR99 crores, respectively, in the previous quarter ended September '25.

items.statement: H2 finance cost broadly in line with H1, slight increase from ROU expense on finance lease rakes
items.quote: It will be broadly in line with what is there in H1 because whatever incremental borrowings are ongoing are all towards capex, wherein the interest cost is getting capitalized. Also for H2, there can be a slight increase in the inte rest cost on account of ROU spend because we have taken some rakes on these finance lease

items.statement: Subscribed INR40 crores equity capital in Oman project awaiting allotment
items.quote: Further update on Oman is in this quarter, we have subscribed to the equity capital by infusing INR40 crores waiting allotment.

items.statement: Fujairah operations disrupted, insurance claims pending war declaration by state
items.quote: No. See, claims are still being assessed by the insurance company. One is obv iously forensic study and all has been done on that. They are also awaiting for the state to declare whether it is a war or not. So that is one fundamental thing which the insurance agencies are awaiting

items.statement: Paradip Iron Ore volumes impacted by transportation moisture limit restrictions after ship sinking incident
items.quote: So actually, if you remember on August 22, ship sank of the coast of Paradip around 240 nautical miles of Paradip Port, carrying iron ore. This was not from our terminal, but it was carrying iron ore and it sank in the coast there. So after that, there's a concept called transportation moisture limit, which is applicable for iron ore traffic. So there has been very -- because of the rainy season.

items.statement: Logistics rake fleet target 267-270 rakes by 2030, fluid target linked to terminal additions
items.quote: So you see this is a fluid target. And our initial goal was to touch if you would have seen our earlier paper was around 157 for containe r rakes and around 110 for LSFTO rakes, broadly a number of around 267, 270 rakes. So these numbers are fixed on basis of the number of terminals that we start to get in place

items.statement: Full-year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 17-19%
items.quote: We are firmly on track to meet our full year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 17% to 19% and you will start seeing further improvements in the balance year.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 pre-sales growth guidance maintained at minimum 20%
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to achieve our full-year guidance of 20% minimum pre-sales growth, return on capital employed of 20% and our EBITDA margins for the year will range between 17% to 19% and the PAT margin will be 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Next 5-year pre-sales CAGR target of approximately 20%
items.quote: So, you can expect an approximately 20% CAGR as far as pre-sale is concerned over the next 5 years.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 pre-sales nearly doubled YoY without new launches
items.quote: We achieved a landmark milestone this quarter by nearly doubling our quarterly pre-sales without any new launches, driven entirely by robust sales velocity and steady price realizations within our existing product portfolio.

items.statement: H1 FY27 booking value increased 111% YoY to INR1,602 crores
items.quote: For the first half of the year, our cumulative c ollections have reached INR1, 233 crores and booking values increased by 111% year -on-year to INR1,602 crores

items.statement: H1 FY27 customer collections surged 67% to INR1,233 crores
items.quote: We also witnessed a 67% surge in customer collection to INR682 crores. This highlights our intense focus on cash flow efficiency and operational rigor. For the first half of the year, our cumulative c ollections have reached INR1, 233 crores

items.statement: Total portfolio GDV stands at approximately INR52,000 crores including INR8,500 crores added in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our total portfolio now stands at an impressive GDV of approximately INR52,000 crores, which includes what we have added in H1 of approximately INR8,500 crores in Parel.

items.statement: JDA projects account for 52% of total GDV portfolio with INR27,000 crores revenue potential
items.quote: Now, driven by our strategic pivot towards asset-light model, if we look at the JDA, JDA is now account for approximately 52% of our total GDV portfolio, which represents a revenue potential of INR27,000 crores at current prices.

items.statement: Two launches planned in H2 FY27 in Mahim with combined GDV of INR4,100 crores
items.quote: So, H2 will see two launches from us. Both of these launches are going to be in Mahim. The combined GDV of these projects is about INR4,100 crores approximately.

items.statement: Plan to add INR8,000-10,000 crores GDV annually through business development
items.quote: Given our strategy, there is a lot of interest that we have. As far as business development and GDV is concerned, going forward, if we add about INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores worth of GDV every year, it should give us this kind of a target easily.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 15% from 14% YoY
items.quote: And through an optimized product mix and disciplined cost management, our EBITDA also rose from 14% to INR115 crores with margins now at 15% as compared to 14% in the corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Margins expected to normalize progressively as more projects reach mid-stage
items.quote: While our margins naturally fluctuate by project phase due to upfr ont marketing and construction setup costs, they are expected to normalize progressively as more of our projects go in mid-stage as this year progresses and moves into next year also

items.statement: Q2 FY27 net debt at INR912 crores, gross debt at INR1,200 crores, debt-to-equity at 0.8x
items.quote: We closed the quarter with a net debt of INR912 crores and a gross debt of INR1,200-odd crores with a healthy debt-to-equity ratio of 0.8x.

items.statement: Debt expected to remain in INR1,200-1,500 crores range for next 1-2 years
items.quote: So, debt is a avenue we will definitely resort to and it will remain around this range, in the middle of INR1,200 crores to INR1,500 crores, I think I don't see any challenge in maintaining that kind of range, and it will still be within 1:1.

items.statement: Subsidiary raised INR210 crores from ICICI Prudential AMC AIF via OCPRS for Mahim project
items.quote: We are also very happy to share that Raymond Realty's subsidiary company has raised INR210 crores from AIF, which is promoted by ICICI Prudential AMC Limited.

items.statement: Promoter committed INR400 crores equity infusion, first tranche coming shortly
items.quote: Apart from that, the promoter himself has committed about INR400 crores of equity that he is infusing and the first tranche of that is going to be received shortly as per the schedule and balance will be as has been approved by the shareholders in their -- in the AGM.

items.statement: ICICI investment structured as equity with zero coupon OCPRS, no debt classification
items.quote: No, it will not reflect as debt. Bhavin Modi: Okay. Harmohan Sahni: Because it is dependent on the terms that you have agreed and our terms are that this is equ ity that we have got from ICICI. And only for ease of movement of cash flow, they have structured it as

items.statement: Construction costs fixed via fixed-price contracts with contingencies for ongoing projects
items.quote: But the projects which are under execution as of now, where contracts have already been given, there, these are all fixed price contracts, there is no provision of increases that anybody can ask for.

items.statement: Future projects will factor in cost inflation, partially passed to customers and partially absorbed
items.quote: The projects which will get launched in future will definitely have that impact. But we are factoring that in our planning and the way we are pricing them. So, part of it will get passed on to the customer and part of it we will absorb in our contingencies.

items.statement: Mid-market and above segment resilient to 25-50 bps rate hikes, lowest apartment INR1.5 crores
items.quote: Our lowest value apartment in Thane is not less than INR1.5 crore s and that's the lowest value and bulk of our inventory is in the category of about INR3.5 crores and onwards going all the way up to INR20 crores if we look at all the MMR inventory that we've

items.statement: Occupation certificate received for Address by GS 1 Tower B (270 units, 3.5 lakh sq ft) ahead of RERA timeline
items.quote: One of the features of that was receiving the occupation certificate for Address by GS 1 Tower B in Thane, which comprises 270 units and almost 3.5 lakh square feet. And this also has been delivered ahead of RERA completion timeline.

items.statement: All projects currently on time or ahead of schedule, no significant challenge to maintain track record
items.quote: Along with that, our operational intensity of committing to timely delivery and everywhere so far we have maintained before time delivery and going forward also all our projects are currently on time or ahead of schedule. We see no significant challenge in maintaining that track record going forward as well.

items.statement: Mature projects generating strong operating cash flows reinvested into new projects
items.quote: You will see that our existing mature projects continue to deliver strong operating cash flows, which is being reinvested into recently launched and new yet to be launched projects.

items.statement: New JDA projects cash flow negative for first 2 years, positive from year 3 onwards
items.quote: And as -- is typical for any new JDA project, it remains cash flow negative for the first 2 years due to upfront investments and then becomes cash flow positive from third year or middle of third year onwards.

items.statement: Current portfolio expected to generate INR10,000+ crores pre-tax cash flow over 4-5 years
items.quote: So, it is around INR10,000 crore s plus kind of pre-tax cash flow that will be getting generated from this current portfolio

items.statement: Expect to reach 150,000 to 155,000 desks by March 2027 and 190,000 to 200,000 desks eventually, with supply for FY28 and FY29 under negotiation
items.value: 150,000 to 155,000 desks by March 2027; 190,000 to 200,000 desks eventually
items.quote: We expect to reach about 150,000 to 155,000 by March of 2027 and on the way to about 190,000 to 200,000 seats, with supply for FY28 and FY29 already under negotiation.

items.statement: Added 11,700 desks in Q2 FY27, total 145,300 desks across 85 centres in 8 cities, up 27% YoY; 4,500 more desks added in October; 47,000 incremental desks secured via signed leases and LOIs
items.quote: We added nearly 11,700 desks in Q2, more than we've ever opened in a quarter, taking us to 145,300 desks across 85 centres in 8 cities, which is up 27% year-over-year, with about 18,400 added in the first half and about 4,500 more added in October.

items.statement: Members grew 32.5% YoY to 121,700, ahead of capacity growth; occupancy at 83.7% (up 357 bps YoY), mature centres at 88%; growth centres at 64.8% occupancy, up from 51.4% a year ago
items.quote: Members grew 32.5% to about 121,700, ahead of capacity, and occupancy grew 357 basis points year-over-year to about 83.7%, with mature centres at nearly 88%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 138 bps QoQ to 21.2% in Q2; centre-level EBITDA margin at 28.4% (up 109 bps YoY); H1 centre-level margin at 28.1% (up 284 bps); structural margin expansion driven by operating leverage and higher-margin VAS/digital re
items.quote: EBITDA grew 37.6% year-on-year and 17.8% quarter-on-quarter to INR162.9 crores, with margin expanding 138 basis points sequentially to 21.2%.

items.statement: VAS revenue grew 35% YoY to INR79.6 crores; digital revenue grew 46% to INR29.2 crores; combined VAS+digital at INR108.8 crores (up 38%), outpacing core revenue growth of 31.7%
items.value: INR79.6 crores VAS; INR29.2 crores digital; INR108.8 crores combined; 38% YoY growth
items.quote: The highlight of this quarter is the platform. VAS grew 35% year-on-year to INR79.6 crores, and digital 46% to INR29.2 crores. Together, they reached INR108.8 crores, up 38%, well ahead of 31.7% growth in our core business.

items.statement: Free cash flow from operations (FCFO) at INR237.7 crores in Q2 (1.5x EBITDA), up 149% YoY and 68% QoQ; H1 FCFO at INR379.8 crores (up 157% YoY), funding entire H1 capex of INR363.8 crores with INR16 crores surplus
items.quote: Free cash flow from operations, or FCFO, was INR237.7 crores this quarter, up 149% year-on-year and 68% on Q1, at 1.5 times EBITDA.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR23.1 crores as of September 2026, from net debt of INR310.5 crores a year ago; credit rating upgraded from A- to A+; average borrowing cost down 184 bps to 8.5%
items.value: INR23.1 crores net cash; A+ rating; 8.5% avg borrowing cost
items.quote: We closed September with a net cash of INR23.1 crores, compared with a net debt of INR310.5 crores a year ago. Our credit rating was upgraded from an A- to A+ over the year, and our average cost of borrowing fell 184 basis points to 8.5%.

items.statement: ROCE reached 34.5% in Q2 (up 590 bps QoQ, 1,235 bps YoY); H1 ROCE doubled to 31.1% despite 75% capex growth; PAT grew 67.4% YoY to INR65.8 crores (margin 8.6%, up 183 bps)
items.quote: ROCE reached 34.5%, up 590 basis points quarter-on-quarter and 1,235 basis points year-on-year. H1 ROCE doubled to 31.1% in a half in which capex grew 75%.

items.statement: Enterprises contribute 77% of core revenue, Fortune 500 ~30%, GCCs ~41%, other global cos ~26%; top 10 members at 23% of revenue; renewal rate 80-85% in H1; 50%+ of customer growth from existing members expanding
items.quote: Enterprises contribute 77% of core revenue, and Fortune 500 companies about 30%. GCCs account for nearly 41% of the overall mix, and with other global companies, about 26%. No sector or customer dominates, and our Top 10 members together are 23% of overall revenue.

items.statement: Platform revenue (VAS + digital) growing faster than core, at higher margins (digital ~80% EBITDA margin, VAS margin-accretive); customization revenue ~INR18 crores in Q2, ~INR30 crores in H1, amortized over contract terms
items.quote: Digital operates at close to 80% EBITDA margin, and VAS is margin accretive. So, as both keep growing faster than the core, they will continue contributing disproportionately to our profitability, all the way down to PAT.

items.statement: One large customer (Commonwealth Bank of Australia) may move out in next year to a 1.2M sq ft built-to-suit campus; timing uncertain but backfill and large contracts being pursued to offset churn
items.quote: we do have one company we have that might be moving out in the next year, but it is not fully certain right now in terms of timing, which month and things like that. But Commonwealth Bank of Australia, that's been a large customer of ours for nearly 7 years, has taken up a large built -to-suit campus with Embassy in Manyata itself of about 1.2 million

items.statement: Corporate action underway to eliminate book losses and enable dividends or buybacks; excess cash may be used for shareholder returns; promoter pledge reduction dependent on market cap recovery, not urgent given 3-year debt maturity and busi
items.quote: We've embarked on this corporate action of getting rid of our book losses or creating the ability for us to pay dividends or do buybacks. That is definitely one option that we're looking at if the business has excess cash.

items.statement: Branded workspace category (pioneered by WeWork) at 29M sq ft of India's 123M sq ft flex market; WeWork operates ~10M sq ft (26% of space, 34% of revenue); 96% unaided brand awareness vs 51% median for other operators
items.quote: Of India's billion-plus square feet of office space, F lex is about 123 million, organized F lex about 83 million, and organized branded workspace, a category we pioneered, about 29 million. We operate about 10 million square feet of WeWork-branded spaces, by our estimate about 26% of the space and 34% of the revenue

items.statement: NPS at +79; 16,000+ accounts; 30% of physical space users work across multiple formats; 27% buy services beyond the desk
items.quote: Our NPS is +79. More than 16,000 accounts work with us, and of those using our physical spaces, nearly 30% work across more than one format, moving from a day pass to a managed office floor without ever leaving the network.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 order booking increased 48% YoY to ₹126 crores; H1 FY27 order booking grew 95% YoY to ₹330 crores
items.quote: The order booking for Q2 FY27 increased by 48% to ₹126 crores compared to the corresponding previous quarter and for H1FY27, it stood at ₹330 crores, a growth of 95% YoY.

items.statement: Closing order book as of 30 September 2026 was ₹626 crores, up 57% from ₹398 crores a year earlier
items.quote: The closing order position on the 30th of September 2026 was ₹626 crores, up 57% from ₹398 crores a year earlier.

items.statement: Medium-term growth ambition is to deliver over 25% year-on-year CAGR over the next five to seven years
items.quote: Our growth ambition is certainly to deliver growth over a medium-term basis, let me say five-seven years basis of over 25% year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA margins were 36.1% in Q2 FY27 and 35.7% in H1 FY27; management aims to maintain EBITDA margins of 35% plus over the medium to long term
items.quote: EBITDA margins were 36.1% in Q2 FY27 and 35.7% in H1 FY27.

items.statement: Management does not expect defence growth to be margin dilutive; targets to maintain EBITDA margins of 35% plus
items.quote: in the medium to long -term, very happy that you asked. Again, I do not believe it to be margin dilutive. In fact, if anything, we would like to say that our growth ambition is to maintain our margins of 35% of EBITDA

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex was ₹41 crores (₹10 crores capitalisation, ₹31 crores CWIP); major capacity and capability investments largely completed; incremental capex expected to be balancing and routine only
items.quote: During H1FY27, the total capital expenditure was ₹41 crores, which comprises capitalisation of ₹10 crores and capital work in prog ress of ₹31 crores

items.statement: Total capex program of ₹340 crores (evenly split between gears and defence) is almost complete; supports production of approximately ₹700 crores based on gearbox mix
items.quote: The ₹340 crores CapEx is not just for gearboxes, but it is also for our defence facility. The total combined Cap ex offers us production of approximately ₹700 crores based on the mix, frankly speaking, of just gearboxes.

items.statement: Next capex expansion trigger expected at 80-85% capacity utilisation; not there yet
items.quote: If your question is what is the trigger for the next cycle of Cap ex, it would be when we are at about 80%, 85% capacity utili sation when we start looking at the next phase of Capex

items.statement: Domestic industrial environment supportive: India Q1 FY27 GDP grew 7.8%, industrial production up 8% YoY in August, manufacturing up 9%, capital goods output up 16.9%
items.quote: India's Q1 FY27 GDP grew at 7.8%, while industrial production grew 8% YoY in August with manufacturing up 9% and capital goods output up 16.9%.

items.statement: Global high-speed industrial gearbox market (OEM + aftermarket) estimated at $1.1 billion in 2026, growing 6-7% through 2033
items.quote: External industry research estimates the combined OEM and aftermarket ecosystem at approximately $1.1 billion in 2026, and the two segments expected to grow between 6% and 7% through 2033.

items.statement: India FY27 defence allocation ₹7.85 lakh crores, capital outlay ₹2.19 lakh crores (21.8% above FY26), ₹1.39 lakh crores earmarked for domestic procurement
items.value: ₹7.85 lakh cr total, ₹2.19 lakh cr capital, ₹1.39 lakh cr domestic
items.quote: India's FY27 Ministry of Defen ce allocation is ₹7.85 lakh crores. The capital outlay on Defen ce Services is ₹2.19 lakh crores, 21.8% above the fiscal ' 26 budget estimates. The government has earmarked ₹1.39 lakh crores for procurement for

items.statement: Aftermarket revenue grew 41% YoY in Q2 FY27 and 29% in H1 FY27, contributing 27% of H1 revenue
items.quote: Q2FY27 aftermarket revenues was up about 41% YoY, and the H1 FY27 was up 29%, contributing 27% to the revenue.

items.statement: Defence revenue scaled meaningfully from low base; order book now ~60% defence; lumpiness expected due to prototype, qualification, approval cycles
items.quote: given that defen ce has become now dominant part, almost 60% of our order book now

items.statement: Significant orders received from Middle Eastern and African customers in Q2 FY27; export order booking grew 3x from ₹12 crores in Q1 to ₹36 crores in Q2
items.quote: we've had a 3x increase in our order booking for ex port orders, which was ₹12 crores and went up to ₹36 crores

items.statement: Qualified across all Indian Navy tenders and shipyards for gearboxes, shafting, fin stabilizers via own tech and global partnerships
items.quote: As far as gearboxes and shafting and fin stabilizers are concerned, we have our project qualification across all tenders that are coming across from the Indian Navy and across all the shipyards.

items.statement: 7-9 global competitors (ex-China), mostly European; largest has ~15% market share; market share unchanged despite competitor presence in India
items.quote: We have between seven to nine competitors, not including China globally that we come across for our export orders. The majority of them are European based companies. The largest company would have a market share of about 15% odd from a global perspective.

items.statement: Compressor gear competition is primarily in Europe, not India; TPTL on AVLs of largest customers and seeing increasing OEM orders
items.quote: The real competition for compressors is Europe. And that is where we are now, not just on the AVL of the largest customers, but our OEMs are buying from us increasingly.

items.statement: Core working capital days improved to 188 days as of September end from 193 days in March; further improved by a couple of weeks in Q2
items.quote: Core working capital days stood at 188 days as of September end versus 193 days in March. It has improved further by a couple of weeks since some overdue receivables have been reali sed during this quarter

items.statement: Generated positive free cash flow after capex of approximately ₹13 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: We generated positive free cash flow after capital expenditure of approximately ₹13 crores in H1 FY27, while continuing to invest in manufacturing infrastructure.

items.statement: Balance sheet allows funding growth primarily through internal accruals; no significant further capex required for near-term growth targets
items.quote: We intend to remain disciplined on our timing and returns from these investments and currently have a balance sheet that allows us to fund the growth primarily through internal accruals.

items.statement: A few more headcount additions expected but small; hiring part of growth and profitability delivery
items.quote: A few more additions will happen, but it is going to be small in terms of those additions.

items.statement: H1 FY27 order inflow split: Product ₹132 crores, Aftermarket ₹64 crores, Defence ₹135 crores
items.value: Product ₹132 cr, Aftermarket ₹64 cr, Defence ₹135 cr
items.quote: In terms of product, the total order booking is ₹132 crores. Aftermarket is ₹64 crores and difference is ₹135 crores.

items.statement: Defence procurement policy (DPP) shifting to Make in India, Make for India; historically products imported, now focus on domestic sourcing
items.quote: Under the various DPPs, the move is towards Make in India, Make for India as well.

items.statement: Middle East capex cycle delayed due to geopolitical turbulence; orders progressing but timing uncertain; ADNOC placing more orders for pumps and compressors
items.quote: The turbulence that we've seen in the last three calendar quarters has been significant. I will not shy away from that. It has certainly been significant. It has created shock waves, frankly speaking, globally

items.statement: New product development milestones expected in next couple of quarters for global efficiency benchmarks in high-speed gearboxes; entering space and data centre gearbox segments
items.quote: We expect over the next couple of quarters significant milestones to be achieved in terms of really setting the benchmark for global efficiency as far as our high-speed gearboxes are concerned.

items.statement: Data centre and space gearbox solutions well within existing technology range (not large MW); team close to developing and selling solutions
items.quote: The team is close to have developing solutions and then selling those solutions that opens up a significant opportunity.

items.statement: Management targets pre-sales CAGR of close to 20% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, our strategic priority for the next two to three years would be to pursue growth within Mumbai city and to grow at a CAGR of close to 20%.

items.statement: Management endeavors 20-25% year-on-year pre-sales growth for FY27 and beyond
items.quote: Right. So, again, our endeavor would be in the range of 20% year-on-year.

items.statement: Target project-level blended EBITDA margins upwards of 25% sustained over next few years
items.quote: But on a blended average, the project level, our EBITDA margins should be upwards of 25%. And as the luxury segment or the mid-income segment continues to give us greater sales and greater velocities in the years to come, the product mix, we should be able to sustain our project margins at greater than 25% over the next few years.

items.statement: Target PAT margin of at least 15% and EBITDA margins close to 28%
items.value: PAT at least 15%, EBITDA close to 28%
items.quote: We are looking at a PAT of close to at least 15%. Siddhant Ludhaya: Oh, no. Subodh Subhash Runwal: I am talking about EBITDA margins close to 28

items.statement: External debt reduced from Rs 2,400 crore to Rs 1,900 crore post-IPO; target to reduce debt further
items.quote: Already it has come down to Rs. 1,900 crores as we speak. So that is the journey that we would endeavor to continue. And the objective is to reduce and get the debt as low as possible.

items.statement: IPO size reduced from Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 500 crore via SEBI one-time concession; primary offering only, no promoter OFS
items.quote: We believe that at this stage to fight the market from a valuation point of view would not be the right thing because it continues to and we are not diluting the fact that the promoters had not offered any share for as an OFS. It was all a primary offering.

items.statement: Cumulative sales of ongoing projects ~Rs 150,542 million; collections ~Rs 114,280 million; collectibles ~Rs 36,000 million
items.quote: On a total basis, all the running projects that we have currently, they have cumulatively achieved a sales of close to Rs. 150,542 million. And against that, we have a collection done already so far, which is roughly Rs. 114,280 million. So, this leaves us with a close to Rs. 36,000 million of collectibles from the sold area.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 pre-sales Rs 4,835 million (~0.35 msf), up ~5% YoY; collections Rs 5,754 million, up from Rs 4,993 million YoY
items.value: pre-sales Rs 4,835 million; collections Rs 5,754 million
items.quote: During quarter one, we recorded pre-sales of close to Rs. 4,835 million, which is close to 5% jump in comparison to Rs. 4,600 million that were reported in the corresponding quarter last year. Collections were also up from Rs. 4,993 million in quarter one of last year to around Rs. 5,754 million in this particular quarter.

items.statement: Enjoy 3-5% price premium over competitors in Dombivli and Kanjurmarg/Mulund; 7 Mahalaxmi prices at par with competition; expect premium to sustain
items.quote: So, at all these places historically and we have disclosed that in prospectus as well, we have enjoyed a differential price of close to 3% to 5% in comparison to our competitors. So, we have enjoyed a premium of close to 3% to 5% in these micro-markets.

items.statement: Gradual shift toward mid-income and luxury (Rs 50k-70k/sft) in South/West Mumbai; affordable share to decline; Dombivli transitioning to mid-income
items.quote: So, you will see that there is a gradual shift because of the nature of the project that we undertake, that our product mix will continue to evolve and change. Affordable housing, which is more towards the Dombivli side, will continue to have a robust journey, continue to give good pre-sales number, but from an overall number point of view, the percentage will keep coming down.

items.statement: Ranked 3rd in Mumbai for new residential launches sales (CY23-Q1 CY27); 1st in eastern suburbs sales and 1st in Kalyan-Dombivli new launches
items.quote: Based on the industry research, Runwal was ranked third in Mumbai for new residential launches on sales between calendar year 23 and the first quarter of calendar year 27. We were also ranked first in eastern suburbs in terms of sales and first in Kalyan-Dombivali in terms of new launches over the same period.

items.statement: HR1 Medicaid renewals shift from annual to six-monthly from Jan 2027; Medicaid eligibility at scale; Voice AI live across eligibility, patient access, collections
items.quote: From January of 2027, under HR1, Medicaid renewals for expansion adults move fro m annual to six -monthly, phasing in through the year.
