name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited

items.statement: Aspire to grow fresh business at 20%+ consistently for a long period and hope to maintain that for this year
items.quote: So as a company, we aspire to grow at 20% plus on fresh business consistently for a long period of time. We hope to maintain that for this year as well.

items.statement: GST exemption demonstrated how affordability unlocks demand for retail health insurance, particularly among first-time buyers
items.quote: The GST exemption demonstrated how strongly affordability unlocks demand for retail health insurance, particularly amongst the first-time buyers.

items.statement: Combined Insurance Service Ratio improved 2.9% to 98% in Q2 FY27 and 2.4% to 97.9% for H1 FY27
items.quote: The Combined Insurance Service Ratio, CISR, improved by 2.9% to 98% in Quarter 2 FY27 and by 2.4% to 97.9% for H1 of FY27.

items.statement: Underwriting result was Rs. 99 crore in Q2 FY27 vs loss of Rs. 40 crore in Q2 FY26, a positive swing of Rs. 139 crore
items.quote: Now coming to the underwriting result for the quarter was Rs. 99 crore compared to a loss of Rs. 40 crore in Quarter 2 of last financial year. This is a positive swing of about Rs. 139 crore.

items.statement: H1 FY27 underwriting result of Rs. 210 crore surpassed full-year FY26 underwriting result of Rs. 198 crore
items.quote: The underwriting results for H1 FY27 surpassed the full-year FY26 underwriting result of Rs. 198 crore.

items.statement: Normalized PAT for Q2 increased 70% YoY to Rs. 390 crore; H1 normalized PAT increased 56% YoY to Rs. 775 crore with normalized ROE of 15.1%
items.quote: Under the normalized framework, our profit after tax for Quarter 2 increased 70% year-on-year to Rs. 390 crore. The profit after tax for H1 increased 56% year-on-year to Rs. 775 crore, with a normalized ROE on annualized basis increasing from 11.2% of last year's H1 FY26 to 15.1% ROE in H1 FY27.

items.statement: Gross written premium on reported 1/n basis increased 19% YoY to Rs. 5,275 crore for Q2 and 19% YoY to Rs. 9,562 crore for H1
items.quote: The gross written premium on reported 1/n basis increased 19% year-on-year to Rs. 5,275 crore for Quarter 2 and also by 19% year-on-year to Rs. 9,562 crore for the H1.

items.statement: Fresh retail health GWP grew 35% YoY for Q2 and 36% YoY for H1 on reported 1/n basis
items.quote: On the reported 1/n basis, the fresh retail health has grown by 35% year-on-year for the quarter and 36% year-on-year for the half year.

items.statement: New-to-insurance mix rose to 93% for Q2 from 89% in Q2 FY26, with new-to-insurance policies growing over 10% YoY and average sum insured rising 13% YoY
items.quote: The new-to-insurance mix rose to 93% for the quarter from 89% in Quarter 2 FY26, reflecting our continued focus on first-time buyers of health insurance and selecting a more healthier pool. The growth during the quarter was led by both volume and value, with the number of new-to-insurance policies growing over 10% year-on-year and the average sum insured also rising 13% year-on-year.

items.statement: Multi-year policies account for close to 50% of fresh business
items.quote: On a fresh basis, we are close to 50%.

items.statement: Upgraded core CRM platform to Salesforce to optimize D2C acquisition; scaled AI bots across acquisition and service channels processing over 7.5 million minutes at less than 20% of human cost
items.quote: During the quarter, we upgraded our core customer relationship management platform to Salesforce. This upgrade optimizes our D2C acquisition by enhancing the lead management precision and conversion. We have also scaled up deployment of AI bots across both our customer acquisition and service channels. Initial trends are highly encouraging. The bots processed over 7.5 million minutes of call volum

items.statement: Added 39,000 new agents during H1 FY27, taking network to 8.7 lakh agents; agency productivity improved 19% YoY
items.quote: We added 39,000 new agents during H1 FY27, taking our network to 8.7 lakh agents. Our agency productivity improved by 19% year-on-year during H1.

items.statement: Loss cost held to mid-single-digit numbers; earned premiums growing close to double-digit, driving loss ratio improvement
items.quote: if you were to take a combined effect of frequency and severity, the loss cost is something that we have been able to hold on to mid-single-digit numbers. That is what has helped us manage this number because our earned premiums have grown close to a double-digit number, and the differential is what is helping us improve the loss ratio.

items.statement: Focus on sub-40 consumers; launched Young Star neo product targeting younger age cohorts; D2C channel attracts younger customers with higher sum insured
items.quote: We have recently launched a product, a revised version of Young Star, which is called Young Star neo targeted towards sub-40 consumers. That possibly answers your question. Our focus is on onboarding sub-40 consumers.

items.statement: Cognizant of IRDAI's focus on dark patterns in digital journeys; will ensure full alignment with evolving framework; consent-led data collection and transparent disclosures will reinforce advantage of trusted direct brands
items.quote: We are cognizant of the authority's sharp focus on dark patterns in digital journeys and we fully share the emphasis on consumer trust. As digital channels account for a growing share of how consumers buy and service their policies, we continue to review our digital journeys and will ensure full alignment with the evolving framework.

items.statement: Home healthcare and telemedicine served over 1 lakh consultations/services in Q2; helped manage medical frequency of claims below last year Q2 despite increase in surgical frequency
items.quote: For the quarter, we could actually do more than lakh of consultations as well as home care services. That's the number that we already provided. The specific impact on the loss ratio is something that we do not disclose, but that's one of the big contributors in terms of medical frequency of claims coming down. Even though there was an increase in surgical frequency, but overall this helped us to

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 30-35% for FY27 and similar expectation for FY28
items.quote: already I have given in the previous call also this year's guidance is around 30% to 35%. We have already achieved 20% in the first half. But all the season that is basically Navratri and Diwali is coming in the second half of the year. So, comfortably we will reach our 30% to 35% of growth '27. And similarly, we are expecting for the '28.

items.statement: Preferential issue of ~INR100 crores approved, funds expected by 6th November, will boost capital adequacy
items.quote: we are successfully raising approximately INR100 crores through a preferential issue, further strengthening our capital base and providing additional headroom to support a future loan book expansion.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio at 24.69% pre-fund raise; expected to improve further after INR100 cr infusion
items.quote: Further, our capital adequacy ratio remained healthy at 24.69%, well above the regulatory requirement, providing ample headroom to support future growth.

items.statement: INR600 crores of borrowings at old higher rates to be repaid by March 2027, reducing cost of funds
items.quote: almost INR600 crores of my total borrowing is lying in the old sanction rates, which will drive down by 31st of March, okay? So that will affect -- that will give a lot of impact on my finance cost.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing expected to reduce by ~25 bps in Q3-Q4 FY27 due to rating upgrade and repricing
items.quote: overall impact will come 25 bps in the third to fourth quarter.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost expected to be 0.25% lower despite RBI rate hike due to rating upgrade
items.quote: at least after the rate increment also, we will be able to get 0.25% on the incremental cost of borrowing.

items.statement: Healthy industry demand with 2-wheeler registrations at 53 lakh units in Q2, 33% YoY growth in September
items.quote: During the second quarter, 2-wheeler registration reached approximately 53 lakh units with August and September both recording their highest ever volumes.

items.statement: 78% of dealers expect growth in Oct-Dec quarter; festive season to support disbursement momentum
items.quote: Looking ahead, the demand outlook remains encouraging with 78% of dealers in the industry expecting growth during the October to December.

items.statement: AUM at INR1,811 crores, up 21% YoY; H1 disbursements INR493 crores vs INR398 crores YoY
items.quote: As of September 30, 2026, our assets under management stood at INR1,811 crores, reflecting a robust year-on-year growth of 21%.

items.statement: Q2 disbursements INR267 crores vs INR233 crores YoY; added 32,330 new customers in quarter
items.quote: During the quarter, the disbursement stood at INR267 crores compared to INR233 crores in corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Product mix: 2-wheeler 83.1%, top-up 5.7%, 3-wheeler 3%, used vehicle 1.6%; over 95% portfolio secured
items.quote: Talking about the product mix for the period under review, 2-wheeler accounted for 83.10 percentage, top-up loan 5.70 percentage, 3-wheeler 3 percentage and used vehicle loan 1.60%.

items.statement: Used 2-wheeler yield 27-28% IRR; top-up/personal loan ~32% IRR; MSME LAP/small business loan 27-28% IRR
items.quote: used 2-wheeler loan at various locations, almost added 100-plus dealers in last 6 months. And of course, the yield is 27 to 28 IRR with a good processing fee and less payout will definitely add and a nice good yield.

items.statement: GNPA 2.96%, NNPA 2.19%; Stage 1 assets 94.4%, Stage 2 2.6%, Stage 3 2.96%; ECL provision INR23 cr vs INR13 cr required
items.quote: As at the end of the quarter, GNPA and NNPA improved substantially to 2.96% and 2.19%, respectively, reflecting a lower delinquency driven by the disciplined underwriting and the strong collection efficiency.

items.statement: New-to-credit borrowers ~40% of book; delinquency similar to overall portfolio due to 75% LTV cap
items.quote: NTC share is around 40% in the total book, okay? As far as the comparison is concerned, how they are behaving, it is almost, I can say, similar because we restrict 75% of LTV to the new to credit customers.

items.statement: Average bounce rate 18-20%; 7-8% customers remain in bounce across tenure
items.quote: So, generally, our bounce rate is 18% to 20%. So, this keeps on revolving because once the customer will bounce, then next time he pays also. So, on an average, there are 7% to 8% customers are there who remain bounce across the tenure.

items.statement: Technology spend ~INR2 crores annually; 28-person tech team; disbursement TAT reduced from 3.5-4 days to 1.5-2 days, targeting same-day
items.quote: on an average yearly, we spend around INR2 crores on the technology. And this is what -- because what we understood that NBFC, the speed and innovation is the essence of success.

items.statement: Expanded to 148 locations across 7 states; added 16 offices in last year; 100+ dealers onboarded in Karnataka in 60 days
items.quote: We have almost onboarded 100-plus dealers in the Karnataka in the first 60 days of operations.

items.statement: Added 3 MSME LAP branches in last 2 months, 2 more planned this quarter; 7 BC partners active, 3 in due diligence
items.quote: we've added 3 more branches in last 2 months and 2 more branches we are going to add in this quarter. So, the new 5 to 6 branch will also give additional INR3 crores to INR4 crores of disbursement in the small business loan.

items.statement: Declared second interim dividend of INR0.25 per share (FV INR10) for FY27
items.quote: Further, the company declared second interim dividend of INR0.25 per equity share on a face value of INR10 each for the financial year '26-'27, reflecting our continued commitment towards shareholder value creation.

items.statement: Chairperson changed from Mr. N.R. Parameshwaran to Mrs. Neelam Tater (Independent Director)
items.quote: I would like to highlight the change in the Chairperson of the company from Mr. Nalliepily Ramaswami Parameshwaran to Mrs. Neelam Tater, Independent Directors.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to A- stable from BBB+ positive by CARE Ratings
items.quote: I'm happy to share that recently, company's credit rating has been upgraded to A minus stable from BBB plus positive by CARE ratings.

items.statement: Market share ~15% in locations with 4+ years operations; key competitors: IDFC, L&T, regional players like Berar
items.quote: wherever we are there in any location and if we have completed 4 years of operations, then generally, our market share is around 15%.

items.statement: Operating expenses up 28% YoY due to Karnataka expansion and sales hiring; management says YoY comparison not appropriate due to expansion
items.quote: operating expense has been increased by 28% is compared to September '25, first of all. And second thing, from September '25 to this September '26, we have increased our locations as well as Karnataka state, where we have recruited the salesperson in every -- lots of salesperson recruited during the season also.

items.statement: Battery replacement financing for EV 3-wheelers launched 2 months ago; pilot for own customers only; will test for 18 months before scaling
items.quote: we have introduced this product to support our own AUM, which we have blended in 3-wheeler electric rickshas. So today, introduced 2 months back only, and we are focusing only for our own customers only because we want to understand how it runs.

items.statement: Net interest income Q2: INR52 crores (+40% YoY); H1: INR94 crores (+39% YoY); PAT Q2: INR14 crores (+20% YoY); H1: INR27 crores (+28% YoY)
items.quote: For the quarter under review, net interest income stood at INR52 crores, registering a significant growth of 40% year-on-year. And profit after tax for the quarter increased by 20% year-on-year to INR14 crores.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing declined to 10.14%; NIM currently ~12.3% vs 13-14% guidance
items.quote: This enhanced credit standing has also supported improving funding efficiency with the average cost of borrowing declined to 10.14%.

items.statement: Agreed to acquire 100% of Vimprotech and TIPS for equity value of INR142 crores via slump sales into wholly owned subsidiaries
items.quote: The most important development this quarter is our agreement to acquire 100% of the business of Vimprotech and TIPS for an equity value of INR142 crores.

items.statement: Vimprotech and TIPS FY26 revenue INR61.7 crores at 28% EBITDA margin, 44% CAGR over 3 years; transaction accretive to revenue, EBITDA, PAT and improves net debt to EBITDA
items.quote: Together with a robust customer base of 200-plus, they have reported FY26 revenue at INR61.7 crores at an EBITDA margin of 28%, with revenue growing up to 44% CAGR over the last three years.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR918-920 crores, ~50% EBITDA margin, PAT ~INR90 crores; PAT growth target 60-80% vs prior 40-44%
items.quote: So, this is this is something that we have actually shared with our investors, which is INR918 crores, INR920 crores of top line, and again a 50% EBITDA to that, and a PAT margin, which is -- and a PAT of around INR90 crores.

items.statement: Movement hire target 3.6-3.7 million pallet movements for FY27, up from 2.8 million in FY26
items.quote: This year, what we have said to the market is that we will do round about 3.6 million to 3.7 million.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance ~INR450 crores; H1 FY27 capex INR213 crores vs INR201 crores H1 FY26, delivering 21% growth
items.quote: So, this quarter, we have done a capex of INR213 crores as compared to INR201 crores last year H1. But the growth has been 21%. So, you can see that we have put in the same amount of capital, but we have grown by 21%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 50.8%, up 91 bps YoY; H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 52.1%
items.quote: With respect to EBITDA was INR1,097 million, up 25%, with EBITDA margin at 50.8%, up 91 basis points year-on-year, supported by higher income, cost optimization, and network synergies.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue INR216 crores, up 22.5% YoY; EBITDA INR110 crores, up 24.8% YoY; PAT up 62% YoY (109% excluding break cost)
items.quote: So, as compared to last year's quarter 2, we have done INR216 crores of turnover. We have grown by 22.5%. We have done INR110 crores of EBITDA, which is we have grown by 24.8%.

items.statement: Net pallet allotment 417,000 in Q2 FY27; 37 new customers added in Q2 (24 LEAP, 13 TARON); 85 new customers in H1 FY27
items.quote: We have put in round about 417,000 net allot of our pallets. So, the people who are asking this question of whether there is growth since you have 90% of the market, that also comes to rest.

items.statement: Asset pool 15.5 million vs 13.8 million YoY (+1.7 million); pallet utilization 89.3%, container 73.7%, MHE 82.3%; target pallet utilization 90-91%
items.quote: We closed H1 with 15.5 million assets compared with 13.8 million a year ago, an addition of 1.7 million.

items.statement: Plastic granule cost up 30-50%, limiting automotive crate supply; timber cost controlled via Plinova (2-3% fluctuation over 6 years); FOB contracts insulate from shipping cost
items.quote: But you can look at it that this time the granule cost has gone overboard, plastic cost has gone overboard. Automotive sector has done fantastically well. If they have asked for four crates, we have been able to deliver only 1.5 crates to them.

items.statement: DSO improved from 128 to 122 days; target <90 days by end FY27 via SAP S/4HANA and centralized PO for top 5-6 customers
items.quote: But as I told you that we have implemented SAP S/4HANA, and the bills are going on time, and you can see that whatever we have billed, we have started collecting more than that. So, we are very confident as a team that by the end of the year, we will be less than 90 days.

items.statement: Post-IPO debt/equity 0.48x, net debt/EBITDA 1.9x (from 4.4x H1 FY26); INR3,596 million debt repaid from IPO proceeds; INR1,100 million held as investments
items.quote: On a post-IPO basis, debt to equity is about 0.48x and net debt to EBITDA is about 1.9x, compared with 4.4x in H1 FY26.

items.statement: India Ratings upgraded long-term rating to A+ from A for LEAP and TARON; third upgrade in 3.5 years
items.quote: I am very happy to announce that in the month of October, India Ratings and Research, a Fitch Group company, upgraded LEAP's long-term rating from A to A plus, and same has happened for TARON business.

items.statement: GCC subsidiaries in Saudi Arabia and UAE established with licenses, warehouse, hiring; engaging 26 customers; revenue may start next month, definite numbers next quarter; spent INR2.5-3 crores so far
items.quote: See, yes, so if you look at Middle East, we can start the revenue maybe from next month. But we are looking at, as I said, that we are looking at certain companies to go for, which already have their operations in GCC. But next quarter, we will be definitely showing numbers on GCC front.

items.statement: Revenue split: ~64% pallets, 20-22% automotive crates/containers, 14-16% MHE; MHE revenue up 52% YoY in Q2
items.quote: So, technically, it is again 64% contribution from pallet side, round about 20-odd percent, 20% to 22% contribution from auto side, and 14% to 16% contribution from MHE side.

items.statement: 1,100+ customers, 11,000+ touchpoints, 27 fulfillment centers; converting dairy, textile, bottles to movement hire; 60 companies in movement hire sales funnel
items.quote: We now serve 1,100-plus customers, and we are constantly adding that. We have 11,000-plus touchpoints.

items.statement: Per pallet yield increased from INR1.46-1.48 to INR1.54/day; at 0.4 movement hire ratio EBITDA 50%, at 1.4 ratio EBITDA 80%; target yield INR1.62 with 3.6M movements
items.quote: If you look at our previous per pallet yield, it was INR1.46, 1.48 paise. Now it has jumped to INR1.54 paise.

items.statement: Textile industry operating at 20% capacity due to granule cost; plastic goods industry hit; automotive crate demand unmet due to 60-70% higher crate cost; drought may boost beverage pallet demand
items.quote: Textile industry is not doing well because of the cost of the granules. Plastic good industry is also absolutely hit due to the granule rate fluctuation.

items.statement: Key managerial persons of Vimprotech and TIPS to continue ensuring leadership continuity and seamless transition
items.quote: The key managerial persons will continue to be associated with us, ensuring leadership continuity and a seamless transition.

items.statement: IPO fresh issue INR480 crores: INR360 crores used for debt repayment, INR120 crores for general corporate purposes; IPO expenses INR112-113 crores held in current liabilities
items.quote: Of the INR4,800 million fresh issue, INR3,596 million has been used to repay debt, and INR1,200 million is unmarked for general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Aims to maintain EBITDA margin around 30% plus or minus 2 percentage points
items.quote: Going forward, we aim to maintain an EBITDA margin of approximately 30%, plus or minus 2 percentage points, supported by disciplined procurement, manufacturing efficiency and appropriate pricing.

items.statement: Machinery worth Rs 50 million commissioned and orders placed for additional Rs 300 million
items.quote: Machinery worth Rs. 50 million has been purchased and commissioned, and orders have been placed for additional machinery worth approximately Rs. 300 million.

items.statement: Pithampur machining and assembly capacity to double from 900,000 to 1,800,000 units annually, operational in Q4 FY27
items.quote: At the Pithampur plant, we plan to increase annual machining and assembly capacity from 900,000 units to 1,800,000 units. Most of the additional capacity is expected to become operational in Q4 FY27.

items.statement: Dewas forging capacity to increase from 3,000 to 5,500 tonnes annually, operational in Q1 FY28
items.quote: At Dewas, annual forging capacity is planned to increase from 3,000 tonnes to 5,500 tonnes, with the additional capacity expected to become operational in Q1 FY28.

items.statement: Current order book approximately Rs 68-70 crore, 78% export and 22% domestic
items.quote: The current order book is approximately Rs. 68 – 70 crore, of which around 78% is export orders and 22% is domestic orders.

items.statement: Finished propeller shafts generate 5-10% higher margins than components
items.quote: Finished propeller shafts generate higher margins because they include additional value addition. Margins on finished shafts can be approximately 5% – 10% higher than on components.

items.statement: Revenue split approximately 64-65% components, balance propeller shaft assemblies; mix expected to remain similar
items.quote: Approximately 64% – 65% of the business comes from components , with the balance from propeller-shaft 8 Adroit Industries (India) Limited 28 October 2026 assemblies. We expect the mix to remain broadly similar, with a variation of around five percentage points

items.statement: Added approximately 13 new customers in the quarter; 87.4% of product sales from repeat customers
items.quote: We made progress in expanding our customer base during the quarter, adding approximately 13 new customers. At the same time, 87.4% of our product sales came from repeat customers, reflecting the strength of our established relationships.

items.statement: US subsidiary targeting 200 new customers over next two to three quarters
items.quote: Our goal is to add 200 new customers over the next two to three

items.statement: H1 FY27 exports 82.36% of revenue, US 59.56% of export sales
items.quote: In H1 FY27, exports represented approximately 82.36% of revenue, with the United States accounting for 59.56% of export sales.

items.statement: Technology for European products available from only 4-5 manufacturers globally; product seeding completed and acceptance received; greater Europe focus next financial year
items.quote: The Company has technology for products required by European customers that is available from only four or five manufacturers globally. The technology was procured before the IPO, product seeding has been completed, and products have received acceptance from customers in several European countries. The next step is to scale up and add customers, with a greater focus on Europe in the next financial

items.statement: Current working capital cycle approximately 248-249 days; expects improvement to 200-230 days as domestic OEM business grows
items.quote: capital cycle, including inventory, is approximately 248-249 days. We intend to grow our Indian OEM business, where payment cycles are typically 45-60 days. Customers such as BEML and Volvo have requested increased production capacity, including dedicated lines. As the domestic business grows, we expect the overall cycle to improve, although we expect it to remain in the range of 200-230 days

items.statement: Believes growth to Rs 250 crore revenue can be managed without additional fundraising
items.quote: I believe we should be able to manage the growth without raising additional funds.

items.statement: Expects revenue of approximately Rs 250 crore in FY28 across industrial, defence and automotive
items.quote: As mentioned earlier, I expect revenue of approximately Rs. 250 crore in FY28.

items.statement: Expanded manufacturing platform could support peak annual revenue of approximately Rs 2,500 million at full ramp-up by Q4 FY28
items.quote: At that scale, the expanded manufacturing platform could support peak annual revenue of approximately Rs. 2,500 million.

items.statement: Sees opportunities from Make in India initiative as customers seek domestically manufactured alternatives to imported shafts
items.quote: A number of critical shafts are still imported into India. We see opportunities arising from the Make in India initiative as customers look for domestically manufactured alternatives.

items.statement: Global competitors include Dana Spicer, Cummins/Arvin Meritor and Neapco; exports to more than 35 countries
items.quote: At the global level, competitors include Dana Spicer, Cummins/Arvin Meritor and Neapco. We export to more than 35 countries and are looking to expand into additional markets.

items.statement: Local inventory in Canada and US can sell at 1.5 to 1.7 times previous margin levels
items.quote: With local teams and inventory, products can be sold at substantially higher margins than when shipped directly, potentially 1.5 to 1.7 times the previous margin level.

items.statement: Procures tubing and universal joints; tubing will continue to be procured, working to manufacture universal joints in-house by end of November 2026
items.quote: The Company currently procures tubing and universal joints. Tubing will continue to be procured, while the Company is working to obtain the technology to manufacture universal joints in-house. Management's target was to complete this by the end of November 2026, which would further improve margins in the propeller-shaft business.

items.statement: Customers such as BEML and Volvo have requested increased production capacity including dedicated lines
items.quote: Customers such as BEML and Volvo have requested increased production capacity, including dedicated lines.

items.statement: Defence testing is rigorous and may take six months because vehicles operate across difficult terrain
items.quote: Defence testing is rigorous and may take six months because vehicles operate across difficult terrain.

items.statement: US team has extensive experience in driveline business and established industry relationships
items.quote: Our US team has extensive experience in the driveline business and established industry relationships.
